chapters.title: Moses on the Mountain
chapters.html:
Jubilees 1

This is the account of the division of the days of the law and of the testimony, of the events of the years, of their weeks and their jubilees, through all the years of the world, as He spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai when he went up to receive the tablets of stone, the law and the commandment, by the word of the Lord, as He had said to him, "Go up to the top of the mountain."

1And it came to pass in the first year after the sons of Israel went out of Egypt, in the third month, on the sixteenth day of that month, that the Lord spoke to Moses, saying, "Come up to Me here on the mountain, and I will give you two tablets of stone, the law and the commandment, which I have written, so that you may teach them."

2Moses went up the mountain of God, and the glory of the Lord settled on Mount Sinai, and a cloud overshadowed it for six days.

3He called Moses on the seventh day from the middle of the cloud, and Moses saw the glory of the Lord like a fire burning on the top of the mountain.

4Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights, and the Lord taught him what had been and what was to come, the account of the division of all the days of the law and of the testimony.

5He said to him, "Set your heart on every word that I speak to you on this mountain, and write it in a book, so that their generations may see that I have not forsaken them for all the evil they have done in straying from the ordinance that I set between Me and you today, for their generations, on Mount Sinai.

6They will tell of it when all this comes upon them, and they will know that I am more righteous than they in all their judgments and in all their deeds, and they will know that I have truly been with them.

7As for you, write down for yourself all the words that I make known to you today. For I know their rebellion and their stiff neck, before I bring them into the land that I swore to Abraham and to Isaac and to Jacob, saying, 'To your seed I will give a land flowing with milk and honey.' They will eat and be satisfied, and they will turn to a foreign god, to gods who cannot save them from any of their distress.

8This testimony will be heard as a witness against them. For they will forget all My commandments that I command them, and they will walk after the nations, after their uncleanness and after their shame, and they will serve their gods, and these will become for them a stumbling block, and distress and anguish and a snare.

9Many will perish, and they will be taken captive and fall into the hand of the enemy, because they have forsaken My ordinances and My commandments, and the festivals of My covenant, and My sabbaths, and the holy things that I made holy for Myself among them, and My tabernacle and My sanctuary that I made holy for Myself in the middle of the land, to set My name on it, so that it might dwell there.

10They will make for themselves high places and groves and carved images, and each will worship his own and go astray. They will sacrifice their children to demons and to every work of the error of their heart. I will send witnesses to them, to testify against them, but they will not listen, and they will kill the witnesses too.

11Those who search out the law they will kill and persecute. They will set everything aside and begin to do evil before My eyes.

12I will hide My face from them and hand them over into the hand of the nations, to be taken captive and plundered and devoured. I will remove them from the middle of the land and scatter them among the nations.

13They will forget all My law and all My commandments and all My judgments, and they will set aside new moon and sabbath and festival and jubilee and ordinance.

14After this they will turn to Me from among the nations with all their heart and with all their soul and with all their strength, and I will gather them from among all the nations.

15They will seek Me, and I will let Myself be found by them. When they seek Me with all their heart and with all their soul, I will reveal to them abundant peace in righteousness, and I will plant them anew as a plant of uprightness, with all My heart and with all My soul.

16They will be a blessing and not a curse; they will be the head and not the tail. I will build My sanctuary among them and dwell with them. I will be their God, and they will be My people in truth and in righteousness. I will not forsake them or turn away from them, for I am the Lord their God."

17Moses fell on his face and prayed and said, "O Lord my God, do not forsake Your people and Your inheritance to walk in the error of their heart, and do not hand them over into the hand of the nations, to rule over them and make them sin against You.

20Let Your mercy, O Lord, be lifted up over Your people, and create in them an upright spirit. Do not let the spirit of Beliar rule over them, to accuse them before You and to trap them away from every path of righteousness, so that they perish from before Your face.

21They are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You rescued by Your great power from the hand of the Egyptians. Create in them a clean heart and a holy spirit, and do not let them be trapped in their sins from now on and forever."

22The Lord said to Moses, "I know their contrariness and their thoughts and their stiff neck, and they will not listen until they acknowledge their sin and the sins of their fathers.

23After this they will turn to Me in all uprightness, with all their heart and with all their soul. I will circumcise the foreskin of their heart and the foreskin of the heart of their seed, and I will create in them a holy spirit, and I will cleanse them, so that they will not turn away from Me from that day on and forever.

24Their souls will cling to Me and to all My commandments, and they will keep My commandments. I will be their Father, and they will be My children.

25They will all be called children of the living God, and every angel and every spirit will know them. They will know that they are My children, and that I am their Father in uprightness and in righteousness, and that I love them.

26As for you, write down for yourself all these words that I make known to you on this mountain: what was first and what is last and what is to come, in all the divisions of the days, in the law and in the testimony, and in their weeks and their jubilees, forever, until I come down and dwell with them for all the ages."

27He said to the angel of the presence, "Write for Moses from the beginning of creation until My sanctuary is built among them for all the ages.

28The Lord will appear to the eyes of all, and all will know that I am the God of Israel, and the Father of all the children of Jacob, and King on Mount Zion forever and ever. Zion and Jerusalem will be holy."

29The angel of the presence, who went before the camps of Israel, took the tablets of the division of the years, from the time of creation, of the law and of the testimony, of the weeks of the jubilees, year by year in their full number, and of the jubilees, from the day of the new creation, when the heavens and the earth and all their creatures are renewed, according to the powers of heaven and according to all the creation of the earth, until the sanctuary of the Lord is made in Jerusalem on Mount Zion, and all the lights are renewed for healing and for peace and for blessing for all the chosen of Israel, so that it may be so from that day and for all the days of the earth.

Notes

  • The opening and the verse numbers — the lines above verse 1 are the book's own title: the account of the division, nagara kufāle. From that word the book takes its Ge'ez name, Maṣḥafa Kufāle, the Book of Division: it divides the history of the world into jubilees of forty-nine years and weeks of seven. Verse numbers follow the EOTC printed Bible. It fits into vv1–17 what other editions number 1–19, then goes on from v20, so there are no verses 18 and 19 here and nothing is missing. From v20 on, the numbers agree with other editions.

  • v1 "which I have written" — the EOTC reads ṣaḥafka, you have written; the second Ge'ez text reads ṣaḥafku, I have written, as Exodus 24:12 does: I will give you the tablets of stone, the instruction and the commandment, which I have written to teach them. The English follows the second Ge'ez text. Exodus dates the arrival at Sinai to the third month (Exodus 19:1); Jubilees gives the day, the sixteenth.

  • vv2–4 "the glory of the Lord settled on Mount Sinai" — Exodus 24:16–18, retold almost word for word: six days of cloud, the call on the seventh, the fire on the top of the mountain, forty days and forty nights. Jubilees adds what Moses was taught there: what had been and what was to come. The second Ge'ez text ends v4 at forty nights.

  • v5 "that I have not forsaken them" — the EOTC lacks the not: ka-ma ḫadagwomu. The second Ge'ez text has it, ka-ma ʾi-ḫadagwomu, and so does Charles. The English follows them, because v6 says the same from the other side: they will know that I have truly been with them.

  • vv7–8 "They will eat and be satisfied, and they will turn to a foreign god… This testimony will be heard as a witness against them" — Deuteronomy 31, where the Lord tells Moses the same at the end of his life: they will eat and be satisfied and grow fat, and turn to other gods… this song will answer before them as a witness (Deuteronomy 31:20–21); I know your rebellion and your stiff neck (31:27). Jubilees moves the warning to the beginning, to Sinai. A snare is the warning of Exodus 23:33: you would serve their gods, and it would become a snare to you.

  • v9 "to set My name on it, so that it might dwell there" — the words of Deuteronomy for the temple: the place that the LORD your God chooses, to make His name dwell there (Deuteronomy 12:11).

  • v10 "They will sacrifice their children to demons… they will kill the witnesses too" — the psalm: they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons (Psalm 106:37). Nehemiah's confession: they killed Your prophets, who testified against them to turn them back to You (Nehemiah 9:26).

  • v12 "I will hide My face from them… to be devoured" — Deuteronomy 31:17: I will forsake them and hide My face from them, and they will be devoured.

  • v13 "they will set aside new moon and sabbath and festival and jubilee" — the EOTC reads yəsəʿəru, set aside. The second Ge'ez text reads yəsəḥətu, go astray, and Charles go astray as to new moons, and sabbaths. The second reading is the book's own fear about the calendar, stated again at 6:34: they will forget the new moons, and seasons, and sabbaths.

  • vv14–16 "with all their heart and with all their soul… with all My heart and with all My soul" — Deuteronomy: you will seek the LORD your God, and you will find Him, if you search for Him with all your heart and with all your soul (Deuteronomy 4:29). Jeremiah gives the promise and its answer: you will seek Me and find Me… I will let Myself be found by you (Jeremiah 29:13–14), and I will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all My heart and with all My soul (Jeremiah 32:41). In truth and in righteousness is Zechariah 8:8, they will be My people and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness; the head and not the tail is Deuteronomy 28:13.

  • vv17, 21 "do not forsake Your people and Your inheritance… whom You rescued by Your great power" — Moses' prayer in Deuteronomy 9: do not destroy Your people and Your inheritance (9:26); they are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You brought out by Your great power (9:29).

  • v20 "the spirit of Beliar… to accuse them before You" — Belḥor. Paul uses the name: What agreement has Christ with Beliar? (2 Corinthians 6:15). In Revelation the one cast down is the accuser of our brothers, who accuses them before our God day and night (Revelation 12:10). Create in them an upright spirit is David's prayer, from the same verse as v21's clean heart: create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me (Psalm 51:10).

  • vv21, 23, 26, 29, the ends of the verses — from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). The EOTC text as held here breaks off before them.

  • v23 "I will circumcise the foreskin of their heart" — the promise of Deuteronomy: the LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your seed, to love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul (Deuteronomy 30:6).

  • vv24–25 "I will be their Father, and they will be My children… children of the living God" — the promise to David's son, I will be his father, and he will be My son (2 Samuel 7:14), and Paul's I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters (2 Corinthians 6:18). In the place where it was said to them, "You are not My people," it will be said to them, "Children of the living God" (Hosea 1:10), which Paul quotes in Romans 9:26.

  • vv27–29 "the angel of the presence" — malʾaka gaṣṣ, the angel of the face: the angel who stands before God's face. Isaiah: the angel of His presence saved them (Isaiah 63:9). God tells this angel to write the history for Moses (v27), and the rest of the book is that history. "who went before the camps of Israel" — the angel of the exodus: the messenger of God who was going before the camp of Israel (Exodus 14:19).

  • v28 "King on Mount Zion forever" — Micah: the LORD will reign over them on Mount Zion from now and forever (Micah 4:7).

  • v29 "from the time of creation… from the day of the new creation" — so the Ge'ez, and Charles gives it the same way. With v27, from the beginning of creation until My sanctuary is built among them, the tablets cover the whole span: from the first creation to the new one, when the heavens and the earth are renewed.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Six Days and the Sabbath
chapters.html:
Jubilees 2

1The angel of the presence spoke to Moses by the word of the Lord, saying: Write down the whole account of creation: how in six days the Lord God finished all His work and all that He created, and kept sabbath on the seventh day, and made it holy for all ages, and set it as a sign for all His works.

2For on the first day He created the heavens above, and the earth, and the waters, and every spirit that serves before Him: the angels of the presence, and the angels of holiness, and the angels of the spirit of fire, and the angels of the spirit of the winds, and the angels of the spirit of the clouds, for darkness and for all things, for hail and for snow; and the angels of the voices and the thunders and the lightnings; and the angels of the spirits of cold and of heat, of winter and of spring, of autumn and of summer; and all the spirits of His works in the heavens and on the earth and in all the deeps; and darkness and light, dawn and evening, which He prepared in the knowledge of His heart.

3Then we saw His works, and we blessed Him and praised Him before Him for all His works, for He made seven great works on the first day.

4On the second day He made the expanse in the middle of the waters, and on that day the waters were divided: half of them went up above, and half of them went down below the expanse, in the middle, over the face of the whole earth. This was the only work He made on the second day.

5On the third day He did as He had said: He told the waters to pass from the face of the whole earth into one place, and the dry ground to appear.

6The waters did as He told them: they withdrew from the face of the earth into one place outside this expanse, and the dry ground appeared.

7On that day He created for it all the seas, each in its own gathering, and all the rivers, and the gatherings of the waters in the mountains and over all the earth, and all the pools, and all the dew of the earth, and the seed that is sown, each with its own seed, and everything that is eaten, and the fruit-bearing trees, and the forests, and the garden of Eden in Eden, for delight. These were the four great kinds He made on the third day.

8On the fourth day the Lord made the sun and the moon and the stars, and set them in the expanse of heaven to give light on all the earth, to rule over the day and the night, and to divide the light from the darkness.

9The Lord made the sun a great sign on the earth for days and for sabbaths, for months and for festivals, for years and for sabbaths of years, for jubilees, and for all the seasons of the years.

10It divides between light and darkness, and it is for well-being, so that everything that sprouts and grows on the earth may prosper. These were the three kinds He made on the fourth day.

11On the fifth day He created the great sea-monsters in the middle of the depths of the waters, for these were the first flesh made by His hands; and everything that moves in the waters, the fish; and everything that flies, the birds, and all their kinds.

12The sun rose over them for their well-being, and over everything that is on the earth, everything that sprouts from the earth, and all the fruit-bearing trees, and all flesh. These were the three kinds He made on the fifth day.

13On the sixth day He made all the wild animals of the earth, and all the cattle, and everything that moves on the earth.

14After all this He made humankind: a man and a woman He made them. He gave him rule over all that is on the earth and in the seas, over what flies, over the wild animals, over the cattle, over everything that moves on the earth, and over the whole earth: over all this He gave him rule. These were the four kinds He made on the sixth day.

15In all there were twenty-two kinds.

16He finished all His work on the sixth day: all that is in heaven and on the earth, in the seas and in the deeps, in the light and in the darkness, and in everything.

17He gave us a great sign, the sabbath day, that we should work six days and keep sabbath on the seventh day from all work.

18All the angels of the presence and all the angels of holiness, these two great kinds: He told us to keep sabbath with Him in heaven and on earth.

19He said to us, "I will set apart for Myself a people from among My nations, and they too will keep sabbath. I will make them holy for Myself as a people, and I will bless them. As I have made the sabbath day holy and keep it holy for Myself, so I will bless them, and they will be My people, and I will be their God.

20I have chosen the seed of Jacob out of all that I have seen, and I have written him down for Myself as a firstborn son, and made him holy for Myself forever and ever. I will teach them the sabbath days, so that they keep sabbath on them from all work."

21In this way He made in it a sign, by which they too keep sabbath with us on the seventh day, to eat and to drink and to bless the One who created all things, as He blessed and made holy for Himself a people that stands out from all the nations, so that they keep sabbath together with us.

22He made His will rise as a soothing aroma, accepted before Him all the days.

23There were twenty-two heads of mankind from Adam to Jacob, and twenty-two kinds of work were made until the seventh day. This one is blessed and holy, and that one too is blessed and holy; this one belongs with that one, for holiness and for blessing.

24It was granted to this seed to be blessed and holy for all days, by the testimony and the first law, as the sabbath day was made holy and blessed on the seventh day.

25He created the heavens and the earth and all that was created in six days, and God gave a holy festival day for all His works. So He commanded concerning it that whoever does any work on it shall die, and whoever defiles it shall surely die.

26As for you, command the sons of Israel to keep this day: to keep it holy, and not to do any work on it, and not to defile it, for it is holier than all days.

27Everyone who profanes it shall surely die, and everyone who does any work on it shall surely die forever, so that the sons of Israel may keep this day through their generations and not be uprooted from the land; for it is a holy day and a blessed day.

28Every man who keeps it and keeps sabbath on it from all his work will be holy and blessed all the days, like us.

29Make known and tell the sons of Israel the law of this day: that they keep sabbath on it and do not forsake it in the error of their heart; that they must not do on it any work that is not fitting, doing their own will on it; and that they must not prepare on it anything to eat or drink, or draw water, or bring in or take out through their gates any load that they had not prepared on the sixth day in their dwellings.

30They shall not take anything out or bring anything in, from house to house, on this day, for it is holier and more blessed than any jubilee day of the jubilees. On it we kept sabbath in the heavens before it was made known to any flesh to keep sabbath on it on the earth.

31The Creator of all blessed it, but He did not make all peoples and nations holy to keep sabbath on it, only Israel: to him alone He gave to eat and drink and keep sabbath on it on the earth.

32The Creator of all, who created this day, blessed it for blessing and for holiness and for glory above all days.

33This law and testimony was given to the sons of Israel as a law forever, for their generations.

Notes

  • v1 "The angel of the presence spoke to Moses" — from here on the angel of 1:27 speaks, and we in this chapter are the angels. The Greek, in a line that speaks of Moses in the third person, calls this angel the archangel Gabriel; the Ge'ez gives no name.

  • vv2–3 "every spirit that serves before Him… Then we saw His works, and we blessed Him" — Genesis names no angels at creation. Jubilees makes them the first day's work, and they watch the rest and praise. God asks Job where he was when the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy (Job 38:7). The voices and the thunders and the lightnings are what John sees coming from the throne: lightnings and voices and thunders (Revelation 4:5).

  • vv7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 20, 23, 24, 25, 27, 29, the ends of the verses — from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). The EOTC text as held here breaks off before them. The Greek has the counts at the ends of vv10, 12 and 14.

  • v7 "These were the four great kinds He made on the third day" — the counts matter to the chapter. Verse 15 adds up to twenty-two kinds, which is 7 + 1 + 4 + 3 + 3 + 4, and v10 speaks of everything that sprouts and grows on the earth, made here on the third day. Genesis also puts the plants on the third day (Genesis 1:11–12).

  • v9 "The Lord made the sun a great sign… for days and for sabbaths, for months and for festivals" — Genesis gives the signs to both lamps: let them be for signs, and for appointed times, and for days and years (Genesis 1:14). Jubilees gives them to the sun alone. The reason comes at 6:36, where those who follow the moon make the seasons slip, ten days too soon each year.

  • vv15, 23 "twenty-two kinds… twenty-two heads of mankind from Adam to Jacob" — the two numbers are made to match, as v23 goes on to say: twenty-two works in the six days, twenty-two fathers from Adam to Jacob. The names in Genesis 5 and 11, from Adam through Isaac to Jacob, come to twenty-two. The EOTC has to him; the Greek names Jacob, the seed of Jacob of v20.

  • v17 "a great sign, the sabbath day" — the words of Exodus 31: it is a sign between Me and you, through your generations (31:13). Here the angels are given the sign first, and keep sabbath in heaven before any man on earth (v30).

  • vv19–20 "I will set apart for Myself a people… as a firstborn son" — God's word to Pharaoh: Israel is My son, My firstborn (Exodus 4:22). From among My nations, ʾaḥzābəya: all the nations are His, and one is set apart.

  • v27 "Everyone who profanes it shall surely die" — Exodus 31:14–15: Whoever profanes it shall surely be put to death… Whoever does work on the sabbath day shall surely be put to death.

  • v29 "doing their own will on it" — Isaiah: if you turn back your foot from the sabbath, from doing your pleasure on My holy day (Isaiah 58:13).

  • v30 "They shall not take anything out or bring anything in, from house to house" — Jeremiah: Do not carry a load out of your houses on the sabbath day (Jeremiah 17:22).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. speech.text: Jubilees 2

The angel of the presence spoke to Moses by the word of the Lord, saying: Write down the whole account of creation: how in six days the Lord God finished all His work and all that He created, and kept sabbath on the seventh day, and made it holy for all ages, and set it as a sign for all His works.

For on the first day He created the heavens above, and the earth, and the waters, and every spirit that serves before Him: the angels of the presence, and the angels of holiness, and the angels of the spirit of fire, and the angels of the spirit of the winds, and the angels of the spirit of the clouds, for darkness and for all things, for hail and for snow; and the angels of the voices and the thunders and the lightnings; and the angels of the spirits of cold and of heat, of winter and of spring, of autumn and of summer; and all the spirits of His works in the heavens and on the earth and in all the deeps; and darkness and light, dawn and evening, which He prepared in the knowledge of His heart.
Then we saw His works, and we blessed Him and praised Him before Him for all His works, for He made seven great works on the first day.

On the second day He made the expanse in the middle of the waters, and on that day the waters were divided: half of them went up above, and half of them went down below the expanse, in the middle, over the face of the whole earth. This was the only work He made on the second day.
On the third day He did as He had said: He told the waters to pass from the face of the whole earth into one place, and the dry ground to appear.
The waters did as He told them: they withdrew from the face of the earth into one place outside this expanse, and the dry ground appeared.

On that day He created for it all the seas, each in its own gathering, and all the rivers, and the gatherings of the waters in the mountains and over all the earth, and all the pools, and all the dew of the earth, and the seed that is sown, each with its own seed, and everything that is eaten, and the fruit-bearing trees, and the forests, and the garden of Eden in Eden, for delight. These were the four great kinds He made on the third day.

On the fourth day the Lord made the sun and the moon and the stars, and set them in the expanse of heaven to give light on all the earth, to rule over the day and the night, and to divide the light from the darkness.
The Lord made the sun a great sign on the earth for days and for sabbaths, for months and for festivals, for years and for sabbaths of years, for jubilees, and for all the seasons of the years.
It divides between light and darkness, and it is for well-being, so that everything that sprouts and grows on the earth may prosper. These were the three kinds He made on the fourth day.

On the fifth day He created the great sea-monsters in the middle of the depths of the waters, for these were the first flesh made by His hands; and everything that moves in the waters, the fish; and everything that flies, the birds, and all their kinds.

The sun rose over them for their well-being, and over everything that is on the earth, everything that sprouts from the earth, and all the fruit-bearing trees, and all flesh. These were the three kinds He made on the fifth day.
On the sixth day He made all the wild animals of the earth, and all the cattle, and everything that moves on the earth.

After all this He made humankind: a man and a woman He made them. He gave him rule over all that is on the earth and in the seas, over what flies, over the wild animals, over the cattle, over everything that moves on the earth, and over the whole earth: over all this He gave him rule. These were the four kinds He made on the sixth day.
In all there were twenty-two kinds.
He finished all His work on the sixth day: all that is in heaven and on the earth, in the seas and in the deeps, in the light and in the darkness, and in everything.
He gave us a great sign, the sabbath day, that we should work six days and keep sabbath on the seventh day from all work.
All the angels of the presence and all the angels of holiness, these two great kinds: He told us to keep sabbath with Him in heaven and on earth.

He said to us, "I will set apart for Myself a people from among My nations, and they too will keep sabbath. I will make them holy for Myself as a people, and I will bless them. As I have made the sabbath day holy and keep it holy for Myself, so I will bless them, and they will be My people, and I will be their God.

I have chosen the seed of Jacob out of all that I have seen, and I have written him down for Myself as a firstborn son, and made him holy for Myself forever and ever. I will teach them the sabbath days, so that they keep sabbath on them from all work."

In this way He made in it a sign, by which they too keep sabbath with us on the seventh day, to eat and to drink and to bless the One who created all things, as He blessed and made holy for Himself a people that stands out from all the nations, so that they keep sabbath together with us.
He made His will rise as a soothing aroma, accepted before Him all the days.

There were twenty-two heads of mankind from Adam to Jacob, and twenty-two kinds of work were made until the seventh day. This one is blessed and holy, and that one too is blessed and holy; this one belongs with that one, for holiness and for blessing.
It was granted to this seed to be blessed and holy for all days, by the testimony and the first law, as the sabbath day was made holy and blessed on the seventh day.

He created the heavens and the earth and all that was created in six days, and God gave a holy festival day for all His works. So He commanded concerning it that whoever does any work on it shall die, and whoever defiles it shall surely die.
As for you, command the sons of Israel to keep this day: to keep it holy, and not to do any work on it, and not to defile it, for it is holier than all days.

Everyone who profanes it shall surely die, and everyone who does any work on it shall surely die forever, so that the sons of Israel may keep this day through their generations and not be uprooted from the land; for it is a holy day and a blessed day.
Every man who keeps it and keeps sabbath on it from all his work will be holy and blessed all the days, like us.

Make known and tell the sons of Israel the law of this day: that they keep sabbath on it and do not forsake it in the error of their heart; that they must not do on it any work that is not fitting, doing their own will on it; and that they must not prepare on it anything to eat or drink, or draw water, or bring in or take out through their gates any load that they had not prepared on the sixth day in their dwellings.

They shall not take anything out or bring anything in, from house to house, on this day, for it is holier and more blessed than any jubilee day of the jubilees. On it we kept sabbath in the heavens before it was made known to any flesh to keep sabbath on it on the earth.
The Creator of all blessed it, but He did not make all peoples and nations holy to keep sabbath on it, only Israel: to him alone He gave to eat and drink and keep sabbath on it on the earth.
The Creator of all, who created this day, blessed it for blessing and for holiness and for glory above all days.
This law and testimony was given to the sons of Israel as a law forever, for their generations.

chapters.title: Adam and Eve in the Garden
chapters.html:
Jubilees 3

1On the six days of the second week, by the word of the Lord, we brought to Adam all the wild animals, and all the cattle, and all the birds, and everything that moves on the earth, and everything that moves in the water, each by its kind and its type: the wild animals on the first day, the cattle on the second day, the birds on the third day, all that moves on the earth on the fourth day, and what moves in the water on the fifth day.

2Adam named them all, each by its name, and as he called them, so was their name.

3On these five days Adam saw all this, male and female of every kind that was on the earth, but he was alone, and he found no one to help him, like himself.

4The Lord said to us, "It is not good for the man to be alone. Let us make him a help like himself."

5The Lord our God cast a deep sleep upon him, and he slept. He took for the woman one bone from among his bones, and this rib was the beginning of the woman from among his bones; and He built up the flesh in its place, and He built the woman.

6He woke Adam from his sleep, and when he woke he rose on the sixth day, and He brought her to him, and he knew her, and said to her, "This is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh. She shall be called my wife, because she was taken from her husband."

7For this reason a man and his wife shall be one, and for this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother and cling to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.

8In the first week Adam was made, and the rib, his wife; in the second week He showed her to him. For this reason the commandment was given to keep women in their uncleanness seven days for a male, and for a female twice seven days.

9After Adam had completed forty days in the land where he had been created, we brought him into the garden of Eden to serve it and to keep it; and his wife we brought in on the eightieth day, and after this she entered the garden of Eden.

10For this reason the commandment is written on the tablets of heaven for a woman who gives birth: "If she bears a male, she shall remain in her uncleanness seven days, like the first week of days, and thirty-three days she shall remain in the blood of her purifying. She shall not touch anything holy, and she shall not enter the sanctuary, until she completes these days for a male.

11For a female, she shall remain in her uncleanness two weeks of days, like the first two weeks, and sixty-six days in the blood of her purifying; and in all they will be eighty days."

12When she had completed these eighty days, we brought her into the garden of Eden, for it is holier than all the earth, and every tree that is planted in it is holy.

13For this reason the law of these days was set for a woman who bears a male or a female: she shall touch nothing holy, and she shall not enter the sanctuary, until these days are completed for the male or the female.

14This is the law and testimony written down for Israel, for them to keep all the days.

15In the first week of the first jubilee, Adam and his wife were in the garden of Eden seven years, serving it and keeping it. We gave him work, and we taught him to do everything that is fitting for tilling.

16He served it, and he was naked but did not know it and was not ashamed. He guarded the garden from the birds and the wild animals and the cattle, and gathered its fruit and ate, and set aside what was left for himself and for his wife, and set aside what was to be kept.

17When the seven years were finished, which he had completed there, seven years exactly, in the second month, on the seventeenth day, the serpent came to the woman: "Has God commanded you, saying, 'You shall not eat of all the fruit of the trees in the garden'?"

18She said to it, "From all the fruit of the trees in the garden the Lord has told us, 'Eat.' But of the fruit of the tree that is in the middle of the garden He has told us, 'You shall not eat from it, and you shall not touch it, or you will die.'"

19The serpent said to the woman, "You will surely not die. For the Lord knows that on the day you eat from it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like gods, and you will know good and evil."

20The woman saw the tree, that it was pleasant and delightful to the eye, and that its fruit was good to eat, and she took from it and ate.

21When she had first covered her shame with fig leaves, she gave some to Adam, and he ate, and his eyes were opened, and he saw that he was naked.

22He took fig leaves and sewed them together, and made himself an apron, and covered his shame.

23The Lord cursed the serpent, and was angry with it forever.

24He was angry with the woman, because she had listened to the voice of the serpent and eaten, and He said to her, "I will greatly increase your sorrow and your pain. In sorrow you shall bear children. Your return shall be to your husband, and he will rule over you."

25To Adam also He said, "Because you listened to your wife and ate from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from, the ground shall be cursed because of you. Thorns and thistles it will bring forth for you, and you will eat your bread by the sweat of your face, until you return to the earth from which you were taken. For earth you are, and to earth you will return."

26He made them garments of skin, and clothed them, and sent them out of the garden of Eden.

27On that day, as Adam went out of the garden of Eden, he burned incense as a soothing aroma: frankincense and galbanum and stacte and spices, in the morning with the rising of the sun, from the day he covered his shame.

28On that day the mouths of all the wild animals and the cattle and the birds, of everything that walks and everything that moves, were closed from speaking. For they had all spoken with one another with one lip and one tongue.

29He sent out of the garden of Eden all flesh that was in the garden of Eden, and all flesh was scattered, each by its kind and its type, to the place that had been created for it.

30To Adam alone, of all the wild animals and cattle, He gave the means to cover his shame.

31For this reason it is commanded on the tablets, for all who know the judgment of the law, that they cover their shame and do not uncover themselves as the nations uncover themselves.

32On the new moon of the fourth month, Adam and his wife went out of the garden of Eden, and they lived in the land of Elda, in the land where they had been created.

33Adam named his wife Eve.

34They had no son until the first jubilee, and after this he knew her.

35He worked the land as he had been taught in the garden of Eden.

Notes

  • vv1, 5, 6, 8, 9, 17, 18, 20, 21, 24, 25, 34 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the EOTC breaks off before them. The Greek, which gives only summaries of this chapter, agrees in substance in four of them: the order of the naming by days (v1), the rib (v5), Eve brought in on the eightieth day of her formation (v9), and Adam knew Eve his wife (v34).

  • v4 "The Lord said to us… Let us make him a help like himself" — in Genesis the Lord says I will make for him a help as his counterpart (Genesis 2:18). In Jubilees He speaks to the angels, and says let us, as He does over the making of humankind: Let us make humankind in our image (Genesis 1:26).

  • vv5, 8 "one bone from among his bones, and this rib… the rib, his wife" — the Ge'ez says first ʿaḍma ʾaḥada, one bone, then names it gabo, which Charles renders rib. The Hebrew of Genesis 2:21, tsela, is rendered side in this project's Genesis; see the note there.

  • vv8–13 "forty days… the eightieth day" — the law for a mother after childbirth: seven days unclean and thirty-three days in the blood of her purifying for a boy, two weeks and sixty-six days for a girl (Leviticus 12:2–5). That makes forty and eighty, and Jubilees finds the reason in Eden: Adam was brought into the garden on his fortieth day, Eve on her eightieth. The garden is holy (v12), and the rule of the sanctuary is the rule of the garden.

  • v17 "in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month" — the same date on which the flood will begin: in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month — on that day all the fountains of the great deep were split open (Genesis 7:11).

  • v19 "You will surely not die" — Genesis 3:4–5, with one change: the serpent says the Lord knows, where Genesis has God knows.

  • v27 "he burned incense as a soothing aroma: frankincense and galbanum and stacte and spices" — the incense of the tabernacle: stacte and onycha and galbanum… and pure frankincense (Exodus 30:34). Adam's first act outside the garden is a priest's.

  • v28 "one lip and one tongue" — the words of Babel: All the earth was one lip and one set of words (Genesis 11:1). Before the animals lost their speech, the serpent's talk with the woman was nothing strange.

  • v31 "that they cover their shame and do not uncover themselves as the nations uncover themselves" — God clothed Adam and Eve (Genesis 3:21), and Jubilees makes that clothing a law.

  • v32 "the land of Elda" — named only here in the book. The Ge'ez says the land of their creation: the place Adam was made, outside the garden (v9).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: From Cain and Abel to Noah
chapters.html:
Jubilees 4

1In the third week of the second jubilee she bore Cain, and in the fourth she bore Abel, and in the fifth she bore her daughter Awan.

2In the first year of the third jubilee Cain killed Abel, because an offering was accepted from his hand, but from the hand of Cain his sacrifice was not accepted.

3He killed him in the field, and his blood cried out from the ground to heaven, lamenting because he had been killed.

4The Lord rebuked Cain because of Abel, because he had killed him, and He made him a fugitive on the earth because of his brother's blood, and He cursed him on the earth.

5For this reason it is written on the tablets of heaven, "Cursed is he who strikes his neighbor with evil intent," and all who have seen it shall say, "So be it"; and the man who has seen it and not told it, let him be cursed like him.

6For this reason, when we come before the Lord our God, we make known all the sin that is done in heaven and on earth, in light and in darkness and everywhere.

7Adam and his wife mourned for Abel four weeks of years. In the fourth year of the fifth week he was glad, and Adam knew his wife again, and she bore him a son, and he called his name Seth, for he said, "The Lord has raised up a second seed for us on the earth in place of Abel, because Cain killed him."

8In the sixth week she bore his daughter Azura.

9Cain took Awan his sister as his wife, and she bore him Enoch at the end of the fourth jubilee. In the first year of the first week of the fifth jubilee houses were built on the earth, and Cain built a city and called its name after the name of his son Enoch.

10Adam knew Eve his wife, and she bore nine more children.

11In the fifth week of the fifth jubilee Seth took Azura his sister as his wife, and in its fourth year she bore him Enosh.

12He was the first to call on the name of the Lord on the earth.

13In the seventh jubilee, in the third week, Enosh took Noam his sister as his wife, and she bore him a son in the third year of the fifth week, and he called his name Kenan.

14At the end of the eighth jubilee Kenan took Mualeleth his sister as his wife, and she bore him a son in the ninth jubilee, in the first week, in the third year of this week, and he called his name Mahalalel.

15In the second week of the tenth jubilee Mahalalel took for himself a wife, Dinah, the daughter of Barakiel, the daughter of his father's sister, and she bore him a son in the third week, in its sixth year, and he called his name Jared; for in his days the angels of the Lord came down to the earth, those who are named the Watchers, to teach the children of men and to do judgment and uprightness on the earth.

16In the eleventh jubilee Jared took for himself a wife named Baraka, the daughter of Rasuyal, the daughter of his father's sister, in the fourth week of this jubilee, and she bore him a son in the fifth week, in the fourth year of the jubilee, and he called his name Enoch.

17He was the first of the sons of men born on the earth to learn writing and knowledge and wisdom, and he wrote down the signs of heaven by the order of their months in a book, so that the children of men might know the seasons of the years by their order, month by month.

18He was the first to write a testimony, and he testified to the sons of men among the generations of the earth. He told the weeks of the jubilees and made known the days of the years; he set the months in order and told the sabbaths of the years, as we made them known to him.

19What had been and what will be he saw in a vision in his sleep, how it will be for the sons of men through their generations until the day of judgment. He saw and understood everything, and he wrote his testimony and placed the testimony on the earth for all the children of men and for their generations.

20In the twelfth jubilee, in its seventh week, he took for himself a wife named Edni, the daughter of Daniel, the daughter of his father's sister, and in the sixth year of this week she bore him a son, and he called his name Methuselah.

21He was with the angels of God for six jubilees of years, and they showed him everything on earth and in the heavens, the rule of the sun, and he wrote down everything.

22He testified to the Watchers, who had sinned with the daughters of men; for these had begun to join themselves with the daughters of men and be defiled, and Enoch testified against them all.

23He was taken up from among the sons of men, and we brought him into the garden of Eden in greatness and honor, and there he writes down the judgment and the condemnation forever, and all the wickedness of the children of men.

24Because of him the waters of the flood did not come over all the land of Eden, for he was set there as a sign, to testify against all the sons of men and to tell all the deeds of the generations until the day of judgment.

25He burned the evening incense of the sanctuary, which is acceptable before the Lord, on the Mountain of Midday.

26For the Lord has four places on the earth: the garden of Eden, and the Mountain of the East, and this mountain on which you are today, Mount Sinai, and Mount Zion, which will be made holy in the new creation for the hallowing of the earth. Through it the earth will be made holy from all guilt and from uncleanness through the generations of the world.

27In the fourteenth jubilee Methuselah took as his wife Edna, the daughter of Ezrael, the daughter of his father's sister, in the third week, in the first year of this week; and he fathered a son and called his name Lamech.

28In the fifteenth jubilee, in the third week, Lamech took a wife named Betenos, the daughter of Barakiel, the daughter of his father's sister, and in this week she bore him a son, and he called his name Noah, saying, "This one will comfort me for my sorrow and for all my work, and for the ground that the Lord has cursed."

29At the end of the nineteenth jubilee, in the seventh week, in its sixth year, Adam died, and all his sons buried him in the land of his creation, and he was the first to be buried in the earth.

30He was seventy years short of a thousand years, for a thousand years are one day in the testimony of the heavens. For this reason it was written about the tree of knowledge, "On the day you eat from it you will die"; and for this reason he did not complete the years of this day.

31At the end of this jubilee Cain was killed, after him, in the same year. His house fell on him, and he died in the middle of his house and was killed by its stones; for with a stone he had killed Abel, and by a stone he was killed, in righteous judgment.

32For this reason it was ordained on the tablets of heaven: with the instrument with which a man kills his neighbor, with it he shall be killed; as he wounded him, so they shall do to him.

33In the twenty-fifth jubilee Noah took for himself a wife named Emzara, the daughter of Rakiel, the daughter of his [father's] sister, in the first year of the fifth week; and in its third year she bore him Shem, in its fifth year she bore him Ham, and in the first year of the sixth week she bore him Japheth.

Notes

  • Verses 3–14 and v2 — the EOTC text here has verses 1–2 and then 15–33. Its v2 runs from Cain killed straight into the last words of v14 (…and he called his name Mahalalel). Verses 3–14 are rendered from the second Ge'ez text, which has them (its v11 holds v12 as well), and the stray end of v2 is rendered where it belongs, in v14.

  • vv1, 2, 7, 9, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 29, 30, 31, 33 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the EOTC breaks off before them, and at v7 the second Ge'ez text does too. The Asmara printing also has vv3–14. The Greek, a list of dates and wives, agrees in substance where it overlaps: a daughter born after Abel (v1), Abel killed and mourned four week-periods, that is, twenty-eight years (vv2, 7), and at v31 he too had killed Abel with stones.

  • The dates — a jubilee is 49 years and a week 7, so Adam's death at the end of the nineteenth jubilee, in the seventh week, in its sixth year (v29) is 18 × 49 + 6 × 7 + 6 = 930, Adam's age in Genesis: All the days of Adam that he lived were nine hundred and thirty years (Genesis 5:5). Abel dies in the first year of the third jubilee, year 99; four weeks of mourning bring it to 127; Seth is born three years later, in year 130 (v7), as in Genesis 5:3, Adam lived a hundred and thirty years… and called his name Seth.

  • v5 "Cursed is he who strikes his neighbor with evil intent," and all… shall say, "So be it" — Deuteronomy's curses: Cursed is he who strikes his neighbor in secret. All the people shall say, "Amen" (Deuteronomy 27:24). The one who saw and did not tell is the witness of Leviticus 5:1: if he does not tell it, he carries his guilt.

  • vv15–33 "the daughter of his father's sister" — so the Ge'ez, for every wife from Dinah on. The Greek has the daughter of Barachiel, his father's brother, and Charles the same. At v33 the Ge'ez has only the daughter of his sister; father's is supplied from Charles, as the rest of the chapter has it; the Asmara printing also has his sister. The early fathers marry their sisters (vv9–14); from Mahalalel on, their cousins.

  • v15 "for in his days the angels of the Lord came down" — Jared is Hebrew Yered, coming down; see 1 Enoch 6:6. In Jubilees the Watchers come down to teach and to do justice, and go wrong only afterward (v22), where 1 Enoch has them come down already sworn to sin.

  • vv17–19 "the first… to learn writing… the signs of heaven… a vision in his sleep" — the books of 1 Enoch: the Astronomical Book, on the months and the signs of heaven (1 Enoch 72–82), and the Dream Visions (83–90). Jude calls him Enoch, the seventh from Adam (Jude 14).

  • vv21–23 "with the angels of God for six jubilees… we brought him into the garden of Eden" — Genesis: Enoch walked with God after he fathered Methuselah three hundred years… He was not, for God took him (Genesis 5:22–24). Six jubilees are 294 years.

  • v24 "the waters of the flood did not come over all the land of Eden" — so both Ge'ez texts, with not. Charles reads the opposite: on account of it (God) brought the waters of the flood upon all the land of Eden.

  • v25 "the evening incense of the sanctuary… on the Mountain of Midday" — dabra qatr, the mountain of noon; Charles has only the Mount. Enoch offers the incense that Aaron will burn between the evenings (Exodus 30:8), as Adam did on leaving the garden (3:27).

  • vv29–30 "a thousand years are one day" — the psalm: a thousand years in Your eyes are like yesterday when it passes (Psalm 90:4); Peter: with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day (2 Peter 3:8). So on the day you eat from it you will die (Genesis 2:17) came true: Adam died within his first thousand-year day.

  • vv31–32 "with the instrument with which a man kills his neighbor, with it he shall be killed" — the law of like for like: as he has done, so it shall be done to him (Leviticus 24:19).

speech.text: Jubilees 4
In the third week of the second jubilee she bore Cain, and in the fourth she bore Abel, and in the fifth she bore her daughter Awan.
In the first year of the third jubilee Cain killed Abel, because an offering was accepted from his hand, but from the hand of Cain his sacrifice was not accepted.
He killed him in the field, and his blood cried out from the ground to heaven, lamenting because he had been killed.
The Lord rebuked Cain because of Abel, because he had killed him, and He made him a fugitive on the earth because of his brother's blood, and He cursed him on the earth.

For this reason it is written on the tablets of heaven, "Cursed is he who strikes his neighbor with evil intent," and all who have seen it shall say, "So be it"; and the man who has seen it and not told it, let him be cursed like him.
For this reason, when we come before the Lord our God, we make known all the sin that is done in heaven and on earth, in light and in darkness and everywhere.

Adam and his wife mourned for Abel four weeks of years. In the fourth year of the fifth week he was glad, and Adam knew his wife again, and she bore him a son, and he called his name Seth, for he said, "The Lord has raised up a second seed for us on the earth in place of Abel, because Cain killed him."
In the sixth week she bore his daughter Azura.

Cain took Awan his sister as his wife, and she bore him Enoch at the end of the fourth jubilee. In the first year of the first week of the fifth jubilee houses were built on the earth, and Cain built a city and called its name after the name of his son Enoch.
Adam knew Eve his wife, and she bore nine more children.
In the fifth week of the fifth jubilee Seth took Azura his sister as his wife, and in its fourth year she bore him Enosh.
He was the first to call on the name of the Lord on the earth.
In the seventh jubilee, in the third week, Enosh took Noam his sister as his wife, and she bore him a son in the third year of the fifth week, and he called his name Kenan.

At the end of the eighth jubilee Kenan took Mualeleth his sister as his wife, and she bore him a son in the ninth jubilee, in the first week, in the third year of this week, and he called his name Mahalalel.

In the second week of the tenth jubilee Mahalalel took for himself a wife, Dinah, the daughter of Barakiel, the daughter of his father's sister, and she bore him a son in the third week, in its sixth year, and he called his name Jared; for in his days the angels of the Lord came down to the earth, those who are named the Watchers, to teach the children of men and to do judgment and uprightness on the earth.

In the eleventh jubilee Jared took for himself a wife named Baraka, the daughter of Rasuyal, the daughter of his father's sister, in the fourth week of this jubilee, and she bore him a son in the fifth week, in the fourth year of the jubilee, and he called his name Enoch.

He was the first of the sons of men born on the earth to learn writing and knowledge and wisdom, and he wrote down the signs of heaven by the order of their months in a book, so that the children of men might know the seasons of the years by their order, month by month.

He was the first to write a testimony, and he testified to the sons of men among the generations of the earth. He told the weeks of the jubilees and made known the days of the years; he set the months in order and told the sabbaths of the years, as we made them known to him.

What had been and what will be he saw in a vision in his sleep, how it will be for the sons of men through their generations until the day of judgment. He saw and understood everything, and he wrote his testimony and placed the testimony on the earth for all the children of men and for their generations.

In the twelfth jubilee, in its seventh week, he took for himself a wife named Edni, the daughter of Daniel, the daughter of his father's sister, and in the sixth year of this week she bore him a son, and he called his name Methuselah.
He was with the angels of God for six jubilees of years, and they showed him everything on earth and in the heavens, the rule of the sun, and he wrote down everything.
He testified to the Watchers, who had sinned with the daughters of men; for these had begun to join themselves with the daughters of men and be defiled, and Enoch testified against them all.

He was taken up from among the sons of men, and we brought him into the garden of Eden in greatness and honor, and there he writes down the judgment and the condemnation forever, and all the wickedness of the children of men.

Because of him the waters of the flood did not come over all the land of Eden, for he was set there as a sign, to testify against all the sons of men and to tell all the deeds of the generations until the day of judgment.
He burned the evening incense of the sanctuary, which is acceptable before the Lord, on the Mountain of Midday.

For the Lord has four places on the earth: the garden of Eden, and the Mountain of the East, and this mountain on which you are today, Mount Sinai, and Mount Zion, which will be made holy in the new creation for the hallowing of the earth. Through it the earth will be made holy from all guilt and from uncleanness through the generations of the world.

In the fourteenth jubilee Methuselah took as his wife Edna, the daughter of Ezrael, the daughter of his father's sister, in the third week, in the first year of this week; and he fathered a son and called his name Lamech.

In the fifteenth jubilee, in the third week, Lamech took a wife named Betenos, the daughter of Barakiel, the daughter of his father's sister, and in this week she bore him a son, and he called his name Noah, saying, "This one will comfort me for my sorrow and for all my work, and for the ground that the Lord has cursed."
At the end of the nineteenth jubilee, in the seventh week, in its sixth year, Adam died, and all his sons buried him in the land of his creation, and he was the first to be buried in the earth.

He was seventy years short of a thousand years, for a thousand years are one day in the testimony of the heavens. For this reason it was written about the tree of knowledge, "On the day you eat from it you will die"; and for this reason he did not complete the years of this day.

At the end of this jubilee Cain was killed, after him, in the same year. His house fell on him, and he died in the middle of his house and was killed by its stones; for with a stone he had killed Abel, and by a stone he was killed, in righteous judgment.
For this reason it was ordained on the tablets of heaven: with the instrument with which a man kills his neighbor, with it he shall be killed; as he wounded him, so they shall do to him.

In the twenty-fifth jubilee Noah took for himself a wife named Emzara, the daughter of Rakiel, the daughter of his [father's] sister, in the first year of the fifth week; and in its third year she bore him Shem, in its fifth year she bore him Ham, and in the first year of the sixth week she bore him Japheth.

chapters.title: The Watchers' Sons and the Flood
chapters.html:
Jubilees 5

1And it came to pass, when the sons of men began to multiply on the face of all the earth and daughters were born to them, that the angels of the Lord saw them in a certain year of this jubilee, that they were beautiful to look at; and they took wives for themselves from all whom they chose, and these bore them sons, and they were giants.

2Wrongdoing grew on the earth, and all flesh corrupted its way, from man to the cattle and to the wild animals and to the birds and to everything that walks on the earth: all of them corrupted their ways and their order, and they began to devour one another; and wrongdoing grew on the earth, and every thought of the minds of all men was evil, all the time.

3The Lord looked at the earth, and it was corrupt. All flesh had corrupted its order, and all that were on the earth had done evil before His eyes.

4He said that He would wipe out man and all flesh on the face of the earth that He had created.

5Noah alone found favor in His eyes.

6Against His angels whom He had sent to the earth He was very angry, and He uprooted them from all their dominion; and He told us to bind them in the depths of the earth, and there they are bound in the middle of them, and are kept apart.

7Against their children a word went out from before His face, to strike them with the sword and remove them from under heaven.

8He said, "My spirit shall not remain on man forever, for they are flesh, and their days shall be a hundred and twenty years."

9He sent His sword among them, so that each should kill his neighbor, and they began to kill with the sword, and they were wiped out from the earth.

10Their fathers watched, and after this they were bound in the depths of the earth until the day of the great judgment, when judgment is carried out on all who have corrupted their ways and their works before the Lord.

11He wiped them all out from their places, and not one of them was left whom He did not judge for all their wickedness.

12He made for all His works a new and righteous nature, so that they should never again sin in all their nature, but should all be righteous, each in its kind, always.

13The judgment of all of them is ordained and written on the tablets of heaven, and there is no injustice: even for all who leave the path that is ordained for them to walk in; if they do not walk in it, judgment is written down for every creature and for every kind.

14There is nothing in heaven or on earth, in light or in darkness, in Sheol or in the deep, or in the place of darkness, whose judgment is not ordained and written and engraved.

15He will judge concerning all: the great according to his greatness, the small according to his smallness, and each one according to his way.

16He is not one who shows partiality, and He is not one who takes gifts, when He says He will carry out judgment on each one. If one gave Him everything that is on the earth, He would not show partiality or accept it from him, for He is a righteous judge.

17Of the sons of Israel it has been written and ordained: if they turn to Him in righteousness, He will forgive all their guilt and pardon all their sins.

18It is written and ordained that He will show mercy to all who turn from all their error, once each year.

19As for all who corrupted their ways and their counsel before the flood, He showed favor to no one except Noah alone. He showed him favor for the sake of his sons, whom He saved from the waters of the flood because of him, for his heart was righteous in all his ways, as was commanded concerning him, and he had not left anything that was ordained for him.

20The Lord said that He would wipe out everything on the dry ground, from man to the cattle, to the wild animals, to the birds, to what moves on the earth.

21He commanded Noah to make himself an ark, to save himself from the waters of the flood.

22Noah made the ark in every respect as He had commanded him, in the twenty-seventh jubilee of years, in the fifth week, in its fifth year.

23He went in, in its sixth year, in the second month, from the new moon of the second month until the sixteenth: he went in, and all that we brought to him, into the ark; and the Lord shut it from outside on the evening of the seventeenth.

24The Lord opened seven floodgates of heaven, and opened the mouths of the springs of the great deep, seven mouths in number.

25The floodgates began to pour down water from heaven forty days and forty nights, and the springs of the deep also sent up waters, until the whole world was full of water.

26The waters grew on the earth. The waters rose fifteen cubits above every high mountain, and the ark was lifted up from the earth and moved on the face of the waters.

27The waters stood on the face of the earth five months, a hundred and fifty days.

28The ark went and came to rest on the top of Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat.

29In the fourth month the springs of the great deep were stopped, and the floodgates of heaven were held back; and on the new moon of the seventh month all the mouths of the depths of the earth were opened, and the water began to go down into the deep below.

30On the new moon of the tenth month the tops of the mountains appeared, and on the new moon of the first month the earth appeared.

31The waters dried up from the earth in the fifth week, in its seventh year, and on the seventeenth day of the second month the earth was dry.

32On its twenty-seventh day he opened the ark and sent out of it the wild animals and the birds and what moves.

Notes

  • vv1, 2, 6, 9, 12, 13, 14, 18, 19, 23, 25, 29, 30, 31 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). In v1 the EOTC stops at daughters were born to them, before the angels ever see them.

  • vv1–2 "the angels of the Lord saw them… every thought of the minds of all men was evil" — Genesis 6:1–5: the sons of God saw the daughters of humankind… every shaping of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all the day. Where Genesis has the sons of God, Jubilees has the angels of the Lord, and the Watchers of 4:15 are meant.

  • vv6–10 "bind them in the depths of the earth… until the day of the great judgment" — the sentence of 1 Enoch 10:12: bind them for seventy generations under the hills of the earth, until the day of their judgment. Jude: the angels who did not keep their own domain, but left their proper dwelling, He has kept in eternal chains under darkness for the judgment of the great day (Jude 6). The sons kill one another with the sword God sends among them (v9), as Gabriel is told in 1 Enoch 10:9: send them against one another in a war of destruction.

  • v16 "He is not one who shows partiality, and He is not one who takes gifts" — Moses: the great God, mighty and fearsome, who does not show partiality and does not take a bribe (Deuteronomy 10:17). The Ge'ez says lift up the face, the Hebrew idiom for favoring someone; v19 uses it too.

  • vv17–18 "He will show mercy to all who turn… once each year" — the Day of Atonement: to make atonement for the sons of Israel for all their sins once a year (Leviticus 16:34). The Asmara printing has once each year, məʿra la-la-ʿāmat; the EOTC text as held here ends at all their error.

  • v19 "He showed him favor for the sake of his sons" — Ezekiel names Noah as a righteous man whose righteousness could save no one else: even if Noah, Daniel and Job were in it… they would save neither son nor daughter (Ezekiel 14:20). In the flood, Jubilees says, it did: his sons were saved because of him.

  • v22 "in the twenty-seventh jubilee" — the EOTC reads in the two jubilees, ba-kəlʾetu ʾiyobelwu, and so do the second Ge'ez text and the Asmara printing. The chapter's own count needs the twenty-seventh, as Charles has it: Noah was born in the fifteenth jubilee (4:28), and 26 × 49 + 4 × 7 + 5 = 1307, about six hundred years after his birth, the age Genesis gives for the flood (Genesis 7:11). The English follows the count.

  • vv23–32 the dates of the flood — Genesis: the flood began in the second month, on the seventeenth day (Genesis 7:11), and the LORD shut him in (7:16); the waters prevailed a hundred and fifty days (7:24); in the tenth month, on the first of the month, the heads of the mountains were seen (8:5); in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dried out (8:14). Jubilees keeps every date and adds its own new-moon markers. Five months of thirty days make the hundred and fifty days of v27.

  • v28 "the top of Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat" — Genesis names only the mountains of Ararat (Genesis 8:4). Jubilees names the peak.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.
