chapters.title: The Covenant with Noah and the Year of 364 Days
chapters.html:
Jubilees 6

1On the new moon of the third month he went out of the ark, and built an altar on that mountain.

2He appeared on the earth, and took a young goat, and made atonement with its blood for all the guilt of the earth, for everything that had been on it had been wiped out except those who were in the ark with Noah.

3He offered up the fat on the altar, and took an ox and a goat and a sheep and kids, and salt, and a turtledove and a young dove, and placed a burnt offering on the altar, and poured on it an offering mixed with oil, and sprinkled wine, and put frankincense on everything, and made a soothing aroma rise, acceptable before the Lord.

4The Lord smelled the soothing aroma, and He made a covenant with him that there should never again be a flood to ruin the earth: all the days of the earth, seed-time and harvest shall not cease; cold and heat, summer and winter, and day and night shall not change their order, and shall never cease.

5"As for you, be fruitful and multiply on the earth, and increase on it, and be a blessing on it. The fear of you and the dread of you I will put on everything that is on the earth and in the sea.

6I have given you all the wild animals, and all the cattle, and all that flies, and all that moves on the earth, and the fish in the waters, and everything for food. Like the green plants, I have given you everything to eat.

7But flesh with its life, with its blood, you shall not eat, for the life of all flesh is in the blood; otherwise your blood, your lives, will be required. From the hand of every man, from the hand of every living thing, I will require the blood of man.

8Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man his blood shall be shed, for in the image of the Lord He made Adam.

9As for you, be fruitful and multiply on the earth."

10Noah and his sons swore that they would not eat any blood that is in any flesh, and he made a covenant before the Lord God forever, through all the generations of the earth, in this month.

11For this reason He told you, too, to make a covenant with the sons of Israel in this month on the mountain, with an oath, and to sprinkle blood on them because of all the words of the covenant that the Lord made with them for all days.

12This testimony is written concerning you, that you keep it all the days, so that you do not eat on any day any blood of wild animals or birds, all the days of the earth; and the man who eats the blood of wild animals or cattle or birds during all the days of the earth, he and his seed shall be uprooted from the land.

13As for you, command the sons of Israel not to eat any blood, so that their name and their seed may be before the Lord our God all the days.

14For this law there is no limit of days, for it is forever. They shall keep it through their generations, so that they continue to plead for themselves with blood before the altar; every day, morning and evening, they make atonement for themselves continually before the Lord, so that they keep it and are not uprooted.

15He gave Noah and his sons a sign that there would not again be a flood on the earth.

16He set His bow in the cloud as a sign of the eternal covenant, that there should not again be a flood on the earth to ruin it, all the days of the earth.

17For this reason it is ordained and written on the tablets of heaven that they should keep the Festival of Weeks in this month, once a year, to renew the covenant every year.

18This whole festival was kept in heaven from the day of creation until the days of Noah, twenty-six jubilees and five weeks of years; and Noah and his sons kept it seven jubilees and one week of years, until the day of Noah's death. From the day of Noah's death his sons corrupted it, until the days of Abraham, and they ate blood.

19Abraham alone kept it, and Isaac and Jacob, his sons, kept it until your days; and in your days the sons of Israel forgot it, until you kept it anew on this mountain.

20As for you, command the sons of Israel to keep this festival in all their generations as a commandment for them: one day in the year, in this month, they shall keep the festival.

21For it is the Festival of Weeks and the Festival of First Fruits. This festival is twofold and of two kinds; keep it as it is written and engraved concerning it.

22For I have written it in the book of the first law, in what I wrote for you, that you should keep it in its season, one day in the year; and I told you its offering too, so that they should remember it, and the sons of Israel should keep it through their generations in this month, one day every year.

23On the new moon of the first month, and on the new moon of the fourth month, and on the new moon of the seventh month, and on the new moon of the tenth month: these are days of remembrance, and they are the days of the seasons in the four divisions of the year. They are written and ordained as a testimony for the year.

24Noah ordained them for himself as festivals for the eternal generations, so that they became a memorial for him.

25On the new moon of the first month he was told to make the ark, and on it the earth dried, and he opened the ark and saw the earth.

26On the new moon of the fourth month the mouths of the depths of the abyss below were closed, and on the new moon of the seventh month all the mouths of the depths of the earth were opened, and the waters began to go down into them.

27On the new moon of the tenth month the tops of the mountains appeared, and Noah was glad.

28For this reason he ordained them for himself as festivals of remembrance forever.

29They placed them on the tablets of heaven; each had thirteen weeks, and their memorial passed from one to another, from the first to the second, and from the second to the third, and from the third to the fourth.

30All the days of the commandments will be fifty-two weeks of days, and these will make the whole year complete.

31So it is engraved and ordained on the tablets of heaven. There is no neglecting it for a single year, or from year to year.

32As for you, command the sons of Israel to keep the years by this number, three hundred and sixty-four days, and it will be a complete year; and they will not disturb its time from its days and from its festivals, for everything will happen in them according to their testimony, and they will not leave out any day or disturb any festival.

33If they transgress and do not keep them as He commanded, then they will all corrupt their seasons, and the years will be shifted from this order. They will corrupt the seasons, and the years will be shifted, and they will transgress their ordinances.

34All the sons of Israel will forget, and will not find the path of the years, and will forget the new moons and seasons and sabbaths, and will go wrong in all the order of the years.

35I know it. From now on I will make it known to you; it is not of my own devising, for the book lies written before me, and on the tablets of heaven the division of days is ordained, so that they do not forget the festivals of the covenant and walk by the festivals of the nations, after their error and after their ignorance.

36There will be those who watch the moon closely, how it disturbs the seasons and comes in ten days too soon from year to year.

37For this reason years will come upon them in which they will corrupt the order and make the day of testimony a worthless day, and an unclean day a festival, and they will confuse all the days, the holy with the unclean and the unclean day with the holy; for they will go wrong as to the months and sabbaths and festivals and jubilees.

38For this reason I command you and testify to you, so that you may testify to them. For after your death your children will corrupt it, so that they do not make the year three hundred and sixty-four days only; and for this reason they will go wrong as to the new moons and seasons and sabbaths and festivals, and they will eat all kinds of blood with all kinds of flesh.

Notes

  • vv1, 3, 5, 10, 11, 12, 16, 19, 22, 23, 29, 30, 31, 32, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). In v23 the EOTC lists only three new moons, the first, fourth and tenth; the Asmara printing has the seventh as well, which vv26 and 29 need for the four divisions of the year.

  • v2 "He appeared on the earth… and made atonement with its blood for all the guilt of the earth" — ʾastarʾaya, appeared, in both Ge'ez texts. Charles has he made atonement for the earth, the verb that follows in the same verse. Before any burnt offering, Noah's first sacrifice in Jubilees is atonement for the land the flood has cleansed.

  • vv3–4 "The Lord smelled the soothing aroma" — Genesis 8:20–22: The LORD smelled the soothing aroma… From now on, all the days of the earth — seed and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night — shall not cease. The offerings, salt and oil and wine and frankincense, are those of Leviticus.

  • vv5–9 "The fear of you and the dread of you… for in the image of the Lord He made Adam" — God's words to Noah in Genesis 9:1–7, retold closely. Genesis ends v6 in the image of God He made the human; the Ge'ez has Adam, the same Hebrew word read as a name.

  • vv10–11 "Noah and his sons swore… He told you, too, to make a covenant… in this month on the mountain" — the covenant at Sinai is dated to the same month as Noah's: Moses took the blood and threw it on the people, and said, "Here is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has cut with you" (Exodus 24:8). Jubilees makes Sinai a renewal of what Noah swore.

  • vv17–21 "the Festival of Weeks… the Festival of First Fruits" — Exodus 34:22: The Festival of Weeks you shall make for yourself, the firstfruits of the wheat harvest. In Jubilees it is also the day the covenant is renewed each year, kept in heaven since creation.

  • v18 "twenty-six jubilees and five weeks of years… seven jubilees and one week of years" — 26 × 49 + 5 × 7 = 1309, the year Noah left the ark (5:22–23 has him enter it in 1308). Seven jubilees and a week are 350 years: Noah lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years (Genesis 9:28).

  • vv23–29 the four new moons — the first days of the first, fourth, seventh and tenth months divide the year into four quarters of thirteen weeks. Jubilees ties each to a day of the flood: the ark ordered and the earth dry (v25), the deep closed (v26), the deep opened (v26), the mountain tops seen (v27; Genesis 8:5).

  • vv30–32 "fifty-two weeks of days… three hundred and sixty-four days" — 52 × 7 = 364: a year of whole weeks, in which every date falls on the same day of the week each year. It is the year of 1 Enoch's Astronomical Book: every three hundred and sixty-four days (1 Enoch 74:12).

  • v36 "those who watch the moon closely… ten days too soon" — a year of twelve moons is about 354 days, ten days short of 364. The warning answers 2:9, where the signs of the calendar are given to the sun alone.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

speech.text: Jubilees 6
On the new moon of the third month he went out of the ark, and built an altar on that mountain.

He appeared on the earth, and took a young goat, and made atonement with its blood for all the guilt of the earth, for everything that had been on it had been wiped out except those who were in the ark with Noah.

He offered up the fat on the altar, and took an ox and a goat and a sheep and kids, and salt, and a turtledove and a young dove, and placed a burnt offering on the altar, and poured on it an offering mixed with oil, and sprinkled wine, and put frankincense on everything, and made a soothing aroma rise, acceptable before the Lord.

The Lord smelled the soothing aroma, and He made a covenant with him that there should never again be a flood to ruin the earth: all the days of the earth, seed-time and harvest shall not cease; cold and heat, summer and winter, and day and night shall not change their order, and shall never cease.
"As for you, be fruitful and multiply on the earth, and increase on it, and be a blessing on it. The fear of you and the dread of you I will put on everything that is on the earth and in the sea.

I have given you all the wild animals, and all the cattle, and all that flies, and all that moves on the earth, and the fish in the waters, and everything for food. Like the green plants, I have given you everything to eat.

But flesh with its life, with its blood, you shall not eat, for the life of all flesh is in the blood; otherwise your blood, your lives, will be required. From the hand of every man, from the hand of every living thing, I will require the blood of man.
Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man his blood shall be shed, for in the image of the Lord He made Adam.
As for you, be fruitful and multiply on the earth."
Noah and his sons swore that they would not eat any blood that is in any flesh, and he made a covenant before the Lord God forever, through all the generations of the earth, in this month.

For this reason He told you, too, to make a covenant with the sons of Israel in this month on the mountain, with an oath, and to sprinkle blood on them because of all the words of the covenant that the Lord made with them for all days.

This testimony is written concerning you, that you keep it all the days, so that you do not eat on any day any blood of wild animals or birds, all the days of the earth; and the man who eats the blood of wild animals or cattle or birds during all the days of the earth, he and his seed shall be uprooted from the land.
As for you, command the sons of Israel not to eat any blood, so that their name and their seed may be before the Lord our God all the days.

For this law there is no limit of days, for it is forever. They shall keep it through their generations, so that they continue to plead for themselves with blood before the altar; every day, morning and evening, they make atonement for themselves continually before the Lord, so that they keep it and are not uprooted.
He gave Noah and his sons a sign that there would not again be a flood on the earth.
He set His bow in the cloud as a sign of the eternal covenant, that there should not again be a flood on the earth to ruin it, all the days of the earth.
For this reason it is ordained and written on the tablets of heaven that they should keep the Festival of Weeks in this month, once a year, to renew the covenant every year.

This whole festival was kept in heaven from the day of creation until the days of Noah, twenty-six jubilees and five weeks of years; and Noah and his sons kept it seven jubilees and one week of years, until the day of Noah's death. From the day of Noah's death his sons corrupted it, until the days of Abraham, and they ate blood.
Abraham alone kept it, and Isaac and Jacob, his sons, kept it until your days; and in your days the sons of Israel forgot it, until you kept it anew on this mountain.
As for you, command the sons of Israel to keep this festival in all their generations as a commandment for them: one day in the year, in this month, they shall keep the festival.
For it is the Festival of Weeks and the Festival of First Fruits. This festival is twofold and of two kinds; keep it as it is written and engraved concerning it.

For I have written it in the book of the first law, in what I wrote for you, that you should keep it in its season, one day in the year; and I told you its offering too, so that they should remember it, and the sons of Israel should keep it through their generations in this month, one day every year.

On the new moon of the first month, and on the new moon of the fourth month, and on the new moon of the seventh month, and on the new moon of the tenth month: these are days of remembrance, and they are the days of the seasons in the four divisions of the year. They are written and ordained as a testimony for the year.
Noah ordained them for himself as festivals for the eternal generations, so that they became a memorial for him.
On the new moon of the first month he was told to make the ark, and on it the earth dried, and he opened the ark and saw the earth.

On the new moon of the fourth month the mouths of the depths of the abyss below were closed, and on the new moon of the seventh month all the mouths of the depths of the earth were opened, and the waters began to go down into them.
On the new moon of the tenth month the tops of the mountains appeared, and Noah was glad.
For this reason he ordained them for himself as festivals of remembrance forever.

They placed them on the tablets of heaven; each had thirteen weeks, and their memorial passed from one to another, from the first to the second, and from the second to the third, and from the third to the fourth.
All the days of the commandments will be fifty-two weeks of days, and these will make the whole year complete.
So it is engraved and ordained on the tablets of heaven. There is no neglecting it for a single year, or from year to year.

As for you, command the sons of Israel to keep the years by this number, three hundred and sixty-four days, and it will be a complete year; and they will not disturb its time from its days and from its festivals, for everything will happen in them according to their testimony, and they will not leave out any day or disturb any festival.

If they transgress and do not keep them as He commanded, then they will all corrupt their seasons, and the years will be shifted from this order. They will corrupt the seasons, and the years will be shifted, and they will transgress their ordinances.
All the sons of Israel will forget, and will not find the path of the years, and will forget the new moons and seasons and sabbaths, and will go wrong in all the order of the years.

I know it. From now on I will make it known to you; it is not of my own devising, for the book lies written before me, and on the tablets of heaven the division of days is ordained, so that they do not forget the festivals of the covenant and walk by the festivals of the nations, after their error and after their ignorance.
There will be those who watch the moon closely, how it disturbs the seasons and comes in ten days too soon from year to year.

For this reason years will come upon them in which they will corrupt the order and make the day of testimony a worthless day, and an unclean day a festival, and they will confuse all the days, the holy with the unclean and the unclean day with the holy; for they will go wrong as to the months and sabbaths and festivals and jubilees.

For this reason I command you and testify to you, so that you may testify to them. For after your death your children will corrupt it, so that they do not make the year three hundred and sixty-four days only; and for this reason they will go wrong as to the new moons and seasons and sabbaths and festivals, and they will eat all kinds of blood with all kinds of flesh.

chapters.title: Noah's Vineyard and Noah's Charge
chapters.html:
Jubilees 7

1In the seventh week, in its first year, in this jubilee, Noah planted vines on the mountain on which the ark had come to rest, named Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat. They bore fruit in the fourth year, and he guarded their fruit and gathered it that year, in the seventh month.

2He made wine from it and put it in a vessel, and kept it until the fifth year, until the first day, on the new moon of the first month.

3He kept the day of this festival with joy, and he made a burnt offering to the Lord: one young bull and one ram, and seven sheep a year old, and a kid of the goats, to make atonement with it for himself and his sons.

4He prepared the kid first, and put some of its blood on the flesh on the altar he had made, and all the fat he offered up on the altar where he made the burnt offering, and the bull and the ram and the sheep; and he laid all their flesh on the altar.

5He placed all their offerings, mixed with oil, on it, and afterward he sprinkled wine on the fire he had made on the altar beforehand, and he put frankincense on the altar and made a soothing aroma rise, pleasing before the Lord his God.

6He rejoiced, and he and his children drank of this wine with joy.

7It was evening, and he went into his tent, and lay down drunk and slept, and he was uncovered in his tent as he slept.

8Ham saw Noah his father naked, and went out and told his two brothers outside.

9Shem took a garment, and he rose, he and Japheth, and they put the garment on their shoulders with their faces turned back, and covered their father's shame, with their faces turned back.

10Noah woke from his sleep and knew all that his younger son had done to him, and he cursed his son and said, "Cursed be Canaan. A servant, a slave, shall he be to his brothers."

11He blessed Shem and said, "Blessed be the Lord, the God of Shem, and let Canaan be his servant.

12May the Lord make wide for Japheth, and may the Lord dwell in the dwelling of Shem, and let Canaan be their servant."

13Ham knew that his father had cursed his younger son, and he was grieved that he had cursed his son, and he parted from his father, he and his sons with him, Cush and Egypt and Put and Canaan.

14He too built himself a city, and called its name after the name of his wife, Neelatamauk.

15Japheth saw it and was jealous of his brother, and he too built himself a city, and called its name after the name of his wife, Adataneses.

16Shem lived with his father Noah, and he built a city near his father, on the mountain, and he too called its name after the name of his wife, Sedeqetelebab.

17Here are these three cities near Mount Lubar: Sedeqetelebab in front of the mountain, on its east; Naeltamauk on its south side; Adataneses toward the sea.

18These are the sons of Shem: Elam and Asshur and Arpachshad — this son was born two years after the flood — [and Lud] and Aram.

19The sons of Japheth: Gomer and Magog and Madai and Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras. These are the sons of Noah.

20In the twenty-eighth jubilee Noah began to command his sons' sons the ordinances and the commandments, all the judgment that he knew. He testified to his sons that they should do righteousness, and cover the shame of their flesh, and bless the One who created them, and honor father and mother, and love each his neighbor, and guard their souls from fornication and uncleanness and from all wrongdoing.

21For because of these three things the flood came on the earth: because of the fornication the Watchers committed, against the command of their ordinances, after the daughters of men. They took wives for themselves from all whom they chose, and made the beginning of uncleanness.

22They fathered sons, the Naphidim, and none of them were alike, and they devoured one another: the Giants killed the Naphil, and the Naphil killed the Elyo, and the Elyo killed mankind, and one man another.

23Everyone sold himself to do wrongdoing and to shed innocent blood, and the earth was filled with wrongdoing.

24After these, [they sinned against] all the wild animals and the birds, and what moves and what walks on the earth; and much blood was shed on the earth, and every thought and desire of men imagined vanity and evil all the time.

25The Lord wiped out everything from the face of the earth, because of their deeds and because of the blood in the middle of the earth.

26"We were left, I and you, my sons, and all that went in with us into the ark; and I see your works before me, that you do not walk in righteousness: you have begun to walk in the path of destruction, and you are parting from one another and are jealous of one another, and so you are not at one, my sons, each with his brother.

27For I see that the demons have begun to lead you and your children astray; and now I fear for you, that after my death you will shed the blood of men on the earth, and that you too will be wiped out from the face of the earth.

28For everyone who sheds the blood of man, and everyone who eats the blood of any flesh, will all be wiped out from the earth.

29No man who eats blood or sheds blood on the earth will be left, nor will any seed or descendants be left to him living under heaven; for they will go into Sheol, and go down into the place of condemnation, and all be taken away into the darkness of the deep by a violent death.

30No blood shall be seen on you, of all the blood there is, all the days that you slaughter any wild animal or cattle or what flies on the earth. Do a good work for your souls by covering what is shed on the face of the earth.

31Do not be like one who eats with the blood, but guard yourselves so that no one eats blood in your presence. Cover the blood, for so I have been commanded to testify to you and your children, together with all flesh.

32Do not eat the life with the flesh, so that your blood, which is your life, will not be required at the hand of any flesh that sheds it on the earth.

33For the earth will not be made clean of the blood that has been shed on it; only through the blood of the one who shed it will the earth be made clean, through all its generations.

34And now, my children, listen: do judgment and righteousness, so that you may be planted in righteousness over the face of the whole earth, and your honor may be lifted up before my God, who saved me from the waters of the flood.

35You will go and build yourselves cities, and plant in them every plant that is on the earth, and all the fruit-bearing trees too.

36For three years its fruit shall not be gathered by anyone for eating, and in the fourth year its fruit shall be made holy, and they shall offer the first fruits, acceptable before the Lord Most High, the Creator of heaven and earth and all things. Let them offer in abundance the first of the wine and oil as first fruits on the altar of the Lord, who receives it; and what is left, let the servants of the house of the Lord eat before the altar that receives it.

37In the fifth year make its release, so that you release it in righteousness and uprightness; and you will be righteous, and all your planting will prosper.

38For so your forefather Enoch commanded Methuselah his son, and Methuselah commanded Lamech his son, and Lamech commanded me all that his fathers had commanded him.

39I too command you, my sons, as Enoch commanded his son in the first jubilees. While he was alive, the seventh in his generation, he commanded and testified to his son and to his sons' sons until the day of his death."

Notes

  • vv3, 4, 8, 13, 15, 18, 22, 24, 26, 27, 29, 31, 35, 36 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). The end of v11, which the Asmara file lacks too, is rendered from Charles's edition of the Ge'ez (1895). Words in [brackets] are Charles's own corrections and are in none of his manuscripts: and Lud (v18), made from Genesis 10:22, where no manuscript names Lud; they sinned against (v24), made from 1 Enoch 7:5.

  • vv1–9 the vineyard — Genesis 9:20–23, told with more: Noah waits the years of the law for the fruit (see vv35–37), and before he drinks he offers the sacrifices of a festival. Genesis says only he drank from the wine and became drunk, and he uncovered himself inside his tent (Genesis 9:21).

  • vv10–12 "Cursed be Canaan… may the Lord dwell in the dwelling of Shem" — Genesis 9:25–27. Genesis says May God make wide for Japheth, and let him dwell in the tents of Shem, and leaves it open whether he is Japheth or God. Jubilees reads it as God: may the Lord dwell in the dwelling of Shem.

  • vv13–17 the three cities — each son names his city after his wife. Genesis names none of Noah's daughters-in-law. "on its south side" — samen, as Charles renders it. In the division of the earth (chapter 8) the same word marks the side of Ham's hot land and its partner dabub the side of Japheth's cold one (8:22–30), so the two words are rendered there, and here, as Charles gives them.

  • vv21–25 "because of these three things the flood came" — fornication, uncleanness and wrongdoing (v20). They took wives for themselves from all whom they chose is Genesis 6:2; the earth was filled with wrongdoing is Genesis 6:11, the earth was filled with violence.

  • v22 "the Naphidim" — the Nephilim of Genesis 6:4, in the form the Ge'ez gives. Charles's fuller text names three kinds, the Giants, the Naphil and the Elyo, each killing the next, as the giants of 1 Enoch 7 turn on men and on one another.

  • vv28–33 the blood — the blood law given to Noah in Genesis 9:4–6, now with its reasons. Covering the blood (vv30–31) is the law of Leviticus 17:13: he shall pour out its blood and cover it with earth. The earth will not be made clean… only through the blood of the one who shed it is Numbers 35:33: no atonement can be made for the land for the blood shed in it, except by the blood of the one who shed it.

  • vv35–37 "For three years its fruit shall not be gathered… in the fourth year… In the fifth year" — the law of new trees: For three years it shall be forbidden to you… In the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy… In the fifth year you may eat its fruit (Leviticus 19:23–25). Noah keeps it with his own vineyard (vv1–2): planted in the first year, fruit in the fourth, the wine opened in the fifth.

  • vv38–39 "Enoch… the seventh in his generation" — Enoch, the seventh from Adam (Jude 14). Noah passes on what came down to him from Enoch through Methuselah and Lamech.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Charles's edition of the Ge'ez (1895): public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.html:
Jubilees 8

1In the twenty-ninth jubilee, in the first week, at its beginning, Arpachshad took a wife named Rasueya, the daughter of Susan, the daughter of Elam, and she bore him a son in the third year of this week, and he called his name Kainam.

2The son grew, and his father taught him writing, and he went to look for a place where he could take a city for himself.

3He found writing that earlier generations had carved on a rock, and he read what was on it and copied it, and went astray because of it; for it held the teaching of the Watchers, by which they observed the omens of the sun and moon and stars, and all the signs of heaven.

4He wrote it down and said nothing about it, for he was afraid to tell Noah about it, in case he would be angry with him because of it.

5In the thirtieth jubilee, in the second week, in its first year, he took a wife named Melka, the daughter of Madai, the son of Japheth.

6In its fourth year he had a son, and called his name Shelah, for he said, "Truly I have been sent." Shelah grew up and took a wife named Muak, the daughter of Kesed, his father's brother, in the thirty-first jubilee, in the fifth week, in its first year.

7She bore him a son in its fifth year, and he called his name Eber; and he took a wife named Azurad, the daughter of Nebrod, in the thirty-second jubilee, in the seventh week, in its third year.

8In the sixth year she bore him a son, and he called his name Peleg; for in the days when he was born the children of Noah began to divide the earth among themselves, and for this reason he called his name Peleg.

9They divided it wrongly among themselves, and told Noah.

10And it came to pass at the beginning of the thirty-third jubilee that they divided the earth into three portions, for Shem and Ham and Japheth, each by his inheritance, in the first year of the first week, when one of us who had been sent was with them.

11He called his sons, and they came near to him, they and their children, and he divided the earth into the lots that his three sons would take; and they reached out their hands and took the writing from the bosom of Noah their father.

12On the writing came out Shem's lot: the middle of the earth, which he would take as an inheritance for himself and his sons for the eternal generations, from the middle of the mountain range of Rafa, from the mouth of the water of the river Tina. His portion goes toward the west through the middle of this river, and it goes as far as the water of the deeps out of which this river comes and pours its waters into the sea of Meat, and this river flows into the great sea. All that is toward the north is Japheth's, and all that is toward the south belongs to Shem.

13It goes as far as Karaso: this is in the bosom of the tongue that looks toward the south.

14His portion goes along the great sea, and it goes straight until it comes to the west of the tongue that looks toward the south; for this sea is named the tongue of the land of Egypt.

15From there it turns toward the south, toward the mouth of the great sea, on the shore of its waters, and it goes toward the west to Afra, and it goes until it reaches the waters of the river Gihon, and to the south of the waters of the Gihon, to the banks of this river.

16It goes toward the east until it comes to the garden of Eden, on its southern side — to the south and the east of the whole land of Eden and of the whole east — and it turns to the east and goes until it reaches the east of the mountain named Rafa, and goes down to the bank of the mouth of the river Tina.

17This portion came out by lot for Shem and his sons, for them to hold forever, for his generations forever.

18Noah rejoiced that this portion came out for Shem and his sons, and he remembered all that he had spoken with his mouth in prophecy, for he had said, "Blessed be the Lord, the God of Shem, and may the Lord dwell in the dwelling of Shem".

19He knew that the garden of Eden is the holy of holies and the dwelling of the Lord, and Mount Sinai the center of the wilderness, and Mount Zion the center of the navel of the earth: these three were created as holy places facing each other.

20He blessed the God of gods, who had put the word of the Lord in his mouth, and the Lord forever.

21He knew that a portion of blessing, a blessed one, had come to Shem and his sons for the eternal generations: the whole land of Eden, and the whole land of the Red Sea, and the whole land of the east, and India, and on the Red Sea and its mountains, and all the land of Bashan, and all the land of Lebanon, and the islands of Caphtor, and Senir and Amana, and the mountain of Asshur in the north, and all the land of Elam, Asshur and Babel, and Susa and Madai, and all the land of Ararat, and all the region beyond the sea, beyond the mountain of Asshur toward the north: a blessed and spacious land, and all that is in it is very good.

22For Ham the second portion came out, beyond the Gihon, toward the south, to the right of the garden, and it goes toward the south, and it goes along all the mountains of fire, and it goes toward the west to the sea of Atel, and it goes toward the west until it reaches the sea of Mauk, the sea into which everything that perishes goes down.

23It goes toward the north to the edge of Gadir, and it comes to the shore of the waters of the sea, to the waters of the great sea, until it comes near the river Gihon; and it goes along the river Gihon until it comes to the right of the garden of Eden.

24This is the land that came out for Ham as the portion he would hold forever, for himself and his sons, for their generations forever.

25For Japheth the third portion came out, beyond the river Tina, to the north of the outflow of its waters, and it goes to the northeast, across the whole region of Gog and all the country east of them.

26It goes north, to the far north, and it goes toward the mountains of Qelt, toward the north, and toward the sea of Mauk, and it comes to the east of Gadir, as far as the region of the waters of the sea.

27It goes until it comes near the west of Fara, and it turns toward Aferag, and it goes east to the waters of the sea of Meat.

28It goes toward the region of the river Tina, to the northeast, until it comes near the edge of its waters toward the mountain Rafa, and it turns around toward the north.

29This is the land that came out for Japheth and his sons as the portion of his inheritance, which he would hold for himself and his sons for their generations forever: five great islands, and a great land in the north.

30But it is cold, and the land of Ham is hot, and the land of Shem is neither hot nor cold, for it is a mixture of cold and heat.

Notes

  • vv6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, 22, 27, 29 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). In v6 the EOTC has only In the fourth year he was born; the Asmara printing names the son there, Shelah. The Greek, a list of wives, agrees with vv5–7: Melcha, the daughter of Madai, the son of Japheth; Moacha, the daughter of Keedam; Azurah, the daughter of Nimrod.

  • North and south in this chapter — the Ge'ez words are samen and dabub, which Charles renders south and north. The chapter bears him out: Japheth's land, on the dabub side (vv25–28), is the cold one, and Ham's, on the samen side (v22), is the hot one (v30). The English follows the chapter.

  • vv1–4 "Kainam" — a son of Arpachshad whom the Hebrew of Genesis 11:12 does not have: there Arpachshad fathers Shelah. The Greek of Genesis 11:12–13 has him, Arpachshad lived a hundred and thirty-five years, and fathered Kainan, and so does Luke's genealogy of Jesus: the son of Kainam, the son of Arpachshad, the son of Shem (Luke 3:36). The teaching he copies from the rock is what the Watchers taught in 1 Enoch 8:3: astrology… the signs of the stars… the omens of the sun.

  • v8 "Peleg" — Genesis 10:25: the name of the one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided. v9 "They divided it wrongly" — ba-ʾəkuy, in evil; Charles has secretly.

  • v19 "Mount Zion the center of the navel of the earth" — Ezekiel speaks of the people who dwell at the navel of the earth (Ezekiel 38:12), and says of Jerusalem, I have set her in the middle of the nations (Ezekiel 5:5). Eden, Sinai and Zion are three of the Lord's four places named at 4:26.

  • v20 "the God of gods" — the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords (Deuteronomy 10:17).

  • v21 "the Red Sea" — baḥra ʾErtrā, the sea of Eritrea, from the Greek name for it, the Erythraean (red) sea. India is ʾƎndake.

  • v22 "everything that perishes goes down" — za-yətḫaggwal, that perishes; Charles, from other manuscripts, has everything which is not destroyed.

  • v30 "neither hot nor cold" — Shem's land is the middle land in climate as in place.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Grandsons' Portions
chapters.html:
Jubilees 9

1Ham divided among his sons, and the first portion came out for Cush, toward the east, and to the west of him for Egypt, and to the west of him for Put, and to the west of him, and to the west of that, on the sea, for Canaan.

2Shem too divided among his sons, and the first portion came out for Elam and his sons, to the east of the river Tigris until it comes near the east: the whole land of India, and on the Red Sea, on its shore, and the waters of Dedan, and all the mountains of Mebri and Ela, and all the land of Susan, and all that is on the side of Pharnak, to the Red Sea and to the river Tina.

3For Asshur the second portion came out: all the land of Asshur and Nineveh and Shinar and Sek, to the border of India, and it goes up and runs along the river.

4For Arpachshad the third portion came out: all the land of the region of the Chaldeans, to the east of the Euphrates, near the Red Sea, and all the waters of the wilderness, near the tongue of the sea that looks toward Egypt; all the land of Lebanon and Senir and Amana, to the border of the Euphrates.

5For Aram the fourth portion came out: all the land of Mesopotamia, between the Tigris and the Euphrates, to the north of the Chaldeans, to the border of the mountains of Asshur and the land of Arara.

6For Lud the fifth portion came out: the mountain of Asshur and all that belongs to it, until it reaches the great sea and reaches the east of Asshur his brother.

7Japheth too divided the land among his sons for an inheritance.

8The first portion came out for Gomer, to the east, from the north side, to the river Tina; and in the north there came out for Magog all the inner parts of the north, until it reaches the sea of Meat.

9For Madai a portion came out, for him to hold, from the west of his two brothers to the islands and to the coasts of the islands.

10For Javan the fourth portion came out: every island, and the islands toward the border of Lud.

11For Tubal the fifth portion came out: in the middle of the tongue that comes near the border of Lud's portion, to the second tongue, and beyond the second tongue to the third tongue.

12For Meshech the sixth portion came out: all the region beyond the third tongue, until it comes near the east of Gadir.

13For Tiras the seventh portion came out: four great islands in the middle of the sea, which come near the portion of Ham; and the islands of Kamaturi came out by lot for the sons of Arpachshad as his inheritance.

14In this way the sons of Noah divided the land among their sons in the presence of Noah their father, and he bound them all by an oath, calling down a curse on anyone who tried to seize a portion that had not fallen to him by his lot.

15They all said, "So be it, so be it," for themselves and their sons forever, through their generations, until the day of judgment, on which the Lord God will judge them with the sword and with fire for all the unclean wickedness of their errors, with which they have filled the earth with guilt and uncleanness and fornication and sin.

Notes

  • vv1, 8, 13, 14 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). Without the end of v8, which the EOTC lacks, Magog, the second son of Japheth in Genesis 10:2, would get no land at all; the portions are numbered, and Madai's (v9) is the third.

  • The sons — the names are those of the table of nations: The sons of Ham: Cush and Egypt and Put and Canaan (Genesis 10:6); The sons of Shem: Elam and Asshur and Arpachshad and Lud and Aram (10:22); The sons of Japheth: Gomer and Magog and Madai and Javan and Tubal and Meshech and Tiras (10:2). Jubilees gives each his land. Canaan's lies in the far west, on the sea; in the next chapter he refuses it and settles in the land of Lebanon, which fell to Shem (10:29–33).

  • v2 "for Elam" — so the Ge'ez. Charles's English has for Ham here, a slip: Elam is Shem's firstborn in Genesis 10:22.

  • v5 "to the north of the Chaldeans" — dabub, rendered as in chapter 8 (see the note there on north and south).

  • vv14–15 "So be it, so be it" — the oath and the curse bind the division, as the people answer Amen to the curses of Deuteronomy 27. It is this oath that Canaan breaks in the next chapter.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Mastema's Tenth and the Tower
chapters.html:
Jubilees 10

1In the third week of this jubilee the unclean demons began to lead astray the children of Noah's sons, and to make them foolish and destroy them.

2Noah's sons came to Noah their father and told him about the demons who were leading astray and blinding and killing his sons' sons.

3He prayed before the Lord his God and said, "God of the spirits that are in all flesh, You who have shown me mercy and saved me and my sons from the waters of the flood, and did not make me perish as You did the children of destruction — for great has been Your grace toward me, and great Your mercy on my soul: let Your grace be lifted up over my sons, and do not let wicked spirits rule over them, or they will destroy them from the earth.

4Bless me and my children, so that we may grow and multiply and fill the earth.

5You know what Your Watchers, the fathers of these spirits, did in my days; and as for these spirits that are alive, imprison them and hold them fast in the place of condemnation, and do not let them bring destruction on the sons of Your servant, my God, for they are cruel and were created to destroy.

6Do not let them rule over the spirits of the living, for You alone know their judgment; and let them have no power over the children of the righteous from now on and forever."

7Our God told us to bind them all.

8The chief of the spirits, Mastema, came and said, "Lord, Creator, leave some of them before me, and let them listen to my voice and do all that I tell them. For if some of them are not left to me, I will not be able to exercise the authority of my will among the sons of men; for these are for corruption and for leading astray before my judgment, for great is the wickedness of the sons of men."

9He said, "Let a tenth of them remain before him, and let him send nine parts down into the place of condemnation."

10He told one of us that we should teach Noah all their healings, for He knew that they would not walk in uprightness or strive in righteousness.

11We did all that He said: all the evil ones who are cruel we bound in the place of condemnation, and a tenth of them we left to be subject before Satan on the earth.

12We told Noah all the healing of their diseases, together with their ways of leading astray, so that he could heal with the plants of the earth.

13Noah wrote down in a book everything we taught him, every kind of healing, and the evil spirits were shut out from following the sons of Noah.

14He gave all the books he had written to Shem, his eldest son, for he loved him most of all his sons.

15Noah slept with his fathers and was buried on Mount Lubar in the land of Ararat.

16He completed nine hundred and fifty years in his life: nineteen jubilees and two weeks and five years.

17In his life on the earth he surpassed the sons of men, because of his righteousness, in which he was perfect — all except Enoch; for Enoch's office was ordained as a testimony to the generations of the world, so that he should tell all the deeds of generation after generation until the day of judgment.

18In the thirty-third jubilee, in the first year of this second week, Peleg took a wife named Lomna, the daughter of Sinaor, and she bore him a son in the fourth year of this week, and he called his name Reu; for he said, "The sons of men have become evil through the counsel to build themselves a city and a tower in the land of Shinar."

19For they had moved from the land of Ararat eastward to Shinar, and in his days they built the city and the tower, saying, "Let us go up by it into heaven."

20They began to build, and in the fourth week they baked bricks with fire, and the bricks served them as stone; and the clay with which they plastered them was asphalt, which comes out of the sea and out of the springs of water in the land of Shinar.

21They built it for forty-three years, with whole bricks, thirteen within it, and a third of one for its height; its height rose to five thousand four hundred and thirty-three cubits.

22The Lord our God said to us, "They are one people, and they have begun to act, and now nothing will be held back from them. Come, let us go down and confuse their language, so that they do not understand one another's speech, and they are scattered into cities and nations, and one purpose will no longer remain with them until the day of judgment."

23The Lord came down, and we came down with Him, to see the city and the tower that the sons of men had built.

24He confused every sound of their languages, and no one understood the speech of another any longer, and they stopped building the city and the tower.

25For this reason the whole land of Shinar is called Babel, because there God confused all the languages of the sons of men, and from there they were scattered into their cities, each by his language and his nation.

26The Lord sent a great wind against their tower and threw it down to the earth; and here it is, between Asshur and Babylon in the land of Shinar, and He called its name "Overthrow."

27In the fourth week, in the first year, at its beginning, in the thirty-fourth jubilee, they were scattered from the land of Shinar.

28Ham and his sons went into the land he was to hold, which he had received as his portion, in the land of the south.

29Canaan saw the land of Lebanon, as far as the river of Egypt, that it was very good, and he did not go into the land of his inheritance, to the west, to the sea; and he lived in the land of Lebanon, east and west, from the border of the Jordan and from the border of the sea.

30Ham his father and Cush and Egypt his brothers said to him, "You have settled in a land that is not yours and did not come out for us by lot. Do not do this; for if you do, you and your sons will fall in the land and be cursed through rebellion. By rebellion you have settled, and by rebellion your children will fall, and you will be uprooted forever.

31Do not live in the dwelling of Shem, for it came to Shem and to his sons by their lot.

32Cursed are you, and cursed you will be above all the sons of Noah, by the curse to which we bound ourselves with an oath before the holy Judge and before Noah our father."

33He did not listen to them, and he lived in the land of Lebanon, from Hamath to the entrance of Egypt, he and his sons, to this day.

34For this reason that land is called the land of Canaan.

35Japheth and his sons went toward the sea and lived in the land of their portion. Madai saw the land of the sea, and it did not please him, and he begged a portion from Elam and Asshur and Arpachshad, his wife's brother, and he has lived in the land of Media, near his wife's brother, to this day.

36He called his dwelling and the dwelling of his sons Media, after the name of their father Madai.

Notes

  • vv3, 5, 8, 16, 17, 22, 25, 26, 29, 30, 31 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). In v16 the EOTC stops at two weeks; the Asmara printing's five years complete the sum: nineteen jubilees and two weeks are 945 years, and the five years bring them to the 950 of v16 and of Genesis 9:29, All the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years.

  • v3 "God of the spirits that are in all flesh" — Moses and Aaron's cry in the wilderness: God, the God of the spirits of all flesh (Numbers 16:22). Noah asks the God of spirits to deal with spirits.

  • vv5–11 "Your Watchers, the fathers of these spirits… a tenth of them we left" — the demons are the spirits of the Watchers' dead sons, as in 1 Enoch 15:9: Evil spirits came out from their bodies. Nine tenths are bound; one tenth is left to Mastema, who is also called Satan (v11). The Greek has the same division: a tenth of them was given to him… so as to tempt humankind… while the remaining nine parts were cast into the abyss. "The chief of the spirits" — malʾaka manāfəst, which Charles renders chief.

  • vv12–14 "healing… with the plants of the earth… He gave all the books he had written to Shem" — the book of healing is Noah's gift against the demons. The lore passes down through Shem, as Enoch's did through Methuselah (7:38).

  • v18 "Reu" — Genesis 11:18. Jubilees explains the name from the building of Babel, as Peleg's was explained from the division (8:8).

  • vv19–26 the tower — Genesis 11:2–9: Come, let us build for ourselves a city, and a tower with its head in the heavens… The LORD came down to see the city and the tower… Therefore its name was called Babel. In Jubilees the angels come down with Him (v23), and a wind throws the tower down (v26), which Genesis does not tell. The Greek has the same forty-three years of building and the same height.

  • v21 the measures — thirteen within it, and a third of one for its height is all the Ge'ez gives. Charles's text and the Greek have the fuller measure: a breadth of 203 bricks, the height of a brick a third of one, a height of 5,433 cubits and two palms, and walls of thirteen and thirty stadia. The Ge'ez keeps the thirteen and the third, and the height.

  • v28 "in the land of the south" — dabub, which here, with Charles, is south: Ham's is the hot land (8:22–30). In chapter 8 Charles renders the same word north. The Ge'ez directions do not keep one meaning throughout, and the English follows the geography each time.

  • vv29–34 Canaan — Canaan breaks the oath of 9:14–15 and takes Shem's land, from Hamath to the entrance of Egypt. The land bears his name, but by the lot it was Shem's.

  • v35 "Elam and Asshur and Arpachshad" — so the Ge'ez; Charles again has Ham for Elam (as at 9:2). "Media" — the Ge'ez writes Medqin and Mediqin; v36 derives it from Madai.

speech.text: Jubilees 10
In the third week of this jubilee the unclean demons began to lead astray the children of Noah's sons, and to make them foolish and destroy them.
Noah's sons came to Noah their father and told him about the demons who were leading astray and blinding and killing his sons' sons.

He prayed before the Lord his God and said, "God of the spirits that are in all flesh, You who have shown me mercy and saved me and my sons from the waters of the flood, and did not make me perish as You did the children of destruction — for great has been Your grace toward me, and great Your mercy on my soul: let Your grace be lifted up over my sons, and do not let wicked spirits rule over them, or they will destroy them from the earth.
Bless me and my children, so that we may grow and multiply and fill the earth.

You know what Your Watchers, the fathers of these spirits, did in my days; and as for these spirits that are alive, imprison them and hold them fast in the place of condemnation, and do not let them bring destruction on the sons of Your servant, my God, for they are cruel and were created to destroy.
Do not let them rule over the spirits of the living, for You alone know their judgment; and let them have no power over the children of the righteous from now on and forever."
Our God told us to bind them all.

The chief of the spirits, Mastema, came and said, "Lord, Creator, leave some of them before me, and let them listen to my voice and do all that I tell them. For if some of them are not left to me, I will not be able to exercise the authority of my will among the sons of men; for these are for corruption and for leading astray before my judgment, for great is the wickedness of the sons of men."
He said, "Let a tenth of them remain before him, and let him send nine parts down into the place of condemnation."
He told one of us that we should teach Noah all their healings, for He knew that they would not walk in uprightness or strive in righteousness.
We did all that He said: all the evil ones who are cruel we bound in the place of condemnation, and a tenth of them we left to be subject before Satan on the earth.
We told Noah all the healing of their diseases, together with their ways of leading astray, so that he could heal with the plants of the earth.
Noah wrote down in a book everything we taught him, every kind of healing, and the evil spirits were shut out from following the sons of Noah.
He gave all the books he had written to Shem, his eldest son, for he loved him most of all his sons.
Noah slept with his fathers and was buried on Mount Lubar in the land of Ararat.
He completed nine hundred and fifty years in his life: nineteen jubilees and two weeks and five years.

In his life on the earth he surpassed the sons of men, because of his righteousness, in which he was perfect — all except Enoch; for Enoch's office was ordained as a testimony to the generations of the world, so that he should tell all the deeds of generation after generation until the day of judgment.

In the thirty-third jubilee, in the first year of this second week, Peleg took a wife named Lomna, the daughter of Sinaor, and she bore him a son in the fourth year of this week, and he called his name Reu; for he said, "The sons of men have become evil through the counsel to build themselves a city and a tower in the land of Shinar."
For they had moved from the land of Ararat eastward to Shinar, and in his days they built the city and the tower, saying, "Let us go up by it into heaven."

They began to build, and in the fourth week they baked bricks with fire, and the bricks served them as stone; and the clay with which they plastered them was asphalt, which comes out of the sea and out of the springs of water in the land of Shinar.
They built it for forty-three years, with whole bricks, thirteen within it, and a third of one for its height; its height rose to five thousand four hundred and thirty-three cubits.

The Lord our God said to us, "They are one people, and they have begun to act, and now nothing will be held back from them. Come, let us go down and confuse their language, so that they do not understand one another's speech, and they are scattered into cities and nations, and one purpose will no longer remain with them until the day of judgment."
The Lord came down, and we came down with Him, to see the city and the tower that the sons of men had built.
He confused every sound of their languages, and no one understood the speech of another any longer, and they stopped building the city and the tower.

For this reason the whole land of Shinar is called Babel, because there God confused all the languages of the sons of men, and from there they were scattered into their cities, each by his language and his nation.
The Lord sent a great wind against their tower and threw it down to the earth; and here it is, between Asshur and Babylon in the land of Shinar, and He called its name "Overthrow."
In the fourth week, in the first year, at its beginning, in the thirty-fourth jubilee, they were scattered from the land of Shinar.
Ham and his sons went into the land he was to hold, which he had received as his portion, in the land of the south.

Canaan saw the land of Lebanon, as far as the river of Egypt, that it was very good, and he did not go into the land of his inheritance, to the west, to the sea; and he lived in the land of Lebanon, east and west, from the border of the Jordan and from the border of the sea.

Ham his father and Cush and Egypt his brothers said to him, "You have settled in a land that is not yours and did not come out for us by lot. Do not do this; for if you do, you and your sons will fall in the land and be cursed through rebellion. By rebellion you have settled, and by rebellion your children will fall, and you will be uprooted forever.
Do not live in the dwelling of Shem, for it came to Shem and to his sons by their lot.
Cursed are you, and cursed you will be above all the sons of Noah, by the curse to which we bound ourselves with an oath before the holy Judge and before Noah our father."
He did not listen to them, and he lived in the land of Lebanon, from Hamath to the entrance of Egypt, he and his sons, to this day.
For this reason that land is called the land of Canaan.

Japheth and his sons went toward the sea and lived in the land of their portion. Madai saw the land of the sea, and it did not please him, and he begged a portion from Elam and Asshur and Arpachshad, his wife's brother, and he has lived in the land of Media, near his wife's brother, to this day.
He called his dwelling and the dwelling of his sons Media, after the name of their father Madai.

chapters.title: Abram and the Ravens
chapters.html:
Jubilees 11

1In the thirty-fifth jubilee, in the third week, in its first year, Reu took a wife named Ara, the daughter of Ur, the son of Kesed, and she bore him a son, and he called his name Serug, in the seventh year of this week.

2In this jubilee the sons of Noah began to fight one another, to take captives and to kill each his brother, and to shed the blood of men on the earth, and to eat blood, and to build strong cities and walls and towers, and one man to raise himself over the people, and to found the beginnings of kingdoms, and to go to war, people against people and nation against nation and city against city; and all began to do evil, and to get weapons, and to teach their sons war, and they began to capture cities and to sell male and female slaves.

3Ur the son of Kesed built the city of Ara of the Chaldeans, and named it after his own name and his father's name.

4They made themselves molten images, and each worshiped the idol, the molten image he had made for himself; and they began to make carved images and unclean likenesses, and cruel spirits helped them and led them astray into transgression and uncleanness.

5The prince Mastema worked hard to do all this, and he sent out by the hand of spirits, those who had been put under his hand, to do all error and sin and all transgression, to corrupt and destroy and shed blood on the earth.

6For this reason Serug was called Serug, for everyone turned to do every sin.

7He grew up and lived in Ur of the Chaldeans, near the father of his wife's mother, and he worshiped idols; and he took a wife in the thirty-seventh jubilee, in the fifth week, in its first year, named Melka, the daughter of Kaber, the daughter of his father's sister.

8She bore him Nahor in the first year of this week; and he grew up and lived in Ur, among the people of Ur of the Chaldeans, and his father taught him the researches of the Chaldeans, to practice divination and to read omens by the signs of heaven.

9In the thirty-seventh jubilee, in the sixth week, in its first year, he took a wife named Iyaska, the daughter of Nestag of the Chaldeans.

10She bore him Terah in the seventh year of this week.

11The prince Mastema sent ravens and birds to eat the seed sown in the land, and to ruin the land, and to rob the sons of men of their labors. Before they could plow in the seed, the ravens picked it from the surface of the ground.

12For this reason he called his name Terah, because the ravens and the birds brought them to poverty and ate their seed.

13The years began to be barren because of the birds, and they ate all the fruit of the trees from the trees; only with great effort could they save a little of all the fruit of the earth in their days.

14In this thirty-ninth jubilee, in the second week, in the first year, Terah took a wife named Edna, the daughter of Abram, the daughter of his father's sister.

15In the seventh year of this week she bore him a son, and he called his name Abram, after the name of his mother's father, for he had died before his daughter conceived a son.

16The child began to understand the errors of the earth, that all were going astray after carved images and after uncleanness; and his father taught him writing, and when he was two weeks of years old he separated himself from his father, so as not to worship idols with him.

17He began to pray to the Creator of all, that He would save him from the errors of the sons of men, and that his portion would not fall into error after uncleanness and shame.

18The time came to sow seed in the land; and they all went out together to protect their seed from the ravens, and Abram went out with those who went, and the child was a boy of fourteen years.

19A cloud of ravens came to eat the seed, and Abram ran to meet them before they settled on the ground, and cried out to them before they settled on the ground to eat the seed, and said, "Do not come down. Go back to the place you came from." They turned back.

20That day he turned back the clouds of ravens seventy times, and of all the ravens, in all the fields where Abram was, not one settled there.

21All who were with him in all the fields saw him cry out, and all the ravens turn back; and his name became great in all the land of the Chaldeans.

22That year all who were sowing came to him, and he went with them until the time of sowing was over, and they sowed their land; and that year they brought home enough grain, and ate and were satisfied.

23In the first year of the fifth week Abram taught those who made tools for oxen, the workers in wood, and they made a vessel above the ground, facing the frame of the plow, to put the seed on it; the seed fell down from it onto the share of the plow and was hidden in the earth, and they no longer feared the ravens.

24They did this on every plow frame above the ground, and they sowed and worked all the land as Abram commanded them, and they no longer feared the birds.

Notes

  • Verse numbers — the EOTC divides this chapter into 24 verses; other editions have 23. From v4 on its numbers run one ahead of Charles's.

  • vv2, 4, 7, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 21, 22 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). The Greek agrees where it overlaps: the wars and kingdoms (v2), Melcha, daughter of Chaber (v7), and Abram's name, whom his mother named after her own father; for he had already died before his birth (v15). Without the ends of vv14–15, the EOTC text here never names Abram's mother, and never gives the child's name at all.

  • vv14–15 "Edna, the daughter of Abram, the daughter of his father's sister" — so Charles; the Greek has daughter of Abraham, his father's brother. Abram is named after his mother's father.

  • v7 "in the thirty-seventh jubilee" — so the Asmara printing, ṣalāsā wa-sabuʿu; Charles has the thirty-sixth. With Nahor born in the first year of that week (v8), the thirty-seventh makes him thirteen when Terah is born in 1806 (v10); the thirty-sixth would make him sixty-two. The EOTC text as held here lacks the date. The text is left as it stands.

  • vv10, 15 the dates — Terah is born in the thirty-seventh jubilee, sixth week, seventh year: 36 × 49 + 5 × 7 + 7 = 1806. Abram is born in the thirty-ninth jubilee, second week, seventh year: 38 × 49 + 7 + 7 = 1876. Terah is seventy, as in Genesis: Terah lived seventy years, and he fathered Abram (Genesis 11:26).

  • vv2–5 "one man to raise himself over the people… molten images… the prince Mastema" — Genesis 10–11 says nothing of idols before Abram. Jubilees sets them in Ur, among Abram's own fathers, with Mastema's spirits behind them. Joshua says the same of Terah: Your fathers lived beyond the River from of old, Terah the father of Abraham and the father of Nahor, and they served other gods (Joshua 24:2).

  • vv11–24 the ravens — Mastema's birds eat the seed; the fourteen-year-old Abram turns them back seventy times in a day, and then teaches the carpenters to fit a seed box to the plow, so that the seed goes straight into the furrow. Before God calls him, Abram is already the one who prays to the Creator (v17) and feeds his neighbors.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Abram Burns the Idols
chapters.html:
Jubilees 12

1And it came to pass in the sixth week, in its seventh year, that Abram said to Terah his father, "Father!" He said, "Here I am, my son."

2He said, "What help or profit do we have from these idols that you serve and bow down before?

3For there is no spirit in them at all; they are dumb forms and an error of the heart. Do not serve them.

4Serve the God of heaven, who sends down the rain and the dew on the earth, and does everything on the earth, and created everything by His word, and all life is from before His face.

5Why do you serve things that have no spirit in them? They are the work of hands, and you carry them on your shoulders, and you have no help from them, only great shame for those who make them and an error of the heart for those who serve them. Do not serve them."

6His father said to him, "I know it too, my son, but what shall I do with the people who have made me serve before them?

7If I tell them the truth, they will kill me, for their soul clings to them, to serve them and praise them. Keep silent, my son, or they will kill you."

8He told these words to his two brothers, and they were angry with him, and he kept silent.

9In the fortieth jubilee, in the second week, in its seventh year, Abram took a wife named Sarai, the daughter of his father, and she became his wife.

10Haran his brother took a wife in the third year of the third week, and she bore him a son in the seventh year of this week, and he called his name Lot.

11Nahor his brother also took a wife.

12In the sixtieth year of Abram's life, that is, the fourth week, in its fourth year, Abram rose by night and burned the house of the idols, and he burned all that was in the house, and no one knew it.

13They rose in the night and tried to save their gods from the middle of the fire.

14Haran rushed to save them, and the fire flared over him, and he was burned in the fire and died in Ur of the Chaldeans before Terah his father, and they buried him in Ur of the Chaldeans.

15Terah went out from Ur of the Chaldeans, he and his sons, to go into the land of Lebanon and into the land of Canaan, and he lived in Harran; and Abram lived with Terah his father in Harran two weeks of years.

16In the sixth week, in its fifth year, Abram sat up through the night, on the new moon of the seventh month, to watch the stars from evening to morning, to see what the year would be like for rain; and he sat alone and watched.

17A word came into his heart, and he said, "All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and of the sun, are all in the hand of the Lord. Why do I search them out?

18If He wishes, He sends rain morning and evening; and if He wishes, He does not send it down. Everything is in His hand."

19He prayed that night and said, "My God, my God, God Most High, You alone are my God. You created everything, and all that is and has been is the work of Your hands, and You and Your rule I have chosen.

20Save me from the hands of evil spirits who rule over the thoughts of men's hearts, and do not let them lead me astray from You, my God; and establish me and my seed forever, so that we do not go astray from now on and forever."

21He said, "Shall I return to Ur of the Chaldeans, who seek my face so that I will return to them, or shall I stay here in this place? The right path before You — prosper it in the hand of Your servant, so that he may walk it, and let me not walk in the error of my heart, my God."

22When he had finished speaking and praying, the word of the Lord was sent to him through me, saying, "Go out from your land, and from your kindred, and from your father's house, to a land that I will show you, and I will make you a great and numerous nation.

23I will bless you and make your name great, and you will be blessed on the earth; and in you all the nations of the earth will be blessed, and I will bless those who bless you, and curse those who curse you.

24I will be God to you, and to your son, and to your son's son, and to all your seed. Do not fear. From now on and to all the generations of the earth, I am your God."

25The Lord God said to me, "Open his mouth and his ears, so that he may hear and speak with his tongue in the language that is revealed"; for it had ceased from the mouths of all the sons of men from the day of the overthrow.

26I opened his mouth and his ears and his lips, and I began to speak with him in Hebrew, in the language of creation.

27He took the books of his fathers, which were written in Hebrew, and copied them, and from then on he began to study them, and I made known to him everything he could not understand; and he studied them during the six rainy months.

28In the seventh year of the sixth week he spoke with his father and told him that he would leave Harran to go to the land of Canaan, to see it, and then return to him.

29Terah his father said to him, "Go in peace. May the eternal God make your path straight, and may the Lord be with you and protect you from all evil, and give you grace, mercy and favor before those who see you, and may none of the sons of men have power over you to harm you. Go in peace.

30If you see a land pleasant to your eyes to live in, come and take me to you; and take Lot with you, the son of Haran your brother, as your own son. The Lord be with you.

31Leave Nahor your brother with me until you return in peace, and then we will all go with you together."

Notes

  • vv4, 7, 12, 15, 17, 20, 22, 23, 27, 29 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). Two of them carry the story. In v12 the EOTC gives the date and stops; the burning of the idols is in the Asmara printing, and the Greek has it too: when Abraham was sixty-one years old, Abraham set fire to the idols of his father. In v22 the EOTC says only when he had finished speaking and praying; the call itself, Genesis 12:1–2, is in the Asmara printing.

  • vv2–5 "they are dumb forms… you carry them on your shoulders" — the prophets' mockery of idols: They lift it on the shoulder, they carry it, and set it in its place, and it stands there; from its place it will not move (Isaiah 46:7).

  • v9 "Sarai, the daughter of his father" — so Abraham says of her in Genesis: she is my sister — the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother — and she became my wife (Genesis 20:12). The Greek makes her the daughter of Harran, sister of Melcha and of Lot.

  • vv12–14 "Haran… died in Ur of the Chaldeans before Terah his father" — Genesis 11:28 gives the death and the place, Haran died before the face of Terah his father… in Ur of the Chaldeans, but not the cause. Jubilees gives the cause: Haran died in the fire trying to save the idols Abram had set alight. The sixtieth year of Abram is the fourth year of the fourth week of the fortieth jubilee: 39 × 49 + 3 × 7 + 4 = 1936, sixty years after his birth in 1876 (11:15).

  • v15 "Harran" — the town, spelled apart from Haran, Abram's brother, as in this project's Genesis.

  • vv16–18 "All the signs of the stars… are all in the hand of the Lord" — the watcher of the stars gives up reading them for rain and turns to the one who sends it; the Chaldean lore his fathers were taught (11:8) is set aside.

  • vv22–24 "I will make you a great and numerous nation… I will be God to you" — Genesis 12:1–3: Go, for yourself, from your land, and from your kindred, and from your father's house… In you all the families of the ground shall be blessed. In Jubilees the word comes through me, the angel of the presence.

  • vv25–27 "I began to speak with him in Hebrew, in the language of creation" — the language lost at Babel (10:24) is given back to Abram, and with it the old books of his fathers. The Greek quotes the same line: I taught Abraham the Hebrew language according to that from the beginning of creation.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.
