And it came to pass in the sixth week, in its seventh year, that Abram said to Terah his father, "Father!" He said, "Here I am, my son."
He said, "What help or profit do we have from these idols that you serve and bow down before?
For there is no spirit in them at all; they are dumb forms and an error of the heart. Do not serve them.
Serve the God of heaven, who sends down the rain and the dew on the earth, and does everything on the earth, and created everything by His word, and all life is from before His face.

Why do you serve things that have no spirit in them? They are the work of hands, and you carry them on your shoulders, and you have no help from them, only great shame for those who make them and an error of the heart for those who serve them. Do not serve them."
His father said to him, "I know it too, my son, but what shall I do with the people who have made me serve before them?
If I tell them the truth, they will kill me, for their soul clings to them, to serve them and praise them. Keep silent, my son, or they will kill you."
He told these words to his two brothers, and they were angry with him, and he kept silent.
In the fortieth jubilee, in the second week, in its seventh year, Abram took a wife named Sarai, the daughter of his father, and she became his wife.
Haran his brother took a wife in the third year of the third week, and she bore him a son in the seventh year of this week, and he called his name Lot.
Nahor his brother also took a wife.
In the sixtieth year of Abram's life, that is, the fourth week, in its fourth year, Abram rose by night and burned the house of the idols, and he burned all that was in the house, and no one knew it.
They rose in the night and tried to save their gods from the middle of the fire.
Haran rushed to save them, and the fire flared over him, and he was burned in the fire and died in Ur of the Chaldeans before Terah his father, and they buried him in Ur of the Chaldeans.

Terah went out from Ur of the Chaldeans, he and his sons, to go into the land of Lebanon and into the land of Canaan, and he lived in Harran; and Abram lived with Terah his father in Harran two weeks of years.

In the sixth week, in its fifth year, Abram sat up through the night, on the new moon of the seventh month, to watch the stars from evening to morning, to see what the year would be like for rain; and he sat alone and watched.
A word came into his heart, and he said, "All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and of the sun, are all in the hand of the Lord. Why do I search them out?
If He wishes, He sends rain morning and evening; and if He wishes, He does not send it down. Everything is in His hand."

He prayed that night and said, "My God, my God, God Most High, You alone are my God. You created everything, and all that is and has been is the work of Your hands, and You and Your rule I have chosen.

Save me from the hands of evil spirits who rule over the thoughts of men's hearts, and do not let them lead me astray from You, my God; and establish me and my seed forever, so that we do not go astray from now on and forever."

He said, "Shall I return to Ur of the Chaldeans, who seek my face so that I will return to them, or shall I stay here in this place? The right path before You — prosper it in the hand of Your servant, so that he may walk it, and let me not walk in the error of my heart, my God."

When he had finished speaking and praying, the word of the Lord was sent to him through me, saying, "Go out from your land, and from your kindred, and from your father's house, to a land that I will show you, and I will make you a great and numerous nation.

I will bless you and make your name great, and you will be blessed on the earth; and in you all the nations of the earth will be blessed, and I will bless those who bless you, and curse those who curse you.
I will be God to you, and to your son, and to your son's son, and to all your seed. Do not fear. From now on and to all the generations of the earth, I am your God."

The Lord God said to me, "Open his mouth and his ears, so that he may hear and speak with his tongue in the language that is revealed"; for it had ceased from the mouths of all the sons of men from the day of the overthrow.
I opened his mouth and his ears and his lips, and I began to speak with him in Hebrew, in the language of creation.

He took the books of his fathers, which were written in Hebrew, and copied them, and from then on he began to study them, and I made known to him everything he could not understand; and he studied them during the six rainy months.
In the seventh year of the sixth week he spoke with his father and told him that he would leave Harran to go to the land of Canaan, to see it, and then return to him.

Terah his father said to him, "Go in peace. May the eternal God make your path straight, and may the Lord be with you and protect you from all evil, and give you grace, mercy and favor before those who see you, and may none of the sons of men have power over you to harm you. Go in peace.
If you see a land pleasant to your eyes to live in, come and take me to you; and take Lot with you, the son of Haran your brother, as your own son. The Lord be with you.
Leave Nahor your brother with me until you return in peace, and then we will all go with you together."

chapters.title: Abram in Canaan and Egypt
chapters.html:
Jubilees 13

1Abram went from Harran, and he took Sarai his wife, and Lot, his brother Haran's son, to the land of Canaan; and he came into Asshur and went on to Shechem, and lived near a tall oak.

2He looked, and the land was very pleasant, from the entrance of Hamath to the tall oak.

3The Lord said to him, "To you and to your seed I will give this land."

4He built an altar there, and offered on it a burnt offering to the Lord who had appeared to him.

5He moved from there to the mountain of Bethel, toward the sea, with Ai toward the east, and pitched his tent there.

6He looked, and the land was wide and very good, and everything grew on it: vines and figs and pomegranates, oaks and holm oaks, and terebinths and olive trees, and cedars and cypresses and frankincense trees, and all the trees of the field, and there was water on the mountains.

7He blessed the Lord who had brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and brought him to this mountain.

8And it came to pass in the first year, in the seventh week, on the new moon of the first month, that he built an altar on this mountain and called on the name of the Lord: "You are my God, the eternal God."

9He offered on the altar a burnt offering to the Lord, that He would be with him and not forsake him all the days of his life.

10He moved from there and went toward the south and came to Hebron, and Hebron was built at that time, and he lived there two years; and he went into the land of the south as far as Bealoth, and a famine arose over the land.

11Abram went into Egypt in the third year of the week, and he lived in Egypt five years before his wife was taken from him.

12Tanis in Egypt was built at that time, seven years after Hebron.

13And it came to pass, when Pharaoh took Sarai, Abram's wife, that the Lord struck Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram's wife.

14Abram was very rich in possessions: in sheep and cattle and donkeys and horses and camels and male and female servants, and in silver and gold, very much; and Lot, his brother's son, also had riches.

15Pharaoh gave back Sarai, Abram's wife, and sent him out of the land of Egypt; and he went to the place where he had pitched his tent at first, to the place of the altar, with Ai to the east and Bethel to the west; and he blessed the Lord his God, who had brought him back in peace.

16And it came to pass in this forty-first jubilee, in the third year of the first week, that he returned to this place and offered a burnt offering on it, and called on the name of the Lord: "God Most High, my God forever and ever."

17In the fourth year of this week Lot parted from him, and Lot lived in Sodom, and the men of Sodom were very great sinners [and wicked in their hearts].

18It grieved him in his heart that his brother's son had parted from him, for he had no children.

19In that year Lot was taken captive. In the fourth year of this week the Lord said to Abram, after Lot had parted from him, "Lift up your eyes from the place where you are living, to the west and to the south and to the east and to the north.

20For all the land that you see I will give to you and to your seed forever. I will make your seed like the sand of the sea, so that if a man could count the sand of the sea, then your seed also could be counted.

21Arise, walk through its length and its breadth and see it all, for to your seed I will give it." Abram went to Hebron and lived there.

22In this year Chedorlaomer king of Elam came, and Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar, and Tidal king of Goiim, and they killed the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Sodom fled; and many fell wounded in the Valley of Siddim, by the Salt Sea.

23They took captive Sodom and Admah and Zeboiim, and they took captive Lot too, the son of Abram's brother, with all his possessions, and they went as far as Dan.

24One who had escaped came and told Abram that his brother's son had been taken captive.

25He armed the servants born in his house. Abram went and killed Chedorlaomer and came back, and he gave a tenth of everything, and gave it to Melchizedek; … for Abram and for his seed, a tenth of the first fruits to the Lord. The Lord ordained it as an ordinance forever, that they should give it to the priests who serve before Him, for them to possess forever.

26For this law there is no limit of days, for He ordained it for the eternal generations, that they should give to the Lord a tenth of everything: of the seed and of the wine and of the oil and of the cattle and of the sheep.

27He gave it to His priests to eat and drink with joy before Him.

28The king of Sodom came to him and bowed down before him and said, "Our lord Abram, give us the souls you have rescued, and let the spoil be yours."

29Abram said to him, "I lift up my hands to God Most High: from a thread to a sandal strap, I will not take anything that is yours, so that you will not say, 'I made Abram rich' — except only what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me, Aner, Eshcol and Mamre: they shall take their portion."

Notes

  • vv1, 10, 14, 19, 20, 21, 22, 25, 29 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). In v19 the EOTC has only In that year Lot was taken captive; the Lord's promise to Abram, Genesis 13:14–17, is in the Asmara printing and in the Latin, which begins at v10 of this chapter. Words in [brackets] (v17) are in no Ge'ez text here; they follow the Latin.

  • vv1–9 Abram's arrival — Genesis 12:6–8, retold: the tall oak near Shechem, the promise To your seed I will give this land, the altar, and the tent with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east (Genesis 12:8). "frankincense trees" — libanos, the Greek name of the frankincense tree; Charles has date trees.

  • v10 "as far as Bealoth" — the EOTC writes it as two words, bo'a Lot, which could be read Lot came; the Latin has the place name, Bealoth.

  • v12 "Tanis… seven years after Hebron" — the note Numbers makes when the spies reach Hebron: Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt (Numbers 13:22). Zoan is Tanis.

  • vv13–15 Pharaoh and Sarai — Genesis 12:14–20. Jubilees adds the years: Abram had been in Egypt five years before she was taken (v11).

  • vv22–29 the war of the kings — Genesis 14, with the kings as named there: Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim (Genesis 14:1).

  • v25 "Abram went and killed Chedorlaomer… and gave it to Melchizedek" — the two Beta Masaheft Ge'ez texts carry these words after an opening bracket, a mark that sets them apart from what comes before. The Asmara printing has no such words: like Charles's manuscripts it has a gap here, and it breaks off at armed his household servants and picks up mid-sentence with the tithe. Genesis: He gave him a tenth of everything (Genesis 14:20); Hebrews: to whom Abraham apportioned a tenth of everything (Hebrews 7:2). In Jubilees the tithe becomes a law forever, for the priests (vv25–27), as in Leviticus 27:30: Every tenth of the land… is the LORD's.

  • v29 "from a thread to a sandal strap" — Genesis 14:23.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Covenant Between the Pieces
chapters.html:
Jubilees 14

1After these things, in the fourth year of this week, on the new moon of the third month, the word of the Lord came to Abram in a dream, saying, "Do not fear, Abram. I am your defender, and your reward will be very great."

2He said, "Lord, Lord, what will You give me, when I am going childless, and the son of Maseq, my maidservant, the Damascene Eliezer — he will inherit me? To me You have given no seed. Give me seed."

3He said to him, "This one will not inherit you; the one who comes out of your own body, he will inherit you."

4He brought him outside and said to him, "Look toward heaven and count the stars, if you are able to count them."

5He looked at the heavens and saw the stars, and He said to him, "So shall your seed be."

6He trusted the Lord, and it was counted to him as righteousness.

7He said to him, "I am the Lord who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans, to give you the land of the Canaanites to hold forever, and to be God to you and to your seed after you."

8He said, "Lord, Lord, how shall I know that I will inherit it?"

9He said to him, "Take for Me a heifer three years old, and a goat three years old, and a sheep three years old, and a turtledove and a pigeon."

10He took all these in the middle of the month, while he was living at the oak of Mamre, which is near Hebron.

11He built an altar there and slaughtered all these, and poured their blood on the altar, and divided them down the middle and laid each half opposite the other; but the birds he did not divide.

12Birds came down on the pieces, and Abram drove them away and did not let the birds touch them.

13And it came to pass, when the sun had set, that a trance fell on Abram, and a great terror of darkness fell on him. It was said to Abram, "Know for certain that your seed will be strangers in a foreign land, and they will enslave them and afflict them four hundred years.

14The people whom they serve I will judge, and after that they will come out from there with great possessions.

15You will go to your fathers in peace and be buried in a good old age.

16In the fourth generation they will return here, for the sin of the Amorites is not yet complete."

17He woke from sleep and rose, and the sun had set, and there was a flame; a furnace was smoking, and a flame of fire passed between the pieces.

18On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, "To your seed I will give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates: the Kenites and the Kenizzites and the Kadmonites and the Perizzites and the Rephaim and the Phakorites and the Hivites and the Amorites and the Canaanites and the Girgashites and the Jebusites."

19The day passed, and he offered them up: the pieces and the birds, and their grain offerings and their drink offerings, and the fire consumed them.

20That night we made a covenant with Abram, like the covenant we had made in this same month with Noah; and Abram renewed the festival and the ordinance for himself forever.

21Abram rejoiced and told all this to Sarai his wife; and he believed that he would have seed, but she did not bear.

22Sarai advised Abram her husband and said to him, "Go in to Hagar, my Egyptian maid; perhaps I will build up seed for you from her."

23Abram listened to the voice of Sarai his wife and said to her, "Do so." Sarai took Hagar her maid, the Egyptian, and gave her to Abram her husband to be his wife.

24He went in to her, and she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Ishmael, in the fifth year of this week; this was the eighty-sixth year of Abram's life.

Notes

  • v14 — the end of the verse is rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the EOTC text as held here breaks off before it. vv18, 19, 20, 21, 23, 24 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from Charles's edition of the Ge'ez (1895); the Asmara file held here lacks 14:16–16:13. Without the end of v24 the EOTC never names Ishmael.

  • vv1–18 the covenant between the pieces — Genesis 15, retold almost verse for verse: Do not fear, Abram… count the stars, if you are able to count them… So shall your seed be (15:1, 5). Jubilees dates it: the dream on the new moon of the third month (v1), the sacrifice in the middle of the month (v10), the time of the Festival of Weeks, the day of Noah's covenant (6:17). That is why the angel says in v20, like the covenant we had made in this same month with Noah.

  • v6 "He trusted the Lord, and it was counted to him as righteousness" — Genesis 15:6, the verse Paul builds on: Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness (Romans 4:3). James quotes it too (James 2:23).

  • v2 "Give me seed" — the EOTC adds these words to Abram's complaint; Genesis has to me You have given no seed (Genesis 15:3). "the son of Maseq, my maidservant" — Genesis 15:2 has the son of the possession of my house, ben-mesheq; Jubilees reads the word as the name of Eliezer's mother.

  • v13 "a trance fell on Abram, and a great terror of darkness" — Genesis 15:12: a deep sleep fell upon Abram, and a dread, a darkness, a great one. "four hundred years" — Genesis 15:13; Paul reckons the law as coming four hundred and thirty years after the promise (Galatians 3:17).

  • v18 "the Phakorites" — a people Genesis 15:19–21 does not list.

  • vv22–24 Hagar — Genesis 16:1–4, 15–16. "the eighty-sixth year of Abram's life" — Charles's figure, the same as Genesis 16:16, Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael. By the book's own dates the fifth year of this week (the forty-first jubilee, first week) is 1965, and Abram was born in 1876 (11:15), which makes him 89. The figure is left as the Ge'ez gives it.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Charles's edition of the Ge'ez (1895): public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Covenant of Circumcision
chapters.html:
Jubilees 15

1In the fifth year of the fourth week of this jubilee, in the third month, in the middle of the month, Abram kept the festival of the first fruits of the wheat harvest.

2He offered a new offering on the altar, the first fruits of the produce, to the Lord: a heifer and a goat and a sheep on the altar, as a burnt offering to the Lord; and their grain offerings and their drink offerings he offered on the altar with frankincense.

3The Lord appeared to Abram, and the Lord said to Abram, "I am God Almighty. Be pleasing before Me, and be whole.

4I will set My covenant between Me and you, and I will increase you greatly."

5Abram fell on his face, and the Lord spoke with him and said,

6"My ordinance is with you, and I will make you a father of many nations.

7Your name will no longer be called Abram, but from now on and forever your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations.

8I will make you very great, and I will make you into nations, and kings will come out of you.

9I will set My covenant between Me and you, and between your seed after you through their generations, for an eternal ordinance, so that I may be God to you and to your seed after you.

10I will give to you and to your seed after you the land where you have lived as a guest, the land of Canaan, to hold forever, and I will be their God."

11The Lord said to Abraham, "And you — keep My covenant, you and your seed after you. Circumcise every male among you, and circumcise your foreskins, and it will be a sign of My eternal ordinance between Me and you.

12The son you shall circumcise on the eighth day, every male through your generations, one born of the house, and one bought with money from any foreigner, whom you have acquired, who is not of your seed.

13One born of your house must surely be circumcised, and those you have bought with money must be circumcised; and My covenant will be in your flesh for an eternal ordinance.

14The male who is not circumcised, who has not circumcised the flesh of his foreskin on the eighth day — that soul will be cut off from its kindred, for he has broken My covenant."

15The Lord said to Abraham, "Sarai your wife — her name will no longer be called Sarai, for Sarah is her name.

16I will bless her, and I will give you a son from her, and I will bless him, and he will become a people, and kings of nations will come from him."

17Abraham fell on his face and rejoiced, and said in his heart, "Shall a son be born to one who is a hundred years old? Shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear?"

18Abraham said to the Lord, "If only Ishmael might live before You!"

19The Lord said, "Yes; and Sarah also will bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac, and I will raise up My covenant with him, an eternal covenant, and with his seed after him.

20As for Ishmael also, I have heard you. I will bless him and make him great and multiply him exceedingly; he will father twelve princes, and I will make him a great nation.

21But My covenant I will raise up with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this season, in the next year."

22When He had finished speaking with him, the Lord went up from Abraham.

23Abraham did as the Lord had told him: he took Ishmael his son, and all born of his house, and those he had bought with money, every male in his house, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin.

24On that same day Abraham was circumcised; and those born of his house, and the men of his house, and all whom he had bought with money, even from the sons of foreigners, were circumcised with him.

25This law is for all generations forever, and there is no cutting short of the days, and no passing over one day of the eight days; for it is an eternal ordinance, ordained and written on the tablets of heaven.

26Everyone who is born whose flesh is not circumcised by the eighth day is not of the sons of the ordinance that the Lord made with Abraham, for he is of the sons of destruction; and there is no longer any sign on him that he belongs to the Lord, but he is for destruction and for slaughter on the earth, to be rooted out of the earth, for he has broken the covenant of the Lord our God.

27For all the angels of the presence and all the angels of sanctification have been so created from the day of their creation; and before the angels of the presence and the angels of sanctification He sanctified Israel, to be with Him and with His holy angels.

28As for you, command the sons of Israel, and let them keep the sign of this covenant through their generations as an eternal ordinance, and they will not be uprooted from the land.

29For the command has been ordained for the covenant, that they should keep it forever among all the sons of Israel.

30For Ishmael and his sons and his brothers and Esau the Lord did not bring near to Himself, and He did not choose them, though they are of the sons of Abraham, for He knew them; but Israel He chose to be His people.

31He sanctified it and gathered it from among all the sons of men; for there are many nations and many peoples, and all are His, and over all He has set spirits in authority to lead them astray from Him.

32But over Israel He set no one, neither angel nor spirit, for He alone is their ruler, and He will keep them and require them at the hand of His angels and His spirits, and at the hand of [all His powers], so that He may keep them and bless them, and they may be His and He theirs from now on and forever.

33Now I tell you that the sons of Israel will be false to this ordinance, and will not circumcise their sons according to all this law; for they will leave some of the flesh of the circumcision uncut when they circumcise their sons; and all of them, sons of Beliar, will leave their sons uncircumcised, as they were born.

34There will be great wrath from the Lord on the sons of Israel, because they have forsaken His covenant and turned aside from His word, and provoked and blasphemed, since they have not kept the ordinance of this sign; for they have made their members like the nations, so that they may be removed and uprooted from the land. There will be no more pardon or forgiveness for them, that they should be pardoned and forgiven for all the sin of this eternal error.

Notes

  • vv2, 8, 12, 13, 19, 20, 25, 26, 27, 29, 31, 32, 34 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from Charles's edition of the Ge'ez (1895); the Asmara file held here lacks 14:16–16:13. Without the end of v19 the EOTC first names Isaac in v21. v32 [all His powers] — Charles's correction, in none of his manuscripts: three of the four have all His commandments, and the fourth leaves the words out.

  • vv1–2 "the festival of the first fruits of the wheat harvest" — the middle of the third month, the Festival of Weeks (6:17–21), and the same day as the covenant between the pieces (14:10). Exodus 34:22: the Festival of Weeks… the firstfruits of the wheat harvest. The date — the fifth year of the fourth week of the forty-first jubilee is 40 × 49 + 3 × 7 + 5 = 1986; with Abram born in 1876 (11:15), that makes him 110, not the ninety-nine of Genesis 17:1. The text is left as it stands (compare 14:24).

  • vv3–22 the covenant of circumcision — Genesis 17:1–22, retold in order, in this project's wording where the Ge'ez allows. v3 "God Almighty" — the Ge'ez keeps the Hebrew name, ʾAmlāka Saday, El Shaddai; see the note at Genesis 17:1. "Be pleasing before Me" — as the Greek of Genesis 17:1, euarestei enantion emou; the Hebrew has Walk about before Me.

  • vv11–14 "a sign… on the eighth day" — Genesis 17:10–14. Paul calls it the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith Abraham had while uncircumcised (Romans 4:11). "money" — the Ge'ez word is warq, gold; Genesis has silver. Both mean the price paid.

  • v17 "rejoiced" — Genesis 17:17 has he laughed, the laugh that gives Isaac his name. Jubilees has Abraham rejoice.

  • v24 and v10, the EOTC's own brackets — the printed EOTC text sets those born of his house (v24) and I will give to you and to your seed after you (v10) in square brackets. They are rendered here as plain text.

  • v25 "no cutting short of the days" — literally no circumcising of the days: the eighth day may not be trimmed.

  • v27 "have been so created" — Charles's reading: the highest angels were made so from their creation, and Israel is sanctified to be with them.

  • v30 "though they are of the sons of Abraham" — so the Latin; the Ge'ez joins the clause with for, ʾəsma.

  • vv31–32 "over all He has set spirits… over Israel He set no one" — Deuteronomy 32:8–9: When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when He divided the sons of man, He set the boundaries of the peoples… For the LORD's portion is His people; Jacob is the measured lot of His inheritance.

  • v33 "sons of Beliar" — the name of the adversary Paul sets against Christ: What agreement has Christ with Beliar? (2 Corinthians 6:15). "leave some of the flesh… uncut" — the Ge'ez matrəfāna, a remainder: the angel foretells a circumcision done only in part.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. chapters.title: Isaac and the First Festival of Booths
chapters.html:
Jubilees 16

1On the new moon of the fourth month we appeared to Abraham at the oak of Mamre, and we talked with him, and we told him that a son would be given to him by Sarah his wife.

2Sarah laughed, for she heard that we had spoken these words with Abraham; and we rebuked her, and she became afraid and denied that she had laughed at the words.

3We told her the name of her son, as it is ordained and written on the tablets of heaven — Isaac —

4and that when we returned to her at the set time, she would have conceived a son.

5In this month the Lord executed His judgment on Sodom and Gomorrah and Zeboiim and all the region of the Jordan, and He burned them with fire and sulfur and destroyed them to this day, even as I have told you all their works: how they were wicked and very great sinners, and defiled themselves and committed fornication in their flesh, and did what is unclean on the earth.

6In the same way the Lord will execute judgment on the places where they do as the uncleanness of Sodom, like the judgment of Sodom.

7But Lot we saved, for the Lord remembered Abraham, and brought him out from the middle of the overthrow.

8He and his daughters also committed a sin on the earth such as had not been on the earth from the days of Adam until then, for the man lay with his daughter.

9It has been commanded and engraved concerning all his seed on the tablets of heaven, to remove them and root them out, and to execute judgment on them like the judgment of Sodom, and to leave him no seed of man on the earth on the day of judgment.

10In this month Abraham moved from Hebron, and went and lived between Kadesh and Shur, in the mountains of Gerar.

11In the middle of the fifth month he moved from there and lived at the Well of the Oath.

12In the middle of the sixth month the Lord visited Sarah and did for her as He had said.

13She conceived and bore a son in the third month, in the middle of the month, at the time the Lord had told Abraham; on the festival of the first fruits of the harvest Isaac was born.

14Abraham circumcised his son at eight days old; he was the first to be circumcised according to the covenant that is ordained forever.

15In the sixth year of the fourth week we came to Abraham at the Well of the Oath, and we appeared to him, as we had told Sarah that we would return to her, and she would have conceived a son.

16We returned in the seventh month and found Sarah with child before us, and we blessed her and told her all that had been decreed for him: that he would not die until he had fathered six more sons, and would see them before he died; and in Isaac a name and seed would be called for him.

17All the seed of his sons would become nations and be counted with the nations; but from the sons of Isaac one would become a holy seed, and would not be counted among the nations.

18For he would become the portion of the Most High, and all his seed had fallen into the possession of God, to be for the Lord a people treasured above all peoples, and to be a kingdom and a priesthood and a holy people.

19We went on our way, and we told Sarah all that we had told him, and they both rejoiced with very great joy.

20He built an altar there to the Lord, who had delivered him and was making him rejoice in the land where he lived as a guest; and he kept a festival of joy in this month for seven days beside the altar he had built at the Well of the Oath.

21He built booths for himself and for his servants at this festival, and he was the first to keep the Festival of Booths on the earth.

22During these seven days he offered every day, day by day, on the altar a burnt offering to the Lord: two bulls and two rams, seven sheep, one male goat for sin, to make atonement with it for himself and for his seed.

23As a peace offering: seven rams and seven kids, seven sheep and seven male goats, and their grain offerings and their drink offerings; and he burned all their fat on the altar, a chosen offering for a soothing aroma.

24Morning and evening he burned fragrant incense: frankincense and galbanum and stacte, nard and myrrh, spice and costus. All seven of these he offered, crushed and mixed in equal parts, and pure.

25He kept this festival seven days, rejoicing with all his heart and with all his soul, he and all who were in his house; and there was no foreigner with him, nor anyone who was uncircumcised.

26He blessed his Creator, who had created him in his generation, for He had created him for His good pleasure; for he knew and perceived that from him would come the plant of righteousness for the eternal generations, and from him a holy seed, to be like the One who made all things.

27He blessed and rejoiced, and he called the name of this festival the festival of the Lord, a joy acceptable to God Most High.

28We blessed him forever, and all his seed after him through all the generations of the earth, because he kept this festival in its season, according to the testimony of the tablets of heaven.

29For this reason it is ordained on the tablets of heaven concerning Israel that they shall keep the Festival of Booths seven days with joy, in the seventh month, acceptable before the Lord, a law forever through their generations, every year.

30To this there is no limit of days, for it is ordained forever concerning Israel that they should keep it and live in booths, and set wreaths on their heads, and take leafy boughs and willows of the brook.

31Abraham took branches of palm trees and the fruit of splendid trees, and every day he went around the altar with the branches seven times; in the morning he rose early and praised and gave thanks to his God for everything with joy.

Notes

  • vv16, 17, 20, 23 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). vv2, 5 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from Charles's edition of the Ge'ez (1895); the Asmara file held here lacks 14:16–16:13.

  • vv1–4 the visit at Mamre — Genesis 18:10–15: At the appointed time I will return to you, at the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son… Sarah denied it, saying, "I did not laugh" — for she was afraid. In Genesis the three visitors eat with Abraham; in Jubilees they are the angels of the presence, and they name the child from the tablets of heaven.

  • vv5–9 Sodom and Lot — Genesis 19:24–29: The LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah sulfur and fire… God remembered Abraham, and He sent Lot out from the midst of the overturning. v8 "with his daughter" — so the EOTC; Charles and the Latin have daughters. v9 "all his seed" — Lot's seed, Moab and Ammon (Genesis 19:37–38). The Greek sums it up: from Lot came the Moabites and Ammonites, an accursed seed from an unlawful union.

  • vv10–11 "between Kadesh and Shur… the Well of the Oath" — Genesis 20:1, he settled between Kadesh and Shur, and he lived as a guest in Gerar. The Well of the Oath is Beersheba: Therefore that place was called Beersheba, for there the two of them swore (Genesis 21:31).

  • vv12–14 Isaac's birth — Genesis 21:1–4: The LORD attended to Sarah as He had said… Abraham circumcised Isaac his son at eight days old. Jubilees dates it to the festival of first fruits, the Festival of Weeks, the day of the covenants with Noah and Abram (6:17; 14:10; 15:1). v13 "in the third month" — so the Ge'ez and Charles; the Latin has the seventh month.

  • vv15–16 the dates — the sixth year of the fourth week is 40 × 49 + 3 × 7 + 6 = 1987, the year after the covenant of 15:1 (1986), and so the year of Isaac's birth. Yet v16 finds Sarah with child in its seventh month, after a birth in the third. The text is left as it stands.

  • v16 "we blessed her and told her" — so the EOTC; Charles and the Latin have him, Abraham, and v19 says the angels then told Sarah all that we had told him. "six more sons" — the sons of Keturah, Genesis 25:1–2. The Asmara printing reads seven, sabʿata. "in Isaac a name and seed would be called for him" — so the Asmara printing; Genesis 21:12 has through Isaac shall seed be called for you.

  • vv17–18 "a people treasured above all peoples… a kingdom and a priesthood and a holy people" — Exodus 19:5–6: you will be My own treasure out of all the peoples… You will be for Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. Of Abraham's sons only Isaac's line, and of Isaac's sons only one, is kept out of the nations.

  • vv20–31 the first Festival of Booths — Abraham keeps it at the Well of the Oath in the seventh month, before the law is given. Leviticus 23:40–42: you shall take for yourselves the fruit of splendid trees, branches of palm trees, boughs of leafy trees, and willows of the brook… You shall live in booths for seven days. Jubilees adds the wreaths on the head (v30) and the sevenfold circling of the altar (v31); the Greek has the circling with branches of palm trees and olive trees.

  • v24 the seven spices — Exodus 30:34 names four of them for the incense of the tabernacle: stacte and onycha and galbanum… and pure frankincense. Each shall be in equal measure. "stacte" — the Ge'ez māya ləbn; "spice" — sanbalt, which the Latin gives as spica, spikenard.

  • v26 "for he knew" — the Latin takes it as Abraham; Charles has He, God. "the plant of righteousness" — the name 1 Enoch gives the chosen line: the plant of righteousness and uprightness forever (1 Enoch 93:5).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin and Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. Charles's edition of the Ge'ez (1895): public domain. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Hagar Sent Away, and Mastema's Challenge
chapters.html:
Jubilees 17

1In the first year of the fifth week of this jubilee Isaac was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast in the third month, on the day his son Isaac was weaned.

2Ishmael, the son of Hagar the Egyptian, was before the face of Abraham his father, in his place; and Abraham rejoiced and blessed the Lord, because he had seen his sons and had not died without sons.

3He remembered the word He had spoken to him on the day Lot parted from him; and he rejoiced because God had given him seed on the earth to inherit it, and with all his mouth he blessed the One who created all things.

4Sarah saw Ishmael playing and dancing, and Abraham rejoicing with great joy, and she was jealous of Ishmael; and she said to Abraham, "Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not inherit with my son Isaac."

5The word was grievous in Abraham's eyes, because of his maidservant and because of his son, that he should drive them away from him.

6The Lord said to Abraham, "Let it not be grievous in your eyes over the boy and over the slave woman. All that Sarah says to you — listen to her words and do it, for through Isaac shall name and seed be called for you.

7As for the son of this slave woman, I will make him into a great nation, for he is of your seed."

8Abraham rose early in the morning and took bread and a skin of water, and set them on the shoulders of Hagar and the child, and sent her away.

9She went and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba, and the water was finished from the skin, and the child was thirsty and could not go on, and fell down.

10His mother took him and cast him under an olive tree, and went and sat opposite him, about a bowshot away, for she said, "Let me not see the death of my child"; and as she sat she wept.

11An angel of God, one of the holy ones, said to her, "Why are you weeping, Hagar? Rise, lift up the child and hold him in your hand, for the Lord has heard your voice and has seen the child."

12She opened her eyes and saw a well of water, and she went and filled her skin with water and gave her child a drink; and she rose and went toward the wilderness of Paran.

13The child grew and became an archer, and the Lord was with him; and his mother took a wife for him from the daughters of Egypt.

14She bore him a son, and he called his name Nebaioth, for she said, "The Lord was near to me when I called on Him."

15And it came to pass in the seventh week, in its first year, in the first month of this jubilee, on the twelfth of this month, that there were words in heaven about Abraham, that he was faithful in all that He told him, and that he loved the Lord, and that in every affliction he was faithful.

16The prince Mastema came and said before God, "Abraham loves Isaac his son and delights in him above all. Tell him to offer him as a burnt offering on the altar, and You will see whether he does this command, and You will know whether he is faithful in everything in which You test him."

17The Lord knew that Abraham was faithful in every affliction He told him of; for He had tested him with his land and with famine, and had tested him with the wealth of kings, and had tested him again with his wife, when she was taken from him, and with circumcision; and had tested him with Ishmael and Hagar his maidservant, when he sent them away.

18In everything in which He had tested him he was found faithful, and his soul was not impatient, and he was not slow to act, for he was faithful and a lover of the Lord.

Notes

  • vv3, 4, 12, 15, 16, 17 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers vv1–5 of this chapter, has vv3 and 4 too. Without the end of v4 Sarah never asks for Hagar to be sent away, and without the end of v16 Mastema never says what the test should be.

  • vv1–14 Hagar and Ishmael sent away — Genesis 21:8–21, retold in order, in this project's wording where the Ge'ez allows: Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not inherit with my son, with Isaac… through Isaac shall seed be called for you (21:10, 12). v4 "playing and dancing" — so the Ge'ez; the Latin has playing with Isaac; Genesis 21:9 has only laughing, the verb of Isaac's name. In Jubilees it is Abraham's joy in Ishmael that makes Sarah jealous. v10 "under an olive tree" — Genesis 21:15 has under one of the bushes. v11 "an angel of God, one of the holy ones" — Genesis 21:17 has the messenger of God called to Hagar from the heavens.

  • v1 the date — the first year of the fifth week of the forty-first jubilee is 40 × 49 + 4 × 7 + 1 = 1989, two years after Isaac's birth (16:15). The weaning feast falls in the third month, the month of his birth.

  • v13 "his mother took a wife for him" — the EOTC writes for them, lomu; the second Ge'ez text has the same. v14 "Nebaioth" — Ishmael's firstborn in Genesis 25:13. The name is explained from The Lord was near; Genesis gives no reason for it.

  • vv15–18 Mastema's challenge — the scene of Job 1:9–11, where the Satan answers the LORD: Is it for nothing that Job fears God?… stretch out Your hand and touch all that he has. Genesis 22:1 says only God tested Abraham; Jubilees names the accuser. The Greek has it too: Mastipham, the ruler of the demons… approached God and said, "If Abraham loves you, let him sacrifice his son to you." v15 the date — the first year of the seventh week is 40 × 49 + 6 × 7 + 1 = 2003, when Isaac, born in 1987, is sixteen; the Greek puts him at twenty-five.

  • vv17–18 the tests — the land he left (12:28), the famine that drove him to Egypt (13:10–11), Sarai taken by Pharaoh (13:13), circumcision (chapter 15), and Hagar and Ishmael sent away (vv8–12). Charles's English gives these in the same order. "a lover of the Lord" — James: Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness, and he was called friend of God (James 2:23). Hebrews: By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac (Hebrews 11:17).

speech.text: Jubilees 17
In the first year of the fifth week of this jubilee Isaac was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast in the third month, on the day his son Isaac was weaned.
Ishmael, the son of Hagar the Egyptian, was before the face of Abraham his father, in his place; and Abraham rejoiced and blessed the Lord, because he had seen his sons and had not died without sons.

He remembered the word He had spoken to him on the day Lot parted from him; and he rejoiced because God had given him seed on the earth to inherit it, and with all his mouth he blessed the One who created all things.

Sarah saw Ishmael playing and dancing, and Abraham rejoicing with great joy, and she was jealous of Ishmael; and she said to Abraham, "Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not inherit with my son Isaac."
The word was grievous in Abraham's eyes, because of his maidservant and because of his son, that he should drive them away from him.

The Lord said to Abraham, "Let it not be grievous in your eyes over the boy and over the slave woman. All that Sarah says to you — listen to her words and do it, for through Isaac shall name and seed be called for you.
As for the son of this slave woman, I will make him into a great nation, for he is of your seed."
Abraham rose early in the morning and took bread and a skin of water, and set them on the shoulders of Hagar and the child, and sent her away.
She went and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba, and the water was finished from the skin, and the child was thirsty and could not go on, and fell down.
His mother took him and cast him under an olive tree, and went and sat opposite him, about a bowshot away, for she said, "Let me not see the death of my child"; and as she sat she wept.
An angel of God, one of the holy ones, said to her, "Why are you weeping, Hagar? Rise, lift up the child and hold him in your hand, for the Lord has heard your voice and has seen the child."
She opened her eyes and saw a well of water, and she went and filled her skin with water and gave her child a drink; and she rose and went toward the wilderness of Paran.
The child grew and became an archer, and the Lord was with him; and his mother took a wife for him from the daughters of Egypt.
She bore him a son, and he called his name Nebaioth, for she said, "The Lord was near to me when I called on Him."

And it came to pass in the seventh week, in its first year, in the first month of this jubilee, on the twelfth of this month, that there were words in heaven about Abraham, that he was faithful in all that He told him, and that he loved the Lord, and that in every affliction he was faithful.

The prince Mastema came and said before God, "Abraham loves Isaac his son and delights in him above all. Tell him to offer him as a burnt offering on the altar, and You will see whether he does this command, and You will know whether he is faithful in everything in which You test him."

The Lord knew that Abraham was faithful in every affliction He told him of; for He had tested him with his land and with famine, and had tested him with the wealth of kings, and had tested him again with his wife, when she was taken from him, and with circumcision; and had tested him with Ishmael and Hagar his maidservant, when he sent them away.
In everything in which He had tested him he was found faithful, and his soul was not impatient, and he was not slow to act, for he was faithful and a lover of the Lord.

chapters.title: The Binding of Isaac
chapters.html:
Jubilees 18

1The Lord said to him, "Abraham, Abraham!" He said, "Here I am."

2He said to him, "Take your son, your beloved one, whom you love — Isaac — and go to the high land, and bring him up on one of the mountains that I will show you."

3He rose early in the morning and saddled his donkey, and took his two young men with him, and Isaac his son, and split the wood for the offering, and went to the place on the third day; and he saw the place from far off.

4He came to a well of water, and said to his young men, "Stay here with the donkey, and I and the boy will go; and when we have bowed down, we will return to you."

5He took the wood of the offering and set it on Isaac his son, and he took in his hand the fire and the knife; and the two of them went together to that place.

6Isaac said to his father, "Father!" He said, "Here I am, my son." He said to him, "Here is the fire and the knife and the wood — but where is the lamb for the burnt offering, father?"

7He said, "The Lord will see to the lamb for the burnt offering for Himself, my son." He came near to the place of the mountain of God.

8He built an altar and set the wood on the altar, and bound Isaac his son and set him on the wood that was on top of the altar, and stretched out his hand to take the knife to slaughter Isaac his son.

9I stood before him and before the prince Mastema, and the Lord said, "Tell him not to lay his hand on the boy or do anything to him, for I know that he fears the Lord."

10I called to him from heaven and said to him, "Abraham!" He was terrified and said, "Here I am."

11I said to him, "Do not lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him, for now I know that you fear the Lord, and you have not withheld your son, your firstborn, from Me."

12The prince Mastema was put to shame. Abraham lifted up his eyes and looked, and saw a ram caught by its horns; and Abraham went and took the ram and brought it up as a burnt offering in place of his son.

13Abraham called that place "The Lord Has Seen," so that it is said, "The Lord has seen." That is Mount Zion.

14The Lord called Abraham by his name a second time from heaven, as He made us appear to speak to him in the name of the Lord.

15He said, "By Myself I have sworn, says the Lord: because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your son, your firstborn, whom you loved, from Me, blessing, I will bless you, and multiplying, I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven and as the sand that is on the seashore; and your seed will inherit the cities of its enemies.

16In your seed all the nations of the earth will be blessed, because you listened to My voice; and I have shown to all that you are faithful to Me in all that I have said to you. Go in peace."

17Abraham went to his young men, and they rose and went together to Beersheba; and Abraham lived at the Well of the Oath.

18He kept this festival every year, seven days with joy, and he named it the festival of the Lord, after the seven days in which he went and returned in peace.

19So it is ordained and written on the tablets of heaven concerning Israel and its seed, to keep this festival seven days with the joy of a festival.

Notes

  • vv3, 5, 6, 7, 15, 16, 17 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which begins at v10 of this chapter, has vv15–17 too. The EOTC of v6 stops at Isaac's Father!; his question about the lamb, and the answer the EOTC keeps in v7, are the heart of Genesis 22:7–8.

  • vv1–19 the binding of Isaac — Genesis 22:1–19, retold in order, in this project's wording where the Ge'ez allows: Take, please, your son — your beloved one — whom you have loved — Isaac (22:2); God will see to the lamb for a burnt offering for Himself, my son (22:8). Jubilees adds what Genesis does not tell: Mastema stands watching (v9), and he is put to shame (v12).

  • v1 "Abraham, Abraham!" — Genesis 22:1 calls him once; the double call is Genesis 22:11, the angel's. Here the order is turned about: v10, the angel's call, has the name once in the EOTC (Charles and the Latin have Abraham, Abraham).

  • v2 "the high land" — Genesis 22:2 has the land of Moriah.

  • vv9, 11 "I know" — so the Ge'ez, as in Genesis 22:12, now I know that you fear God. Charles and the Latin have I have shown: in their text the test is not for God to learn but for the watching Mastema to see, as in v16, I have shown to all that you are faithful to Me.

  • vv11, 15 "your firstborn" — so the EOTC, of Isaac, though Ishmael is older; the Latin has firstborn in v11 and only son in v15. Genesis 22:12, 16 has your beloved one (see the note there).

  • v13 "That is Mount Zion" — Genesis 22:14 ends On the mountain of the LORD it will be seen. Jubilees names the mountain. So does Chronicles: Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, on Mount Moriah (2 Chronicles 3:1). The Greek has where David later established the sanctuary.

  • vv15–16 "By Myself I have sworn" — Genesis 22:16–18. "will inherit the cities of its enemies" — the Latin; Genesis has Your seed shall seize the gate of their enemies.

  • vv18–19 "this festival… seven days" — the Ge'ez does not name it. The heavenly council met on the twelfth of the first month (17:15); counted from there, three days' journey out and seven days in all would fall in the week of the Festival of Unleavened Bread, which Leviticus sets on the fifteenth day of this month… Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread (Leviticus 23:6). v18 "every year" — the Latin has three times each year.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin and Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Sarah's Death, and Abraham Blesses Jacob
chapters.html:
Jubilees 19

1In the first year of the first week of the forty-second jubilee Abraham returned and lived opposite Hebron, that is Kiriath-arba, two weeks of years.

2In the first year of the third week of this jubilee the days of Sarah's life were completed, and she died in Hebron.

3Abraham went to weep for her and to bury her. We tested him, to see whether his spirit was patient and not faint in the words of his mouth; and he was found very patient in this too, and was not troubled.

4For with patience of spirit he spoke with the sons of Heth, that they might give him a place to bury his dead in.

5The Lord gave him favor before all who saw him; and he entreated the sons of Heth in meekness, and they gave him the field of the double cave, which is opposite Mamre — that is Hebron — for forty pieces of silver.

6They pleaded with him, saying, "We will give it to you for nothing"; but he would not take it from their hands for nothing, for he gave the price of the place, the silver in full; and he bowed down before them twice, and after this he buried his dead in the double cave.

7All the days of Sarah's life were one hundred and twenty-seven years, that is, two jubilees and four weeks and one year; these are the days of the years of Sarah's life.

8This is the tenth trial with which Abraham was tried, and he was found faithful, patient in spirit.

9He did not say a word about the promise of the land, that the Lord had said He would give it to him and to his seed after him; and he begged a place from them to bury his dead, for he was found faithful, and he was written on the tablets of heaven as the friend of God.

10In its fourth year he took a wife for Isaac his son, and her name was Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, the sister of Laban and daughter of Bethuel; and Bethuel was the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother.

11Abraham took for himself a third wife, named Keturah, from the daughters of his household servants, for Hagar had died before Sarah.

12She bore him six sons, Zimran and Jokshan and Medan and Midian and Ishbak and Shuah, in two weeks of years.

13In the sixth week, in its second year, Rebekah bore Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. Jacob was whole and upright, and Esau was a fierce man, a man of the field, and hairy; and Jacob lived in tents.

14The young men grew, and Jacob learned writing; but Esau did not learn, for he was a man of the field and a hunter, and he learned war, and all his deeds were fierce.

15Abraham loved Jacob, and Isaac loved Esau.

16Abraham saw Esau's deeds, and he knew that through Jacob name and seed would be called for him; and he called Rebekah and gave her commands about Jacob, for she loved Jacob more than Esau.

17He said to her, "My daughter, watch over my son Jacob, for he will be in my place on the earth, and for a blessing among the sons of men, and for the glory of all the seed of Shem.

18For I know that the Lord will choose him to be a people for His own possession, above all who are on the face of the earth.

19Isaac my son loves Esau more than Jacob, but I see that you love Jacob in truth.

20Add still more kindness to him, and let your eyes be on him in love; for he will be a blessing for us on the earth, from now on and to every generation of the earth.

21Let your hands be strong, and let your heart rejoice in your son Jacob; for I have loved him above all my sons. He will be blessed forever, and his seed will fill all the earth.

22If a man can number the sand of the earth, so also will his seed be numbered.

23All the blessings with which the Lord has blessed me and my seed will belong to Jacob and to his seed all the days.

24In his seed my name will be blessed, and the name of my fathers, Shem and Noah and Enoch and Mahalalel and Enosh and Seth and Adam.

25These will serve to lay the foundations of heaven, and to strengthen the earth, and to renew all the lights that are in the expanse."

26He called Jacob before the eyes of Rebekah his mother, and kissed him and blessed him and said,

27"Jacob, my beloved son, whom my soul loves, may God bless you from above the expanse, and give you all the blessings with which He blessed Adam and Enoch and Noah and Shem, and all that He has told me, and all that He promised to give me; may He make them cleave to you and to your seed forever, according to the days of heaven above the earth.

28May the spirits of Mastema not rule over you or over your seed, to turn you away from following the Lord, who is your God, from now on and forever.

29May the Lord God be a father to you, and you His firstborn son and His people, all the days. Go in peace, my son."

30The two of them went out together from Abraham.

31Rebekah loved Jacob with all her heart and with all her spirit, very much more than Esau; and Isaac loved Esau much more than Jacob.

Notes

  • vv3, 5, 6, 9, 16, 20, 21, 27, 29 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter as far as v26, has most of them too. Without the ends of vv5–6 the EOTC never says where Sarah was buried. v5 "forty pieces of silver" — so the Asmara printing, ʾarbāʿā; the Latin and Genesis 23:16 have four hundred.

  • vv1–7 the dates — the first year of the forty-second jubilee is 41 × 49 + 1 = 2010; the first year of its third week, when Sarah dies, is 2024. v7 "two jubilees and four weeks and one year" — 98 + 28 + 1 = 127, the years of Genesis 23:1: The life of Sarah was a hundred years and twenty years and seven years. The Latin has four weeks minus one year, which comes to 125.

  • vv3–9 the tenth trial — Genesis 23 tells the purchase of the cave at length; Jubilees makes it a test of patience. Abraham, who has been promised the whole land, buys a grave in it and says nothing. "the double cave" — the name, in the Latin and in the Asmara printing, for the cave Genesis calls Machpelah, which it takes as double: the cave of the field of Machpelah, facing Mamre — that is Hebron (Genesis 23:19).

  • v9 "the friend of God" — Isaiah 41:8: the seed of Abraham My friend; James 2:23: he was called friend of God. Here the name is written on the tablets of heaven.

  • v10 "Bethuel was the son of Milcah" — the Ge'ez runs together here (wa-Batuʾel waladomu la-Batuʾelāwiyān, "and Bethuel fathered the Bethuelites"); the sense follows the Latin and Charles. Genesis 22:20: Milcah has borne sons, she also, to Nahor your brother. "In its fourth year" — 2027; Isaac, born in 1987, is forty, as in Genesis 25:20, Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah.

  • vv11–12 Keturah — Genesis 25:1–2. Jubilees makes her a daughter of the household servants, and has Hagar die before Sarah; Genesis says neither.

  • vv13–14 Jacob and Esau — Genesis 25:27: Esau was a man who knew hunting, a man of the field; and Jacob was a whole man, dwelling in tents. Jubilees adds that Jacob learned to write and Esau learned war. The date — the second year of the sixth week is 2046, when Isaac is fifty-nine; Genesis 25:26 has Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them, and the Greek of this verse says the same.

  • vv15–31 Abraham chooses Jacob — in Genesis Abraham's death is told before the twins are born (Genesis 25:7–8), and the blessing reaches Jacob through Rebekah's plan, when Isaac's eyes are dim (Genesis 27:1). In Jubilees Abraham sees the boys grow up and sets his blessing on Jacob himself, with Rebekah as its keeper. v16 "through Jacob name and seed would be called for him" — the words of 16:16 and Genesis 21:12, through Isaac shall seed be called for you, carried on to the next generation.

  • v24 "Shem and Noah and Enoch and Mahalalel and Enosh and Seth and Adam" — Abraham's line, skipping many names; the Latin leaves out Seth.

  • v25 "to lay the foundations of heaven, and to strengthen the earth" — as the LORD says to His people in Isaiah 51:16: to plant the heavens and to lay the foundations of the earth, and to say to Zion, "You are My people."

  • v29 "a father to you, and you His firstborn son" — Exodus 4:22: Israel is My son, My firstborn.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin and Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Abraham Commands His Sons
chapters.html:
Jubilees 20

1In the forty-second jubilee, in the first year of the seventh week, Abraham called Ishmael and his twelve sons, and Isaac and his two sons, and the six sons of Keturah and their sons.

2He commanded them to keep the way of the Lord, to do righteousness, and to love each one his neighbor, and to be so in every strife, each walking toward the others so as to do justice and righteousness on the earth;

3that they should circumcise their sons according to the covenant He had made with them, and not turn aside to the right or the left from all the ways the Lord commanded us; and that we should keep ourselves from all fornication and uncleanness, and put away from among us all uncleanness and fornication.

4If any woman or girl among you commits fornication, burn her with fire; and let them not go whoring after their eyes and their hearts, and let them not take wives for themselves from the daughters of Canaan, for the seed of Canaan will be uprooted from the land.

5He told them of the judgment of the giants and the judgment of Sodom, how they were judged for their wickedness, and died for fornication and uncleanness and corruption among themselves through fornication.

6"You too, keep yourselves from all fornication and uncleanness, and from all the defilement of sin, so that you do not make our name a curse, and all your life a hissing, and all your sons a ruin by the sword, and become cursed like Sodom, and all your remnant like the sons of Gomorrah.

7I testify to you, my sons: love the God of heaven and cling to all His commandments, and do not go after their idols and after their uncleanness.

8Do not make for yourselves molten gods or carved images, for they are empty, and there is no spirit in them, for they are the work of hands, and all who trust in them trust in nothing. Do not serve them, and do not bow down to them.

9But serve the Most High God and bow down to Him always, and hope for His face at all times, and do righteousness and uprightness before Him, so that He may be pleased with you and give you His mercy and send down rain for you morning and evening, and bless all your works that you do on the earth, and bless your bread and your water, and bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your land, the herds of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep.

10You will be a blessing on the earth, and all the nations of the earth will desire you, and they will bless your sons in my name, so that they may be a blessing as I am."

11He gave gifts to Ishmael and his sons and to the sons of Keturah, and sent them away from Isaac his son, and he gave everything to Isaac his son.

12Ishmael and his sons, and the sons of Keturah and their sons, went together and lived from Paran to the entrance of Babylon, in all the land toward the east, facing the desert.

13These mixed with one another, and their name was called Arabs and Ishmaelites[, to this day].

Notes

  • vv8, 9, 10, 13 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which begins partway through v5, has them too. Words in [brackets] (v13) are in no Ge'ez text here; they follow the Latin.

  • v1 the date — the first year of the seventh week of the forty-second jubilee is 41 × 49 + 6 × 7 + 1 = 2052. By the book's date for Abraham's birth (1876, 11:15) he is 176; Genesis 25:7 gives him a hundred years and seventy years and five years in all. His death comes in chapter 23.

  • v2 "to keep the way of the Lord, to do righteousness" — Genesis 18:19: he may charge his sons and his house after him, and they shall keep the way of the LORD, to do righteousness and judgment. Jubilees shows him doing it. "in every strife" — the Ge'ez has ṣabʾ, war or strife; Charles reads among all men.

  • v4 "burn her with fire" — the law of Leviticus 21:9 for a priest's daughter who whores: She shall be burned in the fire. "go whoring after their eyes and their hearts" — Numbers 15:39: you will not go about after your own heart and your own eyes, which you follow like a prostitute. "the daughters of Canaan" — Abraham's charge in Genesis 24:3, here given to all his sons.

  • v5 "the giants" — the sons of the Watchers (5:1; 7:22), destroyed with Sodom as the two great examples of judgment.

  • v6 "a hissing" — so the Latin and Charles; the EOTC has la-təmkəḥt, the word rendered glory at 19:17, which does not fit a curse.

  • v9 "rain… morning and evening" — the Latin has the early and the late rains, as Deuteronomy 11:14: I will give the rain of your land in its season, the early rain and the late rain. "the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your land" — Deuteronomy 28:4: Blessed is the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground.

  • vv11–13 the sons sent east — Genesis 25:5–6: Abraham gave all that was his to Isaac. To the sons of the secondary wives… Abraham gave gifts, and he sent them away from Isaac his son… eastward, to the land of the east. Jubilees adds that the sons of Ishmael and of Keturah mixed together and became the Arabs. "Paran" — the EOTC writes Farmon; the Latin has Faramon.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Abraham Teaches Isaac the Sacrifices
chapters.html:
Jubilees 21

1In the sixth year of the seventh week of this jubilee Abraham called Isaac his son and commanded him, saying, "I have grown old, and I do not know the day of my death, for I am full of my days.

2I am one hundred and seventy-five years old, and all the days of my life I have remembered the Lord, and sought with all my heart to do His will and to walk uprightly in all His ways.

3My soul has hated idols[, and I have despised those who serve them, and I have given my heart and my spirit], so that I might keep myself to do the will of Him who created me.

4For He is the living God, and He is holy, and faithful and righteous above all, and with Him there is no respect of persons and no taking of gifts; for God is righteous, and He executes judgment on all who transgress His commandments and despise His covenant.

5You too, my son, keep His commandments and His ordinances and His judgments, and do not go after the unclean things, nor after carved images, nor after molten ones.

6Eat no blood at all, of wild animal or of cattle, or of any bird that flies in the sky.

7If you slaughter a sacrifice as an acceptable peace offering, slaughter it, and pour out its blood on the altar; and all the fat of the offering offer on the altar, with fine flour and the grain offering mixed with oil, with its drink offering — offer them all together on the altar of burnt offering, a soothing aroma before the Lord.

8The fat of the sacrifice of peace offering you shall set on the fire that is on the altar: the fat that is on the belly, and all the fat that is on the inner parts, and the two kidneys and all the fat that is on them and on the loins, and the liver, which you shall remove with the kidneys.

9Offer all this for a soothing aroma acceptable before the Lord, with its grain offering and its drink offering, for a soothing aroma, the bread of the offering to the Lord.

10Eat its meat on that day and on the next, and do not let the sun go down on it on the next day until it is eaten; and let nothing be left for the third day, for it is not acceptable, for it is not approved, and let it no longer be eaten; and all who eat of it will bring sin on themselves. For so I have found it written in the books of my forefathers, and in the words of Enoch, and in the words of Noah.

11On all your offerings you shall scatter salt, and let not the covenant of salt be missing from all your offerings before the Lord.

12Take care with the wood of the sacrifice, that you bring no other wood onto the altar than these: cypress and bay and almond, fir and pine and cedar, savin and fig and the olive tree, myrrh and laurel, and the cedar called arbat, and besem.

13Of these kinds of wood lay under the offering on the altar such as have been tested by their look; and do not lay on it any split or dark wood, but wood that is hard and firm, without any blemish, whole and of new growth. Do not lay on it old wood, for its fragrance has gone out, for there is no longer fragrance in it as at first.

14Besides these kinds of wood you shall lay no other[; for the fragrance is scattered, and the smell of its fragrance does not go up to heaven].

15Keep this command and do it, my son, so that you may be upright in all your works.

16At all times be clean in your body, and wash with water before you go to offer on the altar; and wash your hands and your feet before you draw near to the altar; and when you have finished offering, wash your hands and your feet again.

17Let no blood be seen on you or on your clothes; be on your guard, my son, against blood, be very much on your guard; cover it with earth.

18Do not eat blood, for blood is the soul; eat no blood at all.

19Take no gifts for any human blood, so that it is not shed with impunity, without judgment; for it is the blood that is shed that makes the earth sin, and the earth cannot be cleansed from human blood except by the blood of the one who shed it.

20Take no present or gift for human blood: blood for blood, and you will be acceptable before God Most High; for He is the defense of the good, and so you will be kept from all evil, and He will save you from every kind of death.

21I see, my son, all the works of the sons of men, that they are sin and wickedness, and all their deeds are uncleanness and abomination and defilement, and there is no righteousness with them.

22Take care not to walk in their ways and tread in their paths, and do not sin a sin to death before God Most High; otherwise He will hide His face from you and give you back into the hands of your transgression, and root you out of the land, and your seed likewise from under heaven, and your name and your seed will perish from the whole earth.

23Turn away from all their deeds and all their uncleanness, and keep the charge of God Most High, and do His will, and be upright in all things.

24He will bless you in all your deeds, and will raise up from you a plant of righteousness in all the earth, through all the generations of the earth; and my name and your name will not be forgotten under heaven, for all days.

25Go, my son, in peace. May God Most High, my God and your God, strengthen you to do His will, and may He bless all your seed and the remnant of your seed for the eternal generations with every blessing of righteousness, so that you may be a blessing on all the earth."

26He went out from him rejoicing.

Notes

  • vv10, 20, 21, 22 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). Words in [brackets] are in no whole Ge'ez text here: in v3 they follow the Latin, which covers this chapter as far as v10; in v14 they follow Charles's English, where the Asmara printing is broken (for its fragrance… to heaven).

  • vv1–2 the date — the sixth year of the seventh week of the forty-second jubilee is 41 × 49 + 6 × 7 + 6 = 2057, which by 11:15 makes Abraham 181; he says he is 175, the age at which he dies in Genesis 25:7. The text is left as it stands (compare 15:1; 20:1).

  • vv6–10 the peace offering — the law of Leviticus 3 and 19, given here by Abraham to Isaac long before Sinai: the fat covering the entrails… and the two kidneys with the fat on them at the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall remove with the kidneys (Leviticus 3:3–4); It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it and on the next day… If it is eaten at all on the third day, it is foul. It will not be accepted (Leviticus 19:6–7). v9 "the bread of the offering" — Leviticus 3:11, food, an offering by fire to the LORD. v10 "the books of my forefathers… Enoch… Noah" — in Charles's text Abraham names his sources. The book has already told of the books of his fathers, which he copied in Hebrew (12:27), and of the book Noah wrote (10:13).

  • v11 "the covenant of salt" — Leviticus 2:13: You shall not let the salt of the covenant of your God be missing from your grain offering. With all your offerings you shall bring salt.

  • v12 the woods — the list follows Charles's English for the first eleven, cypress, bay, almond, fir, pine, cedar, savin, fig, olive, myrrh, laurel; he gives aspalathus for the twelfth. The Ge'ez has thirteen names, the last two left here as it writes them: the cedar called arbat, and besem. Several are Greek names in Ge'ez letters: qeṗarson, ṗiṭin, qedron.

  • v16 washing hands and feet — Exodus 30:20–21: When they come into the tent of meeting they shall wash with water, and they shall not die… They shall wash their hands and their feet.

  • vv17–18 "cover it with earth… blood is the soul" — Leviticus 17:13–14: shall pour out its blood and cover it with earth. For the life of all flesh — its blood is its life. Genesis 9:4: flesh with its soul — its blood — you shall not eat.

  • vv19–20 "blood for blood" — Numbers 35:33: the blood pollutes the land, and for the land no atonement can be made for the blood shed in it except by the blood of the one who shed it. Genesis 9:6: One who sheds the blood of the human, by the human shall his blood be shed.

  • v22 "a sin to death" — 1 John 5:16: There is a sin to death; I do not say that he should ask about that.

  • v24 "a plant of righteousness" — as at 16:26.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.
