chapters.title: Abraham's Last Festival and His Blessing of Jacob
chapters.html:
Jubilees 22

1And it came to pass in the first week of the forty-fourth jubilee, in the second year, the year in which Abraham died, that Isaac and Ishmael came from the Well of the Oath to keep the Festival of Weeks, the festival of the first fruits of the harvest, with Abraham their father; and Abraham rejoiced because both his sons had come.

2For Isaac had many possessions in Beersheba, and Isaac would go and look over his possessions and return to his father.

3In those days Ishmael came to see his father, and they all came together; and Isaac slaughtered a sacrifice for a burnt offering and offered it on the altar of his father that he had made in Hebron.

4He offered a peace offering and made a feast of joy before Ishmael his brother; and Rebekah made new cakes from the new grain and gave them to Jacob her son, to bring to Abraham his father from the first fruits of the land, so that he might eat and bless the Creator of all things before he died.

5Isaac too sent by the hand of Jacob the best peace offering to Abraham, that he might eat and drink.

6He ate and drank, and blessed God Most High, who created heaven and earth, who made all the fat of the earth and gave it to the sons of men to eat and drink and bless their Creator.

7"Now I give thanks to You, my God, because You have let me see this day. I am one hundred and seventy-five years old, old and full of days, and all my days have been peace to me.

8The sword of the enemy has not overcome me in anything You gave me, or in my sons, all the days of my life until this day.

9May Your mercy and Your peace be on Your servant and on the seed of his sons, that they may be to You a chosen people and an inheritance from all the nations of the earth, from now on to all the days of the generations of the earth, for all the ages."

10He called Jacob and said to him, "My son Jacob, may the God of all bless you and strengthen you to do righteousness and His will before Him, and may He choose you and your seed, that you may be to Him a people for His inheritance according to His will, all the days. You, my son Jacob, come near to me and kiss me."

11He came near and kissed him. He said, "Blessed are you, my son Jacob, and all the sons of God Most High, in all the ages. May God give you a seed of righteousness from your sons, and may He make it holy in the middle of the whole earth; nations will serve you, and all the nations will bow down before your seed.

12Be strong before men, and rule over all the seed of Seth; then your ways and the ways of your sons will be justified, so that they become a holy people.

13May God Most High give you all the blessings with which He blessed me and with which He blessed Noah and Adam; may they rest on the holy head of your seed, for every generation of generations and forever.

14May He cleanse you from all the filth of uncleanness, so that you may be forgiven every transgression you have committed in ignorance; and may He strengthen you and bless you, and may you inherit all the earth.

15May He renew His covenant with you, that you may be to Him a people for His inheritance for all the ages, and that He may be God to you and to your seed in truth and righteousness all the days of the earth.

16You too, my son Jacob, remember my words and keep the commandments of Abraham your father: separate yourself from the nations, and do not eat with them, and do not act according to their deeds, and do not become their companion; for their works are defilement, and all their way is uncleanness and abomination and filth.

17They sacrifice their sacrifices to the dead and bow down to demons, and they eat over graves, and all their deeds are empty and nothing.

18They have no heart to understand, and their eyes do not see what their deeds are, and how they go astray, saying to wood, 'You are my god,' and to stone, 'You are my lord and my deliverer'; and they have no heart.

19As for you, my son Jacob, may God Most High help you, and the God of heaven bless you, and may He turn you away from their uncleanness and from all their error.

20Take care, my son Jacob, not to take a wife from any seed of the daughters of Canaan[, for all his seed is to be rooted out of the earth].

21For through the transgression of Ham, Canaan went astray, and all his seed will be wiped out from the earth, and all its remnant, and none of him will be saved on the day of judgment.

22For all who serve idols, and for the profane, there is no hope at all in the land of the living; for they will go down into Sheol, and into the place of condemnation they will go, and there will be no remembrance of them on the earth. As the sons of Sodom were taken away from the earth, so all who serve idols will be taken away.

23Do not fear, my son Jacob, and do not be dismayed, son of Abraham. May God Most High keep you from destruction, and from every path of error may He deliver you.

24This house I have built for myself, to put my name on it on the earth: it is given to you and to your seed forever, and it will be called the house of Abraham; it is given to you and to your seed forever, for you will build my house and establish my name before God forever. Your seed and your name will stand through all the generations of the earth."

25He finished commanding him and blessing him.

26The two of them lay together on one bed, and Jacob slept in the bosom of Abraham, his father's father; and he kissed him seven times, and his affection and his heart rejoiced over him.

27He blessed him with all his heart and said, "God Most High, the God of all and Creator of all, who brought me out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give me this land to inherit forever, and to raise up a holy seed, that it may be blessed forever—"

28He blessed Jacob: "My son, in whom I rejoice with all my heart and with all my affection — may Your grace and Your mercy be lifted high over him and over his seed all the days.

29Do not forsake him or despise him, from now on to the days of eternity; and may Your eyes be open on him and on his seed, to keep him and bless him and make him holy as a people for Your inheritance.

30Bless him with all Your blessings, from now on to all the days of eternity, and renew Your covenant and Your grace with him and with his seed according to all Your good pleasure, to all the generations of the earth."

Notes

  • vv4, 8, 10, 11, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 22, 29, 30 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v2 to v19, has most of them too. v11 — the Latin blessing is broken in places and has a seed of truth and before your name; the Asmara printing, like Charles, has a seed of righteousness and before your seed. Words in [brackets] (v20) are in no Ge'ez text here; they follow Charles's English, made from other Ge'ez manuscripts.

  • v1 the date — the second year of the first week of the forty-fourth jubilee is 43 × 49 + 2 = 2109. Abraham, born in 1876 (11:15), dies at 175 (v7; 23:8), which would be 2051. Charles's English has forty-fourth too. The text is left as it stands (compare 21:1).

  • vv1–5 the last Festival of Weeks — Abraham's sons come to him on the festival of first fruits, the day of the covenants with Noah and with Abram (6:17; 14:10; 15:1). In Genesis Isaac and Ishmael meet once more, at his burial (Genesis 25:9).

  • vv7–9 "old and full of days" — Genesis 25:8: Abraham expired and died at a good gray age, old and satisfied.

  • vv10–24 the blessing of Jacob — the blessing that in Genesis passes from Isaac to Jacob by Rebekah's plan (Genesis 27) is here given openly by Abraham, as 19:16–29 foretold.

  • v16 "separate yourself from the nations, and do not eat with them" — the rule Peter names in Acts: You know how unlawful it is for a Jewish man to join himself to a foreigner or to come to him (Acts 10:28).

  • v17 "They sacrifice… to the dead and bow down to demons" — Psalm 106:28: they ate the sacrifices of the dead; Deuteronomy 32:17: They sacrificed to demons, not God. v18 "saying to wood, 'You are my god'" — Jeremiah 2:27: saying to wood, "You are my father," and to stone, "You gave birth to me."

  • v19 "the God of heaven" — the Latin has the God of Adam.

  • vv20–22 the daughters of Canaan — as Abraham charged all his sons (20:4). Canaan's curse goes back to Ham's sin (Genesis 9:22–25) and to Canaan's seizing of Shem's land (10:29–34).

  • v24 "This house I have built for myself" — Abraham's house in Hebron, given to Jacob; it will be named the house of Abraham.

  • v26 "Jacob slept in the bosom of Abraham" — the last night of Abraham's life. In Luke the poor man is carried by the angels to Abraham's bosom (Luke 16:22).

speech.text: Jubilees 22

And it came to pass in the first week of the forty-fourth jubilee, in the second year, the year in which Abraham died, that Isaac and Ishmael came from the Well of the Oath to keep the Festival of Weeks, the festival of the first fruits of the harvest, with Abraham their father; and Abraham rejoiced because both his sons had come.
For Isaac had many possessions in Beersheba, and Isaac would go and look over his possessions and return to his father.
In those days Ishmael came to see his father, and they all came together; and Isaac slaughtered a sacrifice for a burnt offering and offered it on the altar of his father that he had made in Hebron.

He offered a peace offering and made a feast of joy before Ishmael his brother; and Rebekah made new cakes from the new grain and gave them to Jacob her son, to bring to Abraham his father from the first fruits of the land, so that he might eat and bless the Creator of all things before he died.
Isaac too sent by the hand of Jacob the best peace offering to Abraham, that he might eat and drink.
He ate and drank, and blessed God Most High, who created heaven and earth, who made all the fat of the earth and gave it to the sons of men to eat and drink and bless their Creator.
"Now I give thanks to You, my God, because You have let me see this day. I am one hundred and seventy-five years old, old and full of days, and all my days have been peace to me.
The sword of the enemy has not overcome me in anything You gave me, or in my sons, all the days of my life until this day.

May Your mercy and Your peace be on Your servant and on the seed of his sons, that they may be to You a chosen people and an inheritance from all the nations of the earth, from now on to all the days of the generations of the earth, for all the ages."

He called Jacob and said to him, "My son Jacob, may the God of all bless you and strengthen you to do righteousness and His will before Him, and may He choose you and your seed, that you may be to Him a people for His inheritance according to His will, all the days. You, my son Jacob, come near to me and kiss me."

He came near and kissed him. He said, "Blessed are you, my son Jacob, and all the sons of God Most High, in all the ages. May God give you a seed of righteousness from your sons, and may He make it holy in the middle of the whole earth; nations will serve you, and all the nations will bow down before your seed.
Be strong before men, and rule over all the seed of Seth; then your ways and the ways of your sons will be justified, so that they become a holy people.

May God Most High give you all the blessings with which He blessed me and with which He blessed Noah and Adam; may they rest on the holy head of your seed, for every generation of generations and forever.

May He cleanse you from all the filth of uncleanness, so that you may be forgiven every transgression you have committed in ignorance; and may He strengthen you and bless you, and may you inherit all the earth.

May He renew His covenant with you, that you may be to Him a people for His inheritance for all the ages, and that He may be God to you and to your seed in truth and righteousness all the days of the earth.

You too, my son Jacob, remember my words and keep the commandments of Abraham your father: separate yourself from the nations, and do not eat with them, and do not act according to their deeds, and do not become their companion; for their works are defilement, and all their way is uncleanness and abomination and filth.
They sacrifice their sacrifices to the dead and bow down to demons, and they eat over graves, and all their deeds are empty and nothing.

They have no heart to understand, and their eyes do not see what their deeds are, and how they go astray, saying to wood, 'You are my god,' and to stone, 'You are my lord and my deliverer'; and they have no heart.
As for you, my son Jacob, may God Most High help you, and the God of heaven bless you, and may He turn you away from their uncleanness and from all their error.
Take care, my son Jacob, not to take a wife from any seed of the daughters of Canaan[, for all his seed is to be rooted out of the earth].
For through the transgression of Ham, Canaan went astray, and all his seed will be wiped out from the earth, and all its remnant, and none of him will be saved on the day of judgment.

For all who serve idols, and for the profane, there is no hope at all in the land of the living; for they will go down into Sheol, and into the place of condemnation they will go, and there will be no remembrance of them on the earth. As the sons of Sodom were taken away from the earth, so all who serve idols will be taken away.
Do not fear, my son Jacob, and do not be dismayed, son of Abraham. May God Most High keep you from destruction, and from every path of error may He deliver you.

This house I have built for myself, to put my name on it on the earth: it is given to you and to your seed forever, and it will be called the house of Abraham; it is given to you and to your seed forever, for you will build my house and establish my name before God forever. Your seed and your name will stand through all the generations of the earth."
He finished commanding him and blessing him.
The two of them lay together on one bed, and Jacob slept in the bosom of Abraham, his father's father; and he kissed him seven times, and his affection and his heart rejoiced over him.

He blessed him with all his heart and said, "God Most High, the God of all and Creator of all, who brought me out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give me this land to inherit forever, and to raise up a holy seed, that it may be blessed forever—"
He blessed Jacob: "My son, in whom I rejoice with all my heart and with all my affection — may Your grace and Your mercy be lifted high over him and over his seed all the days.
Do not forsake him or despise him, from now on to the days of eternity; and may Your eyes be open on him and on his seed, to keep him and bless him and make him holy as a people for Your inheritance.

Bless him with all Your blessings, from now on to all the days of eternity, and renew Your covenant and Your grace with him and with his seed according to all Your good pleasure, to all the generations of the earth."

chapters.title: Abraham's Death, and the Shortening and Lengthening of Days
chapters.html:
Jubilees 23

1He laid two of Jacob's fingers on his eyes, and blessed the God of gods, and covered his face and stretched out his feet, and slept the sleep of eternity, and was gathered to his fathers.

2Through all this Jacob was lying in his bosom, and did not know that Abraham, his father's father, had died.

3Jacob woke from his sleep, and Abraham was cold as ice, and he said, "Father, father"; but no one spoke, and he knew that he was dead.

4He rose from his bosom and ran and told Rebekah his mother; and Rebekah went to Isaac in the night and told him, and they went together, and Jacob with them, with a lamp in his hand; and when they went in they found Abraham lying dead.

5Isaac fell on his father's face, and wept and kissed him.

6A voice was heard in the house of Abraham; and Ishmael his son rose and went to Abraham his father, and wept over Abraham his father, he and all the house of Abraham, and they wept with a great weeping.

7His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the double cave, near Sarah his wife; and they wept for him forty days, all the men of his house, and Isaac and Ishmael and all their sons, and all the sons of Keturah in their places; and the days of weeping for Abraham were ended.

8He lived three jubilees and four weeks of years, one hundred and seventy-five years, and completed the days of his life, old and full of days.

9For the days of the ancients, of their life, were nineteen jubilees; and after the flood they began to fall short of nineteen jubilees, and to grow old more quickly, and the days of their lives were shortened by the affliction of many things and the wickedness of their ways — except for Abraham.

10For Abraham was whole in all his deeds with the Lord, and pleasing in truth all the days of his life; yet he did not complete four jubilees in his life before he grew old because of the wickedness of men, and he was full of his days.

11All the generations that arise from now until the day of the great judgment will grow old quickly, before they complete two jubilees, and their understanding will leave them because of their old age, and all their knowledge will pass away.

12In those days, if a man lives a jubilee and a half of years, they will say of him, "He has lived long"; and the greater part of his days are sickness and toil and affliction, and there is no peace.

13For there is blow upon blow, and wound upon wound, and affliction upon affliction, and evil report upon evil report, and sickness upon sickness, and every evil judgment like these, one with another: sickness and overthrow, and snow and frost and ice, and fever and chills and torpor, and famine and death, and sword and captivity, and all kinds of plagues and pains.

14All this will come on an evil generation, which makes the earth sin with the uncleanness of fornication, and with defilement, and with the abominations of their deeds.

15Then they will say, "The days of the ancients were many, up to a thousand years, and good; but the days of our life, if a man lives long, are seventy years, and if he is very strong, eighty, and these are evil, and there is no peace at all in the days of this evil generation."

16In that generation the sons will rebuke their fathers and their elders for sin and for unrighteousness, and for the words of their mouth, and for the great wickedness that they do, because they have forsaken the covenant that God made between Himself and them, to keep and do all His commandments and His ordinances and all His laws, without turning aside to the right or to the left.

17For all have done evil, and every mouth speaks transgression, and all their works are uncleanness and hatred, and all their ways are defilement and abomination and destruction.

18The earth will be destroyed because of all their deeds, and there will be no seed of the vine and no oil, for all their deeds are faithless; and they will all perish together, wild animals and cattle and birds, and all the fish of the sea, because of the sons of men.

19They will quarrel with one another, the young with the old and the old with the young, the poor with the rich, the lowly with the great, and the beggar with the ruler, over the law and over the covenant; for they have forgotten commandment and covenant, and festival and month, and Sabbath and jubilee, and every judgment.

20They will stand with swords and with war to turn them back into the way, and they will not turn back until much blood is shed on the earth, one by another.

21Those who have escaped will not turn back from their wickedness to the way of righteousness, for they will all lift themselves up to deceit and to wealth, so that each may take all that is his neighbor's; and they will name the great name, but not in truth and not in righteousness; and they will defile the holy of holies with the uncleanness of the corruption of their defilement.

22There will be a great punishment from the Lord on the deeds of that generation, and He will give them over to the sword and to judgment, to captivity and to plunder and to being devoured.

23He will rouse against them the sinners of the nations, who have no mercy or compassion on them, and who will show favor to no one, neither old nor young nor anyone, for they are more wicked and strong to do evil than all the sons of men; and they will do violence in Israel and transgression against Jacob, and much blood will be shed on the earth, and there will be none to gather and none to bury.

24In those days they will cry out and call and pray to be saved from the hand of the sinners, the nations, and there will be none to save.

25The heads of the children will be white with gray hair, and a child three weeks old will look old like one a hundred years old, and their stature will be destroyed by affliction and distress.

26In those days the children will begin to search the laws, and to seek the commandment, and to return to the path of righteousness.

27The days will begin to grow many and increase, among the sons of men, generation after generation and day after day, until their days come near to a thousand years, and to more years than the many days before.

28There will be no old man, and none who is full of days, for all of them will be as children and boys.

29They will complete all their days and live in peace and joy, and there will be no Satan and no evil one who destroys; for all their days will be days of blessing and healing.

30Then the Lord will heal His servants, and they will rise and see great peace, and He will drive out His enemies; and the righteous will see and give thanks, and rejoice with joy forever and ever, and will see all His judgments and all His curses on their enemies.

31Their bones will rest in the earth, and their spirits will have much joy, and they will know that it is the Lord who executes judgment and shows mercy to hundreds and thousands, and to all who love Him.

32You too, Moses, write these words, for so they are written, and they are brought up into the testimony of the tablets of heaven for the eternal generations.

Notes

  • vv1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 30, 31 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v8 to v23, has vv9–18 too. Without the ends of vv3–7 the EOTC never says that anyone found Abraham dead or mourned him.

  • vv1–8 Abraham's death — Genesis 25:7–9: Abraham expired and died at a good gray age, old and satisfied, and he was gathered to his people. Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him in the cave of Machpelah. v5 "Isaac fell on his father's face" — as Joseph did at Jacob's death: Joseph fell on his father's face, and wept over him, and kissed him (Genesis 50:1); the forty days of weeping in v7 are the forty days of Genesis 50:3. v8 "three jubilees and four weeks of years" — 147 + 28 = 175.

  • vv9–15 the shortening of days — the ancients, says v9, lived nineteen jubilees (931 years); Abraham, the most righteous since, did not reach four (196). v15 "seventy years… eighty" — Psalm 90:10: The days of our years in them are seventy years, and if by strength, eighty years.

  • vv16–25 the evil generation — the sons rebuke the fathers, the covenant, the festivals, the months and the Sabbaths are forgotten, and the nations are sent against Israel. v17 "every mouth speaks transgression" — Paul, quoting the Psalms: All have turned aside, together they have become worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one (Romans 3:12). v25 "a child three weeks old" — elsewhere in Jubilees a week is seven years; Charles leaves it as three weeks.

  • vv26–31 the lengthening of days — the turn comes when the children will begin to search the laws (v26), and life lengthens back toward a thousand years. Isaiah 65:20: No more will there be from there an infant of days, or an old man who does not fill his days; for the youth shall die a hundred years old. v31 "Their bones will rest in the earth, and their spirits will have much joy" — the body at rest in the ground, the spirit in joy; the second half is in Charles's bracket. "to thousands… to all who love Him" — Exodus 20:6: doing loyal love to thousands, for those who love Me and keep My commandments.

  • v30 "He will drive out His enemies" — so the EOTC; Charles has they shall… drive out their adversaries.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Birthright, the Wells, and the Curse on the Philistines
chapters.html:
Jubilees 24

1And it came to pass after Abraham died that the Lord blessed Isaac his son; and he rose from Hebron and went and lived at the Well of the Vision, in the first year of the third week of this jubilee, seven years.

2In the fourth week a famine came on the land, besides the first famine that was in the days of Abraham.

3Jacob cooked a stew of lentils, and Esau came in from the field hungry, and said to Jacob his brother, "Give me some of this red stew." Jacob said to him, "Hand over to me your birthright, the right of the firstborn, and I will give you bread, and some of this stew too."

4Esau said in his heart, "I am going to die. What is this birthright to me?" He said to Jacob, "I give it to you."

5Jacob said to him, "Swear to me today," and he swore to him.

6Jacob gave his brother Esau bread and stew, and he ate until he was full, and Esau despised the birthright. For this reason his name was called Esau and Edom, because of the red stew that Jacob gave him for his birthright.

7Jacob grew great, and Esau was brought down from his greatness.

8The famine was on the land, and Isaac set out to go down to Egypt, in the second year of this week, and went to the king of the Philistines, to Gerar, to Abimelech.

9The Lord appeared to him and said to him, "Do not go down to Egypt. Settle in the land that I tell you of, and live as a guest in that land, and I will be with you and bless you.

10For to you and to your seed I will give all this land, and I will raise up the oath that I swore to Abraham your father, and I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and I will give to your seed all this land.

11In your seed all the nations of the earth will be blessed, because your father listened to My voice and kept My charge, and My commandments and My laws and My ordinances and My covenant; and now listen to My voice and My command, and live in this land."

12He lived in Gerar three weeks of years.

13Abimelech gave a command about him and about all that was his, saying, "Any man who touches him or anything that is his shall surely die."

14Isaac grew great among the Philistines, and he had many possessions: cattle and sheep and camels and donkeys, and many possessions.

15They sowed in the land of the Philistines, and reaped a hundredfold; and Isaac became very great, and the Philistines envied him.

16All the wells that Abraham's servants had dug in Abraham's lifetime the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham's death, and filled them with earth.

17Abimelech said to Isaac, "Go from us, for you have become much greater than we." Isaac went from there in the first year of the seventh week, and moved to the valleys of Gerar.

18They went back and dug the wells of water that the servants of Abraham his father had dug, which the Philistines had stopped up after the death of Abraham his father; and he called them by the names his father had called them.

19Isaac's servants dug wells in the valley and found living water, and the shepherds of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's shepherds, saying, "This water is ours." Isaac called the name of the well Hardship, because they were hard with us.

20They dug another well, and they quarreled over that one too, and he called its name Narrow. He moved on, and they dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it, and he called its name Room; and Isaac said, "Now the Lord has made room for us, and we have grown great in the land."

21He went up from there to the Well of the Oath, in the first year of the first week of the forty-fourth jubilee.

22The Lord appeared to him that night, on the new moon of the first month, and said to him, "I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not fear, for I am with you, and I will bless you, and I will surely multiply your seed as the sand of the earth, for the sake of Abraham My servant."

23He built an altar there, the one that Abraham his father had first built, and he called on the name of the Lord and offered sacrifice to the God of Abraham his father.

24They dug a well and found living water.

25Isaac's servants dug another well and did not find water; and they came and told Isaac that they had not found water, and Isaac said, "Because I swore an oath this day to the Philistines, this thing has happened to us."

26He called the name of that place the Well of the Oath, for there he had sworn to Abimelech, and to Ahuzzath his companion, and to Phicol the commander of his army.

27Isaac knew that day that he had sworn to them under constraint, to make peace with them.

28Isaac cursed the Philistines that day and said, "Cursed be the Philistines for the day of wrath and indignation, from among all the nations; may God make them a mockery and a curse, for wrath and indignation, in the hands of sinful nations and in the hand of the Kittim, who will root them out.

29Whoever escapes the sword of the enemy and the Kittim, may the righteous nation root out in judgment from under heaven; for they will be enemies and foes to my sons in their days on the earth.

30No remnant will be left to them, nor one who is saved on the day of the wrath of judgment; but they will be for destruction and extermination, so that all the seed of the Philistines may be removed from the face of the earth, and no name at all will remain to them on the earth.

31For even if he goes up to heaven, from there he will come down; and even if he makes himself strong on the earth, from there he will be dragged out; and even if he hides among the nations, from there he will be rooted out; and even if he goes down into Sheol, there his judgment will be great, and there will be no peace for him there.

32If he goes into captivity, by the hands of those who seek his life they will kill him on the way, and neither name nor seed will be left to him in all the earth; for he will go into an eternal curse."

33So it is written and engraved concerning him on the tablets of heaven, to be done to him on the day of judgment, so that he may be rooted out of the earth.

Notes

  • vv3, 10, 11, 15, 17, 18, 19, 23, 25, 28, 30, 31, 32 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v13 on, has most of them too. Without the end of v3 Jacob never asks for the birthright.

  • v1 "the Well of the Vision" — Genesis 25:11: Isaac settled by Beer-lahai-roi, the well Hagar named, the Well of the Living One who sees me.

  • vv1–21 the dates — this jubilee is the forty-fourth, the jubilee of Abraham's death (22:1). Its third week begins in 2122, and the first year of its seventh week (v17) is 2150. Then v21 has Isaac come to the Well of the Oath in the first year of the first week of the forty-fourth jubilee, 2108, before all of these. Charles's English has forty-fourth too. The text is left as it stands. v2 "In the fourth week" — the EOTC has in the year of the fourth week, with no number; Charles has the first year.

  • vv3–7 the birthright — Genesis 25:29–34: Let me gulp down some of that red, that red there… Therefore his name was called Edom… Jacob gave Esau bread and a boiling of lentils… Esau despised the birthright. "red" — in vv3 and 6 the EOTC has sərnāy, wheat, where Charles has red; the name Edom (v6) is explained by the red stew, so the English follows Charles and the note says so. v7 "Jacob grew great, and Esau was brought down" — Jubilees' own summary; Charles has Jacob became the elder.

  • vv8–13 Isaac in Gerar — Genesis 26:1–11. v11 "your father listened to My voice and kept My charge" — Genesis 26:5: because Abraham listened to My voice, and kept My charge: My commands, My statutes, and My instructions. Jubilees leaves out Genesis 26:7–11, where Isaac says of Rebekah She is my sister; only Abimelech's order is kept (v13).

  • vv16–26 the wells — Genesis 26:15–33. The names differ: Genesis has Esek (contention), Sitnah (enmity) and Rehoboth (room). v19 "Hardship" — the Latin; Charles has Perversity. v20 "Narrow" — the EOTC's Ṣabāb; Charles has Enmity. In Jubilees the dry well is a sign against the oath Isaac made under constraint (v27).

speech.text: Jubilees 24

And it came to pass after Abraham died that the Lord blessed Isaac his son; and he rose from Hebron and went and lived at the Well of the Vision, in the first year of the third week of this jubilee, seven years.
In the fourth week a famine came on the land, besides the first famine that was in the days of Abraham.

Jacob cooked a stew of lentils, and Esau came in from the field hungry, and said to Jacob his brother, "Give me some of this red stew." Jacob said to him, "Hand over to me your birthright, the right of the firstborn, and I will give you bread, and some of this stew too."
Esau said in his heart, "I am going to die. What is this birthright to me?" He said to Jacob, "I give it to you."
Jacob said to him, "Swear to me today," and he swore to him.

Jacob gave his brother Esau bread and stew, and he ate until he was full, and Esau despised the birthright. For this reason his name was called Esau and Edom, because of the red stew that Jacob gave him for his birthright.
Jacob grew great, and Esau was brought down from his greatness.
The famine was on the land, and Isaac set out to go down to Egypt, in the second year of this week, and went to the king of the Philistines, to Gerar, to Abimelech.
The Lord appeared to him and said to him, "Do not go down to Egypt. Settle in the land that I tell you of, and live as a guest in that land, and I will be with you and bless you.

For to you and to your seed I will give all this land, and I will raise up the oath that I swore to Abraham your father, and I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and I will give to your seed all this land.

In your seed all the nations of the earth will be blessed, because your father listened to My voice and kept My charge, and My commandments and My laws and My ordinances and My covenant; and now listen to My voice and My command, and live in this land."
He lived in Gerar three weeks of years.
Abimelech gave a command about him and about all that was his, saying, "Any man who touches him or anything that is his shall surely die."
Isaac grew great among the Philistines, and he had many possessions: cattle and sheep and camels and donkeys, and many possessions.
They sowed in the land of the Philistines, and reaped a hundredfold; and Isaac became very great, and the Philistines envied him.
All the wells that Abraham's servants had dug in Abraham's lifetime the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham's death, and filled them with earth.
Abimelech said to Isaac, "Go from us, for you have become much greater than we." Isaac went from there in the first year of the seventh week, and moved to the valleys of Gerar.

They went back and dug the wells of water that the servants of Abraham his father had dug, which the Philistines had stopped up after the death of Abraham his father; and he called them by the names his father had called them.

Isaac's servants dug wells in the valley and found living water, and the shepherds of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's shepherds, saying, "This water is ours." Isaac called the name of the well Hardship, because they were hard with us.

They dug another well, and they quarreled over that one too, and he called its name Narrow. He moved on, and they dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it, and he called its name Room; and Isaac said, "Now the Lord has made room for us, and we have grown great in the land."
He went up from there to the Well of the Oath, in the first year of the first week of the forty-fourth jubilee.

The Lord appeared to him that night, on the new moon of the first month, and said to him, "I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not fear, for I am with you, and I will bless you, and I will surely multiply your seed as the sand of the earth, for the sake of Abraham My servant."
He built an altar there, the one that Abraham his father had first built, and he called on the name of the Lord and offered sacrifice to the God of Abraham his father.
They dug a well and found living water.

Isaac's servants dug another well and did not find water; and they came and told Isaac that they had not found water, and Isaac said, "Because I swore an oath this day to the Philistines, this thing has happened to us."
He called the name of that place the Well of the Oath, for there he had sworn to Abimelech, and to Ahuzzath his companion, and to Phicol the commander of his army.
Isaac knew that day that he had sworn to them under constraint, to make peace with them.

Isaac cursed the Philistines that day and said, "Cursed be the Philistines for the day of wrath and indignation, from among all the nations; may God make them a mockery and a curse, for wrath and indignation, in the hands of sinful nations and in the hand of the Kittim, who will root them out.
Whoever escapes the sword of the enemy and the Kittim, may the righteous nation root out in judgment from under heaven; for they will be enemies and foes to my sons in their days on the earth.

No remnant will be left to them, nor one who is saved on the day of the wrath of judgment; but they will be for destruction and extermination, so that all the seed of the Philistines may be removed from the face of the earth, and no name at all will remain to them on the earth.

For even if he goes up to heaven, from there he will come down; and even if he makes himself strong on the earth, from there he will be dragged out; and even if he hides among the nations, from there he will be rooted out; and even if he goes down into Sheol, there his judgment will be great, and there will be no peace for him there.

If he goes into captivity, by the hands of those who seek his life they will kill him on the way, and neither name nor seed will be left to him in all the earth; for he will go into an eternal curse."
So it is written and engraved concerning him on the tablets of heaven, to be done to him on the day of judgment, so that he may be rooted out of the earth.

chapters.title: Rebekah Blesses Jacob
chapters.html:
Jubilees 25

1In the second year of this week, in this jubilee, Rebekah called Jacob her son and spoke to him, saying, "My son, do not take a wife for yourself from the daughters of Canaan, as Esau your brother did, who took two wives from the seed of Canaan; and they have made my soul bitter with all their unclean deeds, for all their deeds are fornication and lust, and there is no righteousness at all with them, for it is evil.

2I, my son, love you very much, and my heart and my affection bless you every hour of the day and every watch of the night.

3Now, my son, listen to my voice and do the will of your mother, and do not take a wife for yourself from the daughters of this land, but only from my father's house and from my father's kindred. Take a wife for yourself from my father's house, and God Most High will bless you, and your children will be a righteous generation and your seed holy."

4Then Jacob spoke with Rebekah his mother and said to her, "I, mother, am nine weeks of years old, and I have not known or touched any woman, nor have I betrothed myself, nor do I even think of taking a wife for myself from any seed of the daughters of Canaan.

5For I remember, mother, the words of Abraham our father, what he commanded me: not to take a wife from any seed of the house of Canaan, for I will take a wife for myself from the seed of my father's house and from my kindred.

6I heard long ago, mother, that daughters had been born to Laban your brother, and I have set my heart on them, to take a wife from among them.

7For this reason I have kept myself in my spirit from sinning or being corrupted in any of my ways, all the days of my life; for about lust and fornication Abraham my father gave me many commands.

8With all that he commanded me, these twenty-two years my brother has quarreled with me, and he speaks to me often and says, 'My brother, take as a wife a sister of my two wives'; but I do not want to do as he has done.

9I swear before you, mother, that all the days of my life I will not take a wife for myself from any seed of the daughters of Canaan, and I will not do evil as my brother has done.

10Do not fear, mother; be sure that I will do your will and walk in uprightness, and I will not corrupt my ways forever."

11Then she lifted her face to heaven and spread out the fingers of her hands, and opened her mouth and blessed God Most High, who created heaven and earth, and she gave Him thanks and praise.

12She said, "Blessed be the Lord God, and blessed be His name forever and ever, who has given me Jacob as a pure son and a holy seed; for he is Yours, and Yours his seed will be always, through all the generations forever.

13Bless him, O Lord, and put in my mouth the blessing of righteousness, that I may bless him."

14At that hour the spirit of righteousness came down into her mouth, and she laid both her hands on Jacob's head and said,

15"Blessed are You, O righteous Lord, God of the ages; and may He bless you above all the generations of men. May He give you, my son, the way of righteousness, and reveal righteousness to your seed.

16May He make your sons many in your lifetime, and may they rise up to the number of the months of the year; and may their sons become many and great, beyond the stars of heaven, and may their number be greater than the sand of the sea.

17May He give them this good land, as He said He would give it to Abraham and to his seed after him for all days, and may they hold it as a possession forever.

18May I see born to you, my son, blessed children in my lifetime, and may all your seed be a blessed and holy seed.

19As you have refreshed your mother's spirit in her lifetime, so the womb of her who bore you blesses you; my affection and my breasts bless you, and my mouth and my tongue praise you greatly.

20Grow and spread out on the earth, and may your seed be perfect in all the world, in the joy of heaven and earth; and may your seed rejoice, and on the great day of peace may it have peace.

21May your name and your seed endure to all the ages; and may God Most High be their God, and may the God of righteousness dwell with them, and by them may His sanctuary be built for all the ages.

22Blessed is he who blesses you, and all flesh that curses you falsely, may it be cursed."

23She kissed him and said to him, "May the Lord of the world love you as your mother's heart does, and as her affection rejoices in you and blesses you." Then she ceased from blessing.

Notes

  • vv12, 20, 21 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). The Latin has only the opening words of v1.

  • v1 the date — the second year of the first week of the forty-fourth jubilee (24:21) is 2109, the year of Abraham's death by 22:1. Jacob, born in 2046 (19:13), is sixty-three: nine weeks of years, as he says in v4.

  • vv1–3 "do not take a wife… from the daughters of Canaan" — in Genesis Rebekah says it to Isaac, not to Jacob: I am disgusted with my life because of the daughters of Heth (Genesis 27:46); and Isaac sends Jacob away with the charge, You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan. Rise, go to Paddan-aram… from the daughters of Laban your mother's brother (Genesis 28:1–2). Esau's two wives: Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite. They were a bitterness of spirit to Isaac and to Rebekah (Genesis 26:34–35). v8 "these twenty-two years" — Esau married at forty (Genesis 26:34).

  • vv4–10 Jacob's answer — Jacob keeps Abraham's charge (20:4; 22:20) and swears to his mother. v6 "the daughters of Laban" — Leah and Rachel, whom he will marry in chapter 28.

  • vv11–23 Rebekah's blessing — Genesis gives Rebekah no blessing of her own; here the spirit of righteousness comes into her mouth (v14), as a spirit comes on a prophet, and she lays both hands on Jacob's head. v16 "to the number of the months of the year" — twelve, the twelve sons of Jacob. v22 "Blessed is he who blesses you, and all flesh that curses you… may it be cursed" — Isaac's words over Jacob in Genesis 27:29: Those who curse you, cursed; and those who bless you, blessed.

Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Jacob Receives Isaac's Blessing
chapters.html:
Jubilees 26

1In the seventh year of this week Isaac called Esau, his elder son, and said to him, "My son, I am old, and my eyes are too dim to see, and I do not know the day of my death.

2Now take your hunting gear, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field and hunt, and catch game for me, my son; and make me food such as my soul loves, and bring it to me, so that I may eat, and my soul may bless you before I die."

3Rebekah was listening as Isaac spoke to Esau.

4Esau went out early to the field to hunt and catch game and bring it to his father.

5Rebekah called Jacob her son and said to him, "I heard Isaac your father speaking with Esau your brother, saying, 'Hunt for me and make me food, and bring it to me, and let me eat, and I will bless you before the Lord before I die.'

6Now, my son, listen to my voice in what I command you: go to your flock and take me two good kids of the goats, and I will make them into food for your father, such as he loves; and you will bring it to your father and he will eat, so that he may bless you before the Lord before he dies."

7Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, "Mother, I will not hold back anything my father would eat and that would please him; but I am afraid, mother, that he will know my voice and want to touch me.

8You know that I am smooth, and Esau my brother is hairy, and I will be in his eyes like one who does evil, and I will do a deed he did not command me, and he will be angry with me, and I will bring on myself a curse and not a blessing."

9Rebekah his mother said to him, "Upon me be your curse, my son. Only listen to my voice."

10Jacob listened to the voice of Rebekah his mother, and he went and took two tender and good kids of the goats and brought them to his mother; and his mother made them into food, such as he loved.

11Rebekah took the fine garments of Esau, her elder son, which were with her in her house, and clothed Jacob, her younger son; and she put the skins of the kids on his hands, and on the bare parts of his body, and on his neck.

12She gave the stew and the bread that she had made into the hand of Jacob her son.

13He went in to his father and said, "I am your son. I have done as you told me. Rise, sit and eat of what I have caught, father, so that your soul may bless me."

14Isaac said to his son, "How is it that you found it so quickly, my son?"

15Jacob said, "Because your God made it happen before me."

16Isaac said to him, "Come near, and let me feel you, my son, whether you are my son Esau or not."

17Jacob came near to Isaac his father, and he felt him and said,

18"The voice is the voice of Jacob, and the hands are the hands of Esau." He did not recognize him, for it was a turning from heaven to lead his spirit aside; and Isaac did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like the hands of Esau, so that he might bless him.

19He said, "Are you my son Esau?" He said, "I am your son." He said, "Bring it near to me, and let me eat of what you have caught, my son, so that my soul may bless you."

20He brought it near to him, and he ate; and he brought him wine, and he drank.

21Isaac his father said to him, "Come near and kiss me, my son." He came near and kissed him.

22He smelled the smell of his garments, and blessed him and said, "The smell of my son is like the smell of a field that the Lord has blessed.

23May the Lord give to you, and multiply you, from the dew of heaven and from the dew of the earth, and may He multiply for you plenty of grain and oil; let nations serve you, and peoples bow down to you.

24Be lord over your brothers, and let your mother's sons bow down to you; and may all the blessings with which the Lord has blessed me, and blessed Abraham my father, be yours and your seed's forever. Cursed be he who curses you, and blessed be he who blesses you."

25And it came to pass, after Isaac had finished blessing his son Jacob, and when Jacob had gone out from Isaac his father, that he hid himself; and Esau his brother came in from his hunting.

26He too made food and brought it to his father, and said to his father, "Let my father rise and eat of my game, so that your soul may bless me."

27Isaac his father said to him, "Who are you?" He said to him, "I am your firstborn, Esau your son. I have done as you commanded me."

28Isaac was very greatly astonished, and said, "Who is it, then, who hunted and caught game for me and brought it, and I ate of it all before you came, and blessed him? He shall be blessed, and all his seed forever."

29And it came to pass, when Esau heard the words of his father Isaac, that he cried out with a great and very bitter cry, and said to his father, "Bless me — me also, father!"

30He said to him, "Your brother came with guile and took your blessings." He said, "Now I know why his name is called Jacob. He has supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright, and now he has taken away my blessing."

31He said, "Have you not kept back a blessing for me, father?" Isaac answered and said to Esau, "I have made him your lord, and all his brothers I have given to him as servants, and with plenty of grain and wine and oil I have strengthened him. What now shall I do for you, my son?"

32Esau said to Isaac his father, "Is your blessing only one, father? Bless me — me also, father!" Esau lifted up his voice and wept.

33Isaac answered and said to him, "Away from the dew of the earth will be your dwelling, and away from the dew of heaven above.

34By your sword you will live, and you will serve your brother, and he will be your lord; and when you refuse and loosen his yoke from your neck, then you will sin a complete sin to death, and all your seed will be rooted out from under heaven."

35Esau kept threatening Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him, and he said in his heart, "Now let the days of mourning for my father come, and I will kill my brother Jacob."

Notes

  • vv10, 11, 21, 23, 25, 26, 30, 31, 33, 34 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v8 to v23, has vv10, 11 and 21 too. v33 — the whole verse is missing from both Beta Masaheft texts; without it they never give Isaac's answer to Esau's tears. "away from the dew of the earth" — ʾəm-ṭala, from the dew: the Ge'ez preposition, like the Hebrew min of Genesis 27:39, can mean out of or away from; see the note on Genesis 27:39. v34 "when you refuse and loosen his yoke" — the Greek has whenever you cast down and loosen his yoke from your neck.

  • vv1–35 the stolen blessing — Genesis 27:1–41, retold in order, in this project's wording where the Ge'ez allows: The voice is the voice of Jacob, and the hands are the hands of Esau (27:22); Upon me be your curse, my son (27:13); Let the days of mourning for my father draw near, and I will kill Jacob my brother (27:41).

  • vv13, 19 "I am your son" — in Genesis 27:19 Jacob says I am Esau your firstborn, and in 27:24, to Are you really my son Esau?, he answers I am. In Jubilees he says only I am your son both times: he does not speak the lie in so many words.

  • v18 "a turning from heaven to lead his spirit aside" — Genesis 27:23 says only that he did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy. Jubilees adds that heaven itself turned Isaac's mind aside, so that the blessing went where it was meant to go (19:16–29; 22:10–24). The Latin has the same, a turning away from heaven to distract his spirit.

  • v1 the date — the seventh year of this week, the first week of the forty-fourth jubilee (24:21; 25:1), is 2114. Jacob, born in 2046, is sixty-eight.

  • v23 "plenty of grain and oil" — Genesis 27:28 has abundance of grain and new wine.

  • v34 "you will sin a complete sin to death" — Genesis 27:40 ends you will tear his yoke off your neck. Jubilees, in the Asmara printing and in Charles, adds that Esau's breaking free will be his final sin (compare 21:22).

Be lord over your brothers, and let your mother's sons bow down to you; and may all the blessings with which the Lord has blessed me, and blessed Abraham my father, be yours and your seed's forever. Cursed be he who curses you, and blessed be he who blesses you."
And it came to pass, after Isaac had finished blessing his son Jacob, and when Jacob had gone out from Isaac his father, that he hid himself; and Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
He too made food and brought it to his father, and said to his father, "Let my father rise and eat of my game, so that your soul may bless me."
Isaac his father said to him, "Who are you?" He said to him, "I am your firstborn, Esau your son. I have done as you commanded me."

Isaac was very greatly astonished, and said, "Who is it, then, who hunted and caught game for me and brought it, and I ate of it all before you came, and blessed him? He shall be blessed, and all his seed forever."
And it came to pass, when Esau heard the words of his father Isaac, that he cried out with a great and very bitter cry, and said to his father, "Bless me — me also, father!"

He said to him, "Your brother came with guile and took your blessings." He said, "Now I know why his name is called Jacob. He has supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright, and now he has taken away my blessing."

He said, "Have you not kept back a blessing for me, father?" Isaac answered and said to Esau, "I have made him your lord, and all his brothers I have given to him as servants, and with plenty of grain and wine and oil I have strengthened him. What now shall I do for you, my son?"
Esau said to Isaac his father, "Is your blessing only one, father? Bless me — me also, father!" Esau lifted up his voice and wept.
Isaac answered and said to him, "Away from the dew of the earth will be your dwelling, and away from the dew of heaven above.

By your sword you will live, and you will serve your brother, and he will be your lord; and when you refuse and loosen his yoke from your neck, then you will sin a complete sin to death, and all your seed will be rooted out from under heaven."

Esau kept threatening Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him, and he said in his heart, "Now let the days of mourning for my father come, and I will kill my brother Jacob."

chapters.title: Jacob Sent Away, and the Stairway at Bethel
chapters.html:
Jubilees 27

1The words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah in a dream; and Rebekah sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said to him,

2"Esau your brother is bearing a grudge against you, to kill you.

3Now, my son, listen to my voice: rise and flee to Laban my brother, to Harran, and stay with him a few days, until your brother's anger turns and he puts away his anger from you and forgets all that you have done to him; then I will send and bring you from there."

4Jacob said, "I am not afraid. If he wants to kill me, I will kill him."

5She said to him, "Let me not be bereaved of both my sons in one day."

6Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, "You know that my father has grown old, and I see that his eyes are dim; and if I leave him, it will be evil in his eyes, because I leave him and go away from you; and my father will be angry and will curse me. I will not go; only when he sends me will I go."

7Rebekah said to Jacob, "I will go in and speak to him, and he will send you away."

8Rebekah went in and said to Isaac, "I loathe my life because of the two daughters of Heth whom Esau has taken as wives; and if Jacob takes a wife from the daughters of the land such as these, why should I live any longer? For the daughters of Canaan are evil."

9Isaac called Jacob his son, and blessed him and charged him, and said to him,

10"Do not take a wife for yourself from any of the daughters of Canaan. Rise, go to Mesopotamia, to the house of Bethuel, your mother's father, and take a wife for yourself from there, from the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.

11May God Almighty bless you, and make you grow and multiply you, and may you become a company of nations; and may He give the blessings of my father Abraham to you and to your seed after you, so that you may inherit the land where you have lived as a guest, and all the land that the Lord gave to Abraham. Go, my son, in peace."

12Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Mesopotamia, to Laban the son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob's mother.

13And it came to pass, after Jacob had set out to go to Mesopotamia, that Rebekah's spirit grieved after her son, and she wept.

14Isaac said to Rebekah, "My sister, do not weep for my son, for he goes in peace, and in peace he will return.

15God Most High will keep him from all evil and will be with him, and will not forsake him all his days.

16For I know that his ways will prosper in everything, wherever he goes, until he returns to us in peace and we see him in peace.

17Do not fear for him, my sister, for he is upright in his way, and he is a whole man; he is faithful, and he will not perish. Do not weep."

18Isaac comforted Rebekah about Jacob her son, and he blessed him.

19Jacob went out from the Well of the Oath to go to Harran, in the first year of the second week of the forty-fourth jubilee, and he came to Luz, which is on the mountain, that is Bethel, on the new moon of the first month of this week. He came to the place at evening, and turned from the road to the west of the path that night, and slept there, for the sun had set.

20He took one of the stones of that place and set it under the tree, and he was traveling alone.

21He dreamed that night: a stairway was set up on the earth, and its top reached to heaven; the angels of God were going up and coming down on it, and the Lord was standing on it.

22He spoke with Jacob and said, "I am the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac. The land on which you are sleeping — to you I will give it, and to your seed after you.

23Your seed will be like the sand of the earth, and you will increase to the west and the east and the north and the south; and in you and in your seed all the tribes of the earth will be blessed.

24I will be with you and keep you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land in peace; for I will not leave you until I have done all that I have told you."

25Jacob woke from his sleep and said, "Truly this place is the house of the Lord, and I did not know it." He was afraid and said, "How fearful is this place! It is nothing but the house of the Lord, and this is the gate of heaven."

26Jacob rose early in the morning, and took the stone he had set at his head, and set it up as a pillar for a sign, and poured oil on its top; and he called the name of that place Bethel, but at first the name of the land was Luz.

27Jacob prayed a prayer to the Lord, saying, "If the Lord is with me and keeps me on this way that I am going, and gives me bread to eat and clothing to wear, and I return to my father's house in peace, then the Lord will be my God; and this stone, which I have set up as a pillar for a sign in this place, will be the house of the Lord; and of all that You give me, I will give the tenth to You, my God."

Notes

  • vv1, 6, 8, 15, 21, 23, 27 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v11 to v23, has vv15, 21 and 23 too. v21 "the Lord was standing on it" — so the Asmara printing, yəqawwəm; the Latin has resting. Genesis 28:13: Here, the LORD standing over him.

  • vv1–18 Jacob sent away — Genesis 27:42–28:5: until your brother's anger turns from you, and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send and take you from there. Why should I be bereaved of both of you in one day? (27:45). Jubilees adds Jacob's answer, If he wants to kill me, I will kill him (v4), and his refusal to leave his blind father unless his father sends him (v6). v10 "Mesopotamia" — so the Ge'ez; Genesis 28:2 has Paddan-aram. v11 "God Almighty… a company of nations" — Genesis 28:3–4: May God Almighty bless you, and make you fruitful and multiply you, and you shall become an assembly of peoples. May He give you the blessing of Abraham. vv14–17 "My sister" — Isaac's name for his wife; Genesis gives Isaac no words of comfort to Rebekah.

  • v19 the date — the first year of the second week of the forty-fourth jubilee is 43 × 49 + 7 + 1 = 2115; the Latin has the second year. Jacob, born in 2046, is sixty-nine.

  • vv19–27 the stairway at Bethel — Genesis 28:10–22: here, a stairway set on the earth, and its head reaching to the heavens. Here, messengers of God going up and coming down on it… How fearful is this place! This is nothing but the house of God, and this is the gate of the heavens. Jesus takes up the scene: you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God going up and coming down on the Son of Man (John 1:51). v23 "the sand of the earth" — so the Ge'ez and the Latin; Genesis 28:14 has the dust of the earth. v25 "Jacob woke" — the EOTC has wa-noma, "and he slept"; the English follows Charles and the sense. v27 "I will give the tenth to You" — the vow Jacob pays at Bethel in 32:2.

Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Leah and Rachel, and the Birth of Jacob's Children
chapters.html:
Jubilees 28

1He lifted his feet and went to the land of the east, to Laban, Rebekah's brother; and he stayed with him and served him for Rachel his daughter one week.

2In the first year of the third week he said to him, "Give me my wife, for whom I have served you seven years." Laban said to Jacob, "I will give you your wife."

3Laban made a feast, and took Leah his elder daughter and gave her to Jacob as a wife, and gave her Zilpah his maidservant as a maid; and Jacob did not know, for he thought she was Rachel.

4He went in to her, and here — she was Leah. Jacob was angry with Laban and said to him, "Why have you done this to me? Did I not serve you for Rachel and not for Leah? Why have you wronged me?

5Take your daughter, and I will go, for you have done evil to me." For Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah; for Leah's eyes were weak, though her form was very lovely, and Rachel's eyes were beautiful, and her form beautiful and very lovely.

6Laban said to Jacob, "It is not done so in our land, to give the younger before the elder." It is not right to do this; for so it is ordained and written on the tablets of heaven, that no one should give his younger daughter before the elder, but one gives the elder first and after her the younger; and against the man who does so they write down guilt in heaven, and no one who does this thing is righteous, for this deed is evil before the Lord.

7You too, command the sons of Israel not to do this thing: let them neither take nor give the younger before they have given the elder, for it is very wicked.

8Laban said to Jacob, "Let the seven days of the feast for this one pass, and I will give you Rachel, so that you serve me another seven years, pasturing my sheep as you did in the first week."

9On the day when the seven days of Leah's feast had passed, Laban gave Rachel to Jacob, that he might serve him another seven years; and he gave Rachel Bilhah, Zilpah's sister, as a maid.

10He served another seven years for Rachel, for Leah had been given to him for nothing.

11The Lord opened Leah's womb, and she conceived and bore Jacob a son, and he called his name Reuben, on the fourteenth of the ninth month, in the first year of the third week.

12But Rachel's womb was closed, for the Lord saw that Leah was hated and Rachel loved.

13Jacob went in to Leah again, and she conceived and bore Jacob a second son, and he called his name Simeon, on the twenty-first of the tenth month, in the third year of this week.

14Jacob went in to Leah again, and she conceived and bore him a third son, and he called his name Levi[, on the new moon of the first month, in the sixth year of this week].

15Once more he went in to her, and she bore a fourth son; and he called his name Judah, on the fifteenth of the third month, in the first year of the fourth week.

16In all this Rachel was jealous of Leah, for she did not bear; and she said to Jacob, "Give me children." Jacob said, "Have I withheld from you the fruit of your womb? Have I forsaken you?"

17When Rachel saw that Leah had borne Jacob four sons, Reuben and Simeon and Levi and Judah, Rachel said to Jacob, "Go in to Bilhah my maid, and she will conceive and bear a son for me."

18[She gave Bilhah her maid as a wife.] He went in, and she conceived and bore him a son; and she called his name Dan, on the ninth of the sixth month, in the sixth year of the third week.

19Jacob went in again to Bilhah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a second son, and Rachel called his name Naphtali, on the fifth of the seventh month, in the second year of the fourth week.

20When Leah saw that she had become barren and was not bearing, she too was jealous of Rachel, and she too gave Zilpah her maid to Jacob as a wife; and she conceived and bore a son, and Leah called his name Gad, on the twelfth of the eighth month, in the third year of the fourth week.

21He went in to her again, and she conceived and bore him a second son, and Leah called his name Asher, on the second of the eleventh month, in the fifth year of the fourth week.

22Jacob went in to Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a son, and he called his name Issachar, on the fourth of the fifth month, in the fourth year of the fourth week; and she gave him to a wet nurse.

23Jacob went in to her again, and she conceived and bore two, a son and a daughter, and she called the son's name Zebulun and the daughter's name Dinah[, on the seventh of the seventh month, in the sixth year of the fourth week].

24The Lord had mercy on Rachel and opened her womb; and she conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Joseph, on the first day of the fourth month, in the sixth year of this fourth week.

25In the days when Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, "Give me my wives and my sons, and let me go to my father Isaac and make a house for myself; for I have completed the years in which I served you for your two daughters, and I will go to my father's house."

26Laban said to Jacob, "Stay with me for your wages, and pasture my flock for me again, and take your wages."

27They agreed with each other that he would give him as his wages every one of the lambs and kids born dark, speckled, and marked with white; that would be his wages.

28All the flocks bore speckled young, all of them marked, spotted and dark and speckled; and again the flocks bore young like themselves; and all that were marked were Jacob's, and those without a mark were Laban's.

29Jacob's possessions grew very great, and he acquired cattle and sheep and donkeys and camels, and menservants and maidservants.

30Laban and his sons were jealous of Jacob, and Laban took back his sheep from him and watched him with evil intent.

Notes

  • vv4–7, 11, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 22, 24 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v16 to v27, has vv17–24 too. Words in [brackets] are in no Ge'ez text here and follow Charles's English: the opening of v18; the date of Levi's birth in v14, which the Asmara file skips; and the date of Zebulun and Dinah (v23). There the Asmara printing reads, like the Latin, in the seventh month of the seventh year, in the sixth week of the forty-fourth jubilee — 2149, after Joseph's birth and after Jacob leaves Laban (29:5) — so the date follows Charles and the book's own sequence. Without these verses the EOTC never names Judah or Dan, never tells of Joseph's birth, and gives only four of the birth dates.

  • vv1–10 Leah and Rachel — Genesis 29:1–30: Jacob lifted his feet and went to the land of the sons of the east… And it came to pass in the morning — and here, it was Leah… It is not done so in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn (29:1, 25–26). v5 "Leah's eyes were weak" — Genesis 29:17 has Leah's eyes were soft. vv6–7 the law of the elder daughter — Laban's excuse becomes a law of the tablets of heaven, given to Israel through Moses.

  • vv11–24 the children — Genesis 29:31–30:24. Jubilees dates every birth. In this book's reckoning the third week of the forty-fourth jubilee begins in 2122 and the fourth in 2129, so the twelve children are born in thirteen years: Reuben in 2122, Simeon in 2124, Levi and Dan in 2127, Judah in 2129, Naphtali in 2130, Gad in 2131, Issachar in 2132, Asher in 2133, and Zebulun, Dinah and Joseph in 2134. v16 "Give me children" — Genesis 30:1–2: Give me sons — and if not, I am dead… Am I in the place of God, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb? v23 "Zebulun… Dinah" — born together here, as twins; Genesis 30:20–21 tells them one after the other.

  • vv25–30 the wages — Genesis 30:25–43: every speckled and spotted sheep, and every dark one among the lambs, and the spotted and speckled among the goats. That shall be my wages (30:32). Jubilees leaves out Jacob's peeled rods (30:37–42): the flocks simply bear marked young. v30 "watched him with evil intent" — Genesis 31:2: Jacob saw that Laban's face was not toward him as yesterday and the day before.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Jacob Leaves Laban, and Provides for His Parents
chapters.html:
Jubilees 29

1And it came to pass, after Rachel had borne Joseph, that Laban went to shear his sheep, for they were three days' journey away from him.

2Jacob saw that Laban was going to shear his sheep; and Jacob called Leah and Rachel and spoke kindly to them, that they should come with him to the land of Canaan.

3For he told them how he had seen everything in a dream, and all that He had told him, that he should return to his father's house; and they said, "Wherever you go, we will go with you."

4Jacob blessed the God of Isaac his father and the God of Abraham his father's father; and he rose and set his wives and his children on the animals, and took all his possessions and crossed the river, and came to the land of Gilead; and Jacob hid his purpose from Laban and did not tell him.

5In the seventh year of the fourth week Jacob turned toward Gilead, in the first month, on the twenty-first of it; and Laban pursued him and overtook Jacob on the mountain of Gilead in the third month, on the thirteenth of it.

6The Lord did not let him harm Jacob, for He appeared to him in a dream by night; and Laban spoke to Jacob.

7On the fifteenth of those days Jacob made a feast for Laban and for all who came with him; and Jacob swore to Laban that day, and Laban to Jacob, that neither would cross over to the other with evil on the mountain of Gilead.

8He made a heap there for a witness; for this reason the name of that place is called the Heap of Witness, after this heap.

9Before, they used to call the land of Gilead the land of the Rephaim, for it is the land of the Rephaim; and the Rephaim were born there, giants whose height was ten cubits, and nine, and eight, down to seven cubits.

10Their dwellings were from the land of the sons of Ammon to Mount Hermon, and the seats of their kingdom were Karnaim and Ashtaroth and Edrei and Misur and Beon.

11The Lord destroyed them for the evil of their deeds, for they were very fierce; and in their place He made the Amorites live, evil and sinful, so that no nation is so hateful; for they filled up all their sins, and they no longer have length of life on the earth.

12Jacob sent Laban away, and he went to Mesopotamia, the land of the east[; and Jacob turned back to the land of Gilead].

13He crossed the Jabbok in the ninth month, on the eleventh of it, he and his eleven sons; and on that day Esau his brother came to him and was reconciled to him, and went away from him to the land of Seir; and Jacob lived in tents.

14In the first year of the fifth week of this jubilee he crossed the Jordan and lived beyond the Jordan, and he pastured his sheep from the Sea of the Heap to Beth-shan, and to Dothan, and to the forest of Akrabbim.

15He sent to his father Isaac from all his possessions: clothing and food, meat and drink, milk and butter and cheese, and some dates of the valley;

16and to his mother Rebekah too, four times a year, between the seasons of the months — between plowing and reaping, between autumn and the rains, and between winter and spring — to the tower of Abraham.

17For Isaac had returned from the Well of the Oath and gone up to the tower of his father Abraham, and lived there, apart from Esau his son.

18For in the days when Jacob went to Mesopotamia, Esau took for himself a wife, Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, and gathered all his father's flocks and his wives, and went up and lived on Mount Seir, and left Isaac his father at the Well of the Oath alone.

Notes

  • vv2, 3, 4, 9, 11, 13, 18, 20 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v8 on, has most of them too. Without the end of v13 the EOTC never tells of Jacob's meeting with Esau. Words in [brackets] (v12) are in no Ge'ez text here; they follow the Latin.

  • vv1–8 the flight from Laban — Genesis 31. Jubilees tells in a few verses what Genesis tells at length, and leaves out Rachel's theft of the household gods (31:19, 30–35). v5 the dates — the seventh year of the fourth week is 2135, the year after Joseph's birth (28:24). v8 "the Heap of Witness" — Genesis 31:48: Laban said, "This heap is a witness between me and you today."   • vv9–11 the land of the Rephaim — Genesis 14:5 names the Rephaim in Ashteroth-karnaim; Deuteronomy 3:11 their last king: Only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim; his bed was a bed of iron… nine cubits its length. v9 "the land of the Rephaim" — the EOTC writes the first as the land of Raphael, then the land of the Rephaim.

  • vv12–13 Esau — Genesis 32–33 tells of Jacob's fear, the wrestling at Peniel, the new name Israel, and the meeting with Esau; Jubilees keeps only the crossing of the Jabbok and, in the Latin, the reconciliation on the same day. v12 — the Greek dates Jacob's return to the 153rd year of Isaac.

  • v14 the date and the places — the first year of the fifth week is 2136. "the Sea of the Heap" — so Charles; the Latin has the Salt Sea.

  • vv15–20 the tower of Abraham — Jacob, though living apart, provides for both parents four times a year; Esau takes his father's flocks and leaves him. v18 "Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael" — Genesis 28:9: Esau went to Ishmael, and took Mahalath daughter of Ishmael son of Abraham.
