chapters.title: Dinah, Shechem, and Levi's Zeal
chapters.html:
Jubilees 30

1In the first year of the sixth week he went up to Salem, east of Shechem, in peace, in the fourth month.

2There they carried off Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, into the house of Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, and he lay with her and defiled her; and she was a young girl, a daughter of twelve years.

3He begged her father that she be given to him as a wife, and her brothers, as a wife for him; and Jacob and his sons were indignant against the men of Shechem, because they had defiled Dinah their sister, and they spoke to them deceitfully and mocked them with guile.

4Simeon and Levi came to Shechem unexpectedly and executed judgment on all the men of Shechem, and killed every man they found in it, and did not leave a single one in it; they killed them all in torment, because they had dishonored Dinah their sister.

5Let it not be done so again from now on, that a daughter of Israel is defiled; for judgment was ordained against them in heaven, that they should destroy all the men of Shechem with the sword, because they had done a shameful thing in Israel.

6The Lord gave them into the hands of the sons of Jacob, to root them out with the sword and to execute judgment on them, and that it might no longer be in Israel that a virgin of Israel is defiled.

7If there is a man in Israel who wants to give his daughter or his sister to any man of the seed of the nations, he shall surely die, and they shall stone him with stones, for he has done a sin and a shameful thing in Israel; and the woman shall be burned with fire, because she has defiled the name of her father's house; she shall be rooted out of Israel.

8Let no prostitute and no uncleanness be found in Israel, all the days of the generations of the earth, for Israel is holy to the Lord; and any man who defiles it shall die, stoned with stones.

9For so it is ordained and written on the tablets of heaven about all the seed of Israel: whoever defiles it shall surely die, and they shall stone him with stones.

10To this law there is no limit of days, and no remission, and no atonement at all; but the man who has defiled his daughter shall be rooted out in the middle of all Israel, because he has given of his seed to Molech and sinned so as to defile it.

11You, Moses, command the sons of Israel and testify to them that they should not give any of their daughters to the nations, and should not take any of the daughters of the nations, for it is abominable before the Lord.

12For this reason I have written for you in the words of the law all the deeds of the Shechemites, which they did against Dinah, and how the sons of Jacob spoke, saying, "We will not give our daughter to a man who has a foreskin, for that is a disgrace to us."

13It is a disgrace to Israel, to those who give and to those who take from the daughters of the nations, for it is unclean and abominable to Israel.

14Israel will not be clean of this uncleanness while one has a wife from the daughters of the nations, or has given one of his daughters to a man of any of the nations.

15For it is plague upon plague and curse upon curse, and every judgment and plague and curse will come on anyone who does this deed; and if he transgresses and despises it, committing abomination and defiling the sanctuary of God, and those who defile His holy name, the whole people will be judged together for all his abominations.

16There will be no respect of persons and no partiality, and no receiving from his hand of fruit and offering and burnt offering and fat, or of the fragrance of a soothing aroma, so as to accept it; and so it will be with every man or woman in Israel who defiles the sanctuary.

17For this reason I have commanded you, saying, "Testify this testimony to Israel: see what happened to the Shechemites and their sons, how they were given into the hands of two sons of Jacob, and they killed them in judgment; and it was counted to them for truth, and written down for them as righteousness."

18The seed of Levi was chosen for the priesthood and to be Levites, to minister before the Lord as we do, all the days; and Levi and his sons are blessed forever, for he was zealous for the truth, to execute judgment and vengeance on all who rose up against Israel.

19So they bring up for him, as a testimony on the tablets of heaven, blessing and righteousness before the God of all.

20We remember the righteousness that a man has done in his life, at all the times of the year; up to a thousand generations they bring it up, and it comes to him and to his generations after him; and he has been written on the tablets of heaven as a friend and a righteous man.

21All this account I have written for you, and have commanded you to tell the sons of Israel not to sin, nor transgress the ordinances, nor break the covenant ordained for them, but to do it and be written down as friends.

22But if they transgress and do any of the ways of uncleanness, they will be written on the tablets of heaven as enemies, and they will be blotted out of the book of the living and written in the book of those who will be destroyed, and with those who will be rooted out of the earth.

23On the day the sons of Jacob killed Shechem, a writing went up for them in heaven, that they had done righteousness and uprightness and vengeance on the sinners, and it was written for a blessing.

24They brought Dinah their sister out of the house of Shechem, and they took captive all that was in Shechem, their sheep and their cattle and their donkeys, and all their goods and all their flocks, and brought it all to Jacob their father.

25He spoke with them about their having killed the city, for he feared those who lived in the land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites.

26The dread of the Lord was on all the cities around Shechem, and they did not rise to pursue the sons of Jacob, for terror had fallen on them.

Notes

  • vv2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers the whole chapter, has them too.

  • vv1–4 Dinah and Shechem — Genesis 34. v1 "to Salem… in peace" — Genesis 33:18: Jacob came in one piece to the city of Shechem; the Hebrew shalem, "whole, in one piece," is read here as a place, Salem. The date is 2143. v2 "a daughter of twelve years" — the Latin; by this book's dates, Dinah was born in 2134 (28:23) and is nine. v12 "a man who has a foreskin" — Genesis 34:14: We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to a man who has a foreskin, for that is a disgrace to us. Jubilees leaves out the circumcision of the men of Shechem (Genesis 34:15–24), the deceit that let the brothers kill them.

  • vv5–17 the law against marrying outside Israel — the angel makes the story a law on the tablets of heaven. v10 "given of his seed to Molech" — Leviticus 20:2: Any man of the sons of Israel… who gives any of his children to Molech shall surely be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him. The Latin has to a foreigner for to Molech.

  • vv17–23 Levi's zeal — in Genesis Jacob condemns the deed: You have muddied me, to make me stink among those who dwell in the land (34:30); and at his death, Simeon and Levi are brothers; instruments of violence are their trade… Cursed be their anger (49:5, 7). Jubilees counts it as righteousness and makes it the reason Levi is chosen for the priesthood, as Phinehas was for his zeal: because he was jealous for his God and made atonement for the sons of Israel (Numbers 25:13), and it was counted to him as righteousness, from generation to generation, forever (Psalm 106:31). v22 "blotted out of the book of the living" — Psalm 69:29: Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.

  • vv25–26 Jacob's fear — Genesis 34:30 and 35:5: A terror of God was on the cities around them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Isaac Blesses Levi and Judah
chapters.html:
Jubilees 31

1On the new moon of the month Jacob spoke to all the people of his house, saying, "Purify yourselves and change your clothes, and let us rise and go up to Bethel, where I made my vow to Him on the day I fled from the face of Esau my brother, because He has been with me and brought me back into this land in peace; and put away the foreign gods that are among you."

2They gave up the foreign gods, and what was in their ears and on their necks, and the idols that Rachel had stolen from Laban her father she gave, all of them, to Jacob; and he burned them and broke them to pieces and destroyed them, and hid them under an oak that is in the land of Shechem.

3On the new moon of the seventh month he went up to Bethel, and built an altar at the place where he had slept, and set up a pillar there; and he sent word to his father Isaac to come to him to his sacrifice, and to his mother Rebekah.

4Isaac said, "Let my son Jacob come, and let me see him before I die."

5Jacob went to his father Isaac and to his mother Rebekah, to the house of his father Abraham, and took two of his sons with him, Levi and Judah; and he came to his father Isaac and to his mother Rebekah.

6Rebekah came out of the tower to the gate of the tower to kiss Jacob and embrace him; for her spirit had revived when she heard, "Jacob your son has come"; and she kissed him.

7She saw his two sons, and she recognized them, and said to him, "Are these your sons, my son?" She embraced them and kissed them and blessed them, saying, "In you the seed of Abraham will become famous, and you will be a blessing on the earth."

8Jacob went in to Isaac his father, into his chamber where he lay; and his two sons were with him; and he took his father's hand and bent down and kissed him, and Isaac clung to the neck of Jacob his son and wept on his neck.

9The darkness passed from Isaac's eyes, and he saw the two sons of Jacob, Levi and Judah, and he said, "Are these your sons, my son? For they are like you."

10He told him that they were truly his sons: "Truly you have seen that they are truly my sons."

11They came near to him, and he turned and kissed them and embraced them both together.

12The spirit of prophecy came down into his mouth, and he took Levi by his right hand and Judah by his left.

13He turned to Levi first and began to bless him first, and said to him, "May the Lord of all bless you, He, the Lord of all the ages, you and your sons forever and ever.

14May the Lord give to you and to your seed greatness and great glory, and bring you and your seed near to Himself from all flesh, to serve in His sanctuary like the angels of the presence and like the holy ones; and like them the seed of your sons will be, for glory and greatness and holiness, and may He make them great for all the ages.

15They will be princes and judges and chiefs to all the seed of the sons of Jacob; they will speak the word of the Lord in righteousness, and they will judge all His judgments in righteousness; and they will declare My ways to Jacob and My paths to Israel. The blessing of God will be given in their mouth, that they may bless all the seed of the beloved.

16Your mother called your name Levi, and truly she called your name: you will be joined to the Lord, and be the companion of all the sons of Jacob. Your table will be yours, and you and your sons will eat of it; and your table will be full forever, and your food will not fail forever and ever.

17All who hate you will fall down before you, and all your enemies will be rooted out and perish. Blessed is he who blesses you, and every nation that curses you will be cursed."

18To Judah he said, "May the Lord give you power and strength to trample all who hate you. Be a prince, you and one of your sons, over the sons of Jacob; may your name and the name of your sons go out and travel through all the earth and the cities. Then the nations will fear before your face, and all the nations will tremble, and all the peoples will tremble.

19In you will be the help of Jacob, and in you the salvation of Israel will be found.

20On the day you sit on the throne of the honor of your righteousness, there will be great peace for all the seed of the sons of the beloved. Blessed is he who blesses you; and all who hate you and afflict you and curse you will be rooted out and destroyed from the earth, and be cursed."

21He turned and kissed him again and embraced him, and rejoiced greatly, for he had seen the sons of Jacob his son in truth.

22He went out from between his feet, and fell down and bowed down to him, and he blessed them; and he rested there with Isaac his father that night, and they ate and drank with joy.

23He laid the two sons of Jacob to sleep, one on his right and one on his left, and it was counted to him as righteousness.

24Jacob told his father everything in the night, how the Lord had shown him great mercy, and had prospered him in all his ways and protected him from all evil.

25Isaac blessed the God of his father Abraham, who had not withdrawn His mercy and His righteousness from the son of His servant Isaac.

26In the morning Jacob told his father Isaac the vow he had vowed to the Lord, and the vision he had seen, and that he had built an altar, and that everything was ready for the sacrifice to be made before the Lord as he had vowed, and that he had come to set him on a donkey.

27Isaac said to Jacob his son, "I cannot come with you, for I am old and cannot bear the way. Go, my son, in peace, for I am one hundred and sixty-five years old this day; I am no longer able to journey. Set your mother on a donkey, and let her go with you.

28I know, my son, that you have come on my account; and blessed be this day on which you have seen me alive, and I also have seen you, my son.

29Prosper, and fulfill the vow you have vowed, and do not put off your vow, for the vow will be required of you; now hurry to perform it, and may He who made all things, to whom you have vowed the vow, be pleased."

30He said to Rebekah, "Go with Jacob your son." Rebekah went with her son Jacob, and Deborah her nurse with her, and they came to Bethel.

31Jacob remembered the prayer with which his father had blessed him and his two sons, Levi and Judah, and he rejoiced and blessed the God of his fathers, Abraham and Isaac.

32He said, "Now I know that I have an eternal hope, and my sons too, before the God of all." So it is ordained concerning the two of them, and they bring it up for them as an eternal testimony on the tablets of heaven, how Isaac blessed them.

Notes

  • vv3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 27, 28, 29, 30 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v9 to v18 and from v29 on, has many of them too.

  • vv1–3 back to Bethel — Genesis 35:1–4: Remove the foreign gods that are among you, and purify yourselves, and change your clothes… They gave Jacob all the foreign gods that were in their hand, and the rings that were in their ears, and Jacob hid them under the terebinth that is by Shechem. Jubilees has Jacob burn and break them first.

  • vv4–32 the visit to Isaac — Genesis tells nothing of it. In Jubilees Isaac's blindness lifts (v9), the spirit of prophecy comes into his mouth (v12), and he blesses the two sons from whom Israel's priests and kings will come; the Greek sums it up, he blessed Levi as high priest, and Judah as king and ruler.

  • vv13–17 Levi — v14 "like the angels of the presence" — the priests of Israel serve on earth as the highest angels serve in heaven. v15 — as Moses blesses Levi: They shall teach Your judgments to Jacob and Your law to Israel (Deuteronomy 33:10). v16 "you will be joined to the Lord" — Genesis 29:34: Now, this time, my husband will be joined to me… Therefore he called his name Levi. Isaac turns the joining from husband to God.

  • vv18–20 Judah — "a prince, you and one of your sons" — Genesis 49:10: The staff shall not turn aside from Judah, nor the ruler's rod from between his feet.

  • v27 "one hundred and sixty-five years old" — by this book's dates Isaac was born in 1987 (16:13, 15) and this is 2143 (30:1), which makes him 156; the Greek at 29:12 puts Jacob's return in Isaac's 153rd year. Genesis 35:28 has Isaac live a hundred years and eighty years. The text is left as it stands.

  • v29 "do not put off your vow" — Deuteronomy 23:22: When you vow a vow to the LORD your God, you shall not delay to pay it, for the LORD your God will surely require it of you. v30 "Deborah her nurse" — she dies at Bethel in Genesis 35:8, below Bethel, under the oak.

speech.text: Jubilees 31

On the new moon of the month Jacob spoke to all the people of his house, saying, "Purify yourselves and change your clothes, and let us rise and go up to Bethel, where I made my vow to Him on the day I fled from the face of Esau my brother, because He has been with me and brought me back into this land in peace; and put away the foreign gods that are among you."

They gave up the foreign gods, and what was in their ears and on their necks, and the idols that Rachel had stolen from Laban her father she gave, all of them, to Jacob; and he burned them and broke them to pieces and destroyed them, and hid them under an oak that is in the land of Shechem.

On the new moon of the seventh month he went up to Bethel, and built an altar at the place where he had slept, and set up a pillar there; and he sent word to his father Isaac to come to him to his sacrifice, and to his mother Rebekah.
Isaac said, "Let my son Jacob come, and let me see him before I die."

Jacob went to his father Isaac and to his mother Rebekah, to the house of his father Abraham, and took two of his sons with him, Levi and Judah; and he came to his father Isaac and to his mother Rebekah.
Rebekah came out of the tower to the gate of the tower to kiss Jacob and embrace him; for her spirit had revived when she heard, "Jacob your son has come"; and she kissed him.

She saw his two sons, and she recognized them, and said to him, "Are these your sons, my son?" She embraced them and kissed them and blessed them, saying, "In you the seed of Abraham will become famous, and you will be a blessing on the earth."

Jacob went in to Isaac his father, into his chamber where he lay; and his two sons were with him; and he took his father's hand and bent down and kissed him, and Isaac clung to the neck of Jacob his son and wept on his neck.
The darkness passed from Isaac's eyes, and he saw the two sons of Jacob, Levi and Judah, and he said, "Are these your sons, my son? For they are like you."
He told him that they were truly his sons: "Truly you have seen that they are truly my sons."
They came near to him, and he turned and kissed them and embraced them both together.
The spirit of prophecy came down into his mouth, and he took Levi by his right hand and Judah by his left.
He turned to Levi first and began to bless him first, and said to him, "May the Lord of all bless you, He, the Lord of all the ages, you and your sons forever and ever.

May the Lord give to you and to your seed greatness and great glory, and bring you and your seed near to Himself from all flesh, to serve in His sanctuary like the angels of the presence and like the holy ones; and like them the seed of your sons will be, for glory and greatness and holiness, and may He make them great for all the ages.

They will be princes and judges and chiefs to all the seed of the sons of Jacob; they will speak the word of the Lord in righteousness, and they will judge all His judgments in righteousness; and they will declare My ways to Jacob and My paths to Israel. The blessing of God will be given in their mouth, that they may bless all the seed of the beloved.

Your mother called your name Levi, and truly she called your name: you will be joined to the Lord, and be the companion of all the sons of Jacob. Your table will be yours, and you and your sons will eat of it; and your table will be full forever, and your food will not fail forever and ever.
All who hate you will fall down before you, and all your enemies will be rooted out and perish. Blessed is he who blesses you, and every nation that curses you will be cursed."

To Judah he said, "May the Lord give you power and strength to trample all who hate you. Be a prince, you and one of your sons, over the sons of Jacob; may your name and the name of your sons go out and travel through all the earth and the cities. Then the nations will fear before your face, and all the nations will tremble, and all the peoples will tremble.
In you will be the help of Jacob, and in you the salvation of Israel will be found.

On the day you sit on the throne of the honor of your righteousness, there will be great peace for all the seed of the sons of the beloved. Blessed is he who blesses you; and all who hate you and afflict you and curse you will be rooted out and destroyed from the earth, and be cursed."
He turned and kissed him again and embraced him, and rejoiced greatly, for he had seen the sons of Jacob his son in truth.
He went out from between his feet, and fell down and bowed down to him, and he blessed them; and he rested there with Isaac his father that night, and they ate and drank with joy.
He laid the two sons of Jacob to sleep, one on his right and one on his left, and it was counted to him as righteousness.
Jacob told his father everything in the night, how the Lord had shown him great mercy, and had prospered him in all his ways and protected him from all evil.
Isaac blessed the God of his father Abraham, who had not withdrawn His mercy and His righteousness from the son of His servant Isaac.

In the morning Jacob told his father Isaac the vow he had vowed to the Lord, and the vision he had seen, and that he had built an altar, and that everything was ready for the sacrifice to be made before the Lord as he had vowed, and that he had come to set him on a donkey.

Isaac said to Jacob his son, "I cannot come with you, for I am old and cannot bear the way. Go, my son, in peace, for I am one hundred and sixty-five years old this day; I am no longer able to journey. Set your mother on a donkey, and let her go with you.
I know, my son, that you have come on my account; and blessed be this day on which you have seen me alive, and I also have seen you, my son.

Prosper, and fulfill the vow you have vowed, and do not put off your vow, for the vow will be required of you; now hurry to perform it, and may He who made all things, to whom you have vowed the vow, be pleased."
He said to Rebekah, "Go with Jacob your son." Rebekah went with her son Jacob, and Deborah her nurse with her, and they came to Bethel.
Jacob remembered the prayer with which his father had blessed him and his two sons, Levi and Judah, and he rejoiced and blessed the God of his fathers, Abraham and Isaac.

He said, "Now I know that I have an eternal hope, and my sons too, before the God of all." So it is ordained concerning the two of them, and they bring it up for them as an eternal testimony on the tablets of heaven, how Isaac blessed them.

chapters.title: Levi the Priest, the Second Tithe, and the Name Israel
chapters.html:
Jubilees 32

1He stayed that night at Bethel, and Levi dreamed that they had appointed and made him priest of God Most High, him and his sons forever; and he woke from his sleep and blessed the Lord.

2Jacob rose early in the morning, on the fourteenth of this month, and tithed everything that had come with him, from men to every living creature, and from gold to every vessel and garment; he tithed everything.

3In those days Rachel was pregnant with Benjamin her son, and Jacob counted his sons from him; and the count went up, and Levi fell to the portion of the Lord; and his father clothed him in the garments of the priesthood and consecrated him.

4On the fifteenth of this month he brought to the altar fourteen bulls from the cattle, and twenty-eight rams, and forty-nine sheep, and sixty lambs, and twenty-nine kids of the goats, as a burnt offering on the altar, an acceptable offering for a soothing aroma before God.

5This was his offering from the vow he had vowed, to give a tenth, with their grain offerings and their drink offerings.

6When the fire had consumed it, he burned incense on it, over the fire; and as a peace offering, four calves and four rams and four male goats, and two yearling sheep and two kids of the goats; and he did this every morning for the seven days.

7He and all his sons and his men were eating there with joy for seven days, and blessing and thanking the Lord, who had delivered him from all his distress and had granted him his vow.

8He tithed all the clean animals and made a burnt offering of them; and the unclean animals he gave to Levi his son, and all the souls of men he gave him.

9Levi served as priest at Bethel before Jacob his father, above his ten brothers, and he was priest there; and Jacob paid his vow: so he tithed the tithe again to the Lord and made it holy, and it became holy to Him.

10For this reason it is ordained on the tablets of heaven as a law, to tithe the tithe again, to eat it before the Lord in the place chosen for His name to dwell on it, from year to year; and to this law there is no limit of days forever.

11This ordinance is written, to be done from year to year: to eat the second tithe before the Lord in the place that has been chosen; and nothing of it shall be left over from this year to the next.

12For in its year the seed shall be eaten, until the days of the harvest of the seed of the year; and the wine until the days of the wine; and the oil until the days of its season.

13All that is left of it and grows old, let it be counted defiled; let it be burned with fire, for it has become unclean.

14So let them eat it together in the sanctuary, and not let it grow old.

15All the tithes of cattle and sheep are holy to the Lord, and let them be for His priests to eat before Him from year to year; for so it is ordained and engraved concerning the tithe on the tablets of heaven.

16On the second night, on the twenty-second day of this month, Jacob resolved to build that place and to surround the court with a wall, and to make it holy, and to make it holy forever, for himself and for his sons after him forever.

17The Lord appeared to him by night and blessed him and said to him, "Your name shall not be called Jacob only, but they will call your name Israel."

18He said to him again, "I am the Lord who created heaven and earth, and I will make you grow and multiply you very greatly; and kings will come from you, and they will rule everywhere the foot of the sons of men has trodden.

19I will give to your seed all the earth that is under heaven, and they will rule over all the nations as they wish; and after this they will gather in all the earth and inherit it forever."

20He finished speaking with him and went up from him, and Jacob watched until He had gone up into heaven.

21He saw in a vision of the night an angel coming down from heaven with seven tablets in his hands; and he gave them to Jacob, and he read them, and read all that was written in them, what would happen to him and to his sons in all the ages.

22He showed him all that was written on the tablets, and said to him, "Do not build this place, and do not make it an eternal sanctuary, and do not live here, for this is not the place. Go to the house of Abraham your father, and live with Isaac your father until the day of your father's death.

23For in Egypt you will die in peace, and in this land you will be buried with honor, in the tomb of your fathers, with Abraham and Isaac.

24Do not fear, for as you have seen and read, so it will all be; and you, write down all that you have seen and read."

25Jacob said, "Lord, how shall I remember all that I have read and seen?" He said to him, "I will bring all things to your remembrance."

26He went up from him; and he woke from his sleep, and remembered everything he had read and seen, and wrote down all the words he had read and seen.

27He kept one more day there, and sacrificed on it according to all that he had sacrificed on the former days, and called its name Addition, for that day was added; and the former days he called the festival.

28So it was shown that it should be, and it is written on the tablets of heaven; for this reason it was revealed to him to keep it, and to add it to the seven days of the festival.

29Its name was called Addition, because it was recorded in the testimony of the festival days, according to the number of the days of the year.

30In the night, on the twenty-third of this month, Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died, and they buried her below the city, under the oak of the river; and he called the name of that place the River of Deborah, and the oak, the Oak of the Mourning of Deborah.

31Rebekah went and returned to her house, to his father Isaac; and Jacob sent by her hand rams and sheep and male goats, so that she might prepare a meal for his father such as he desired.

32He went after his mother until he came near the land of Kabratan, and he lived there.

33Rachel bore a son in the night, and called his name Son of My Sorrow, for she had hard labor bearing him; but his father called his name Benjamin.

34On the tenth of the eighth month, in the first year of the sixth week of this jubilee, Rachel died there and was buried in the land of Ephrath, which is Bethlehem; and Jacob built a pillar on Rachel's grave, on the way, over her grave.

Notes

  • vv1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 10, 11, 15, 22, 25, 26, 28, 31, 34 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v1 to v8 and from v18 on, has many of them too. v26 — the Latin says that Jacob concealed the words he had read; the Asmara printing, like Charles, has wrote down, which is what the angel commands in v24. v31 — the Latin has Jacob, not Rebekah, return to Isaac; the Asmara printing has Rebekah.

  • vv1–9 Levi made priest — on the fifteenth of the seventh month, the Festival of Booths (16:29), Jacob tithes everything he has, counts his sons upward from Benjamin still in the womb, and the tenth, Levi, falls to the Lord. v6 the peace offering — so the Asmara printing: four calves, four rams, four male goats, two yearling sheep, two kids; the Latin and Charles have two calves, four rams, two yearling lambs and two male goats. v4 the numbers — so the EOTC: fourteen bulls, twenty-eight rams, forty-nine sheep, sixty lambs, twenty-nine kids. Charles and the Latin have seven and twenty-one for the last two, and so every number a multiple of seven. v8 "the unclean animals he gave to Levi" — Charles's text reads he gave (not); compare Numbers 18:15, where the firstborn of unclean animals is redeemed, not given to the priest.

  • vv10–15 the second tithe — Deuteronomy 14:23: You shall eat before the LORD your God, in the place that He chooses to make His name dwell there, the tithe of your grain, your new wine and your oil; Leviticus 27:32: Every tenth of the herd and the flock… shall be holy to the LORD. Jubilees roots both laws in Jacob's vow at Bethel (27:27).

  • vv16–26 the name Israel, and the seven tablets — Genesis 35:9–15. v17 "Your name shall not be called Jacob only" — Genesis 35:10: Your name shall no longer be called Jacob — Israel shall be your name. The EOTC's only keeps both names, as the Bible goes on using both. vv21–26 "seven tablets" — Jacob is shown the future of his sons; the Latin calls them boxwood tablets. v22 "Do not build this place" — the sanctuary will be built elsewhere, in the place God chooses (v10).

  • vv27–29 "Addition" — the eighth day after the seven of Booths, as in Leviticus 23:36: On the eighth day you shall have a holy assembly… It is a closing assembly. The Latin calls it Retention.

  • v30 Deborah — Genesis 35:8: Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died, and she was buried below Bethel, under the oak. He called its name Allon-bacuth, "oak of weeping."

  • vv32–34 Benjamin and Rachel's death — Genesis 35:16–20: There was still a stretch of ground to come to Ephrath, and Rachel gave birth, and her labor was hard… she called his name Ben-oni. His father called him Benjamin… Jacob set up a pillar over her grave. "Kabratan" — apparently the Hebrew kivrat, a stretch of ground, read as a place name. v34 the date — the first year of the sixth week is 2143, the year of 30:1 and 31:1. The Asmara printing sets the date with Rachel's death, the Latin with Benjamin's birth, which was the same night. The Asmara printing and the Latin have the tenth of the eighth month, Charles the eleventh.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Reuben and Bilhah
chapters.html:
Jubilees 33

1Jacob went and lived to the south of Migdal-eder; and he went to his father Isaac, he and Leah his wife, on the new moon of the tenth month.

2Reuben saw Bilhah, Rachel's maid, his father's secondary wife, bathing in water in a hidden place, and he loved her.

3He hid himself at night, and went into Bilhah's house by night, and found her sleeping alone on her bed in her house.

4He lay with her, and she woke and saw Reuben lying with her in the bed; and she uncovered the corner of her garment and seized him and cried out, and recognized that it was Reuben, and was ashamed.

5She was ashamed because of him, and let go her hand from him, and he fled.

6She grieved over this thing very much, and told no one.

7When Jacob came and sought her, she said to him, "I am not clean for you, for I have been defiled as regards you; for Reuben has defiled me and lain with me in the night, and I was asleep and did not know until he uncovered my skirt and lay with me."

8Jacob was very angry with Reuben, because he had lain with Bilhah, because he had uncovered his father's skirt.

9Jacob did not come near her again, because Reuben had defiled her. As for any man who uncovers his father's skirt, his deed is very evil, for he is abominable before the Lord.

10For this reason it is written and ordained on the tablets of heaven that a man shall not lie with his father's wife, and shall not uncover his father's skirt, for it is unclean: they shall surely die together, the man who lies with his father's wife and the woman too, for they have done an unclean thing on the earth.

11Let there be nothing unclean before our God in the people He has chosen for Himself as a possession.

12Again it is written a second time: "Cursed be he who lies with his father's wife, for he has uncovered his father's shame"; and all the holy ones of the Lord said, "So be it, so be it."

13You too, Moses, command the sons of Israel to keep this word, for it is a judgment of death, and it is unclean, and there is no atonement ever to atone for the man who has done this, but to put him to death, to kill him, to stone him with stones, and to root him out from among the people of our God.

14For no man who does it in Israel shall live a single day on the earth, for he is abominable and unclean.

15Let them not say, "Reuben had life and forgiveness after he lay with his father's secondary wife, and she too, though she had a husband, and her husband, Jacob his father, was alive."

16For until then the ordinance and the judgment and the law had not been revealed in full to all; but in your days it has been revealed as a law of times and of days, and an eternal law for the eternal generations.

17To this law there is no end of days, and no atonement for it, except that both of them be rooted out from among the people; on the day they did it they shall kill them.

18You too, Moses, write it for Israel, and let them keep it and not do anything like this thing, and not go astray into a sin to death; for the Lord our God is the judge, who does not respect persons and does not take gifts.

19Tell them these words of the ordinance, that they may hear and keep them and guard themselves concerning them, and not perish and not be rooted out of the land; for it is uncleanness and abomination and hatred and defilement to all who do them on the earth before our God.

20There is no greater sin than the fornication they commit on the earth, for Israel is a holy people to the Lord its God, and a people of inheritance, and a priestly and royal people, and set apart; and let no uncleanness appear among the holy people.

21In the third year of the sixth week Jacob went, with all his sons, and they lived in the house of Abraham, near Isaac his father and Rebekah his mother.

22These are the names of the sons of Jacob: the firstborn Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, the sons of Leah; and the sons of Rachel, Joseph and Benjamin; and the sons of Bilhah, Dan and Naphtali; and the sons of Zilpah, Gad and Asher; and Dinah, the daughter of Leah, Jacob's only daughter.

23They came and bowed down to Isaac and Rebekah; and when they saw them, they blessed Jacob and all his sons; and Isaac rejoiced greatly, because he saw the sons of Jacob his younger son, and he blessed them.

Notes

  • vv4, 16, 19, 20, 22, 23 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v1 to v9 and from v18 on, has most of them too. v9 — the EOTC stops at because Reuben had defiled her; the second sentence is in the second Ge'ez text and the Asmara printing. v6 "told no one" — the Latin has told everyone.

  • vv1–9 Reuben and Bilhah — Genesis 35:21–22: Israel pulled up and pitched his tent beyond Migdal-eder. And it came to pass… that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father's secondary wife. Israel heard. Genesis says no more until Jacob's last words: you went up on your father's bed. Then you defiled it (Genesis 49:4). Jubilees tells the night from Bilhah's side. "Migdal-eder" — the EOTC writes Magdaladrāʾef; the Latin has Migdal-Eder.

  • vv10–20 the law — Leviticus 18:8: You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife; Leviticus 20:11: A man who lies with his father's wife has uncovered his father's nakedness. Both of them shall surely be put to death. v12 "written a second time" — Deuteronomy 27:20: Cursed is he who lies with his father's wife, for he has uncovered his father's skirt. And all the people shall say, Amen. In Jubilees it is the holy ones of heaven who answer.

  • vv15–16 "Let them not say, 'Reuben had life and forgiveness'" — Jubilees meets the obvious objection: Reuben was not put to death because the law had not yet been revealed in full. The law revealed to Moses leaves no such room.

  • vv21–23 the date and the sons — the third year of the sixth week is 2145. The list is Genesis 35:23–26, with Dinah added.

Again it is written a second time: "Cursed be he who lies with his father's wife, for he has uncovered his father's shame"; and all the holy ones of the Lord said, "So be it, so be it."

You too, Moses, command the sons of Israel to keep this word, for it is a judgment of death, and it is unclean, and there is no atonement ever to atone for the man who has done this, but to put him to death, to kill him, to stone him with stones, and to root him out from among the people of our God.
For no man who does it in Israel shall live a single day on the earth, for he is abominable and unclean.
Let them not say, "Reuben had life and forgiveness after he lay with his father's secondary wife, and she too, though she had a husband, and her husband, Jacob his father, was alive."

For until then the ordinance and the judgment and the law had not been revealed in full to all; but in your days it has been revealed as a law of times and of days, and an eternal law for the eternal generations.
To this law there is no end of days, and no atonement for it, except that both of them be rooted out from among the people; on the day they did it they shall kill them.

You too, Moses, write it for Israel, and let them keep it and not do anything like this thing, and not go astray into a sin to death; for the Lord our God is the judge, who does not respect persons and does not take gifts.

Tell them these words of the ordinance, that they may hear and keep them and guard themselves concerning them, and not perish and not be rooted out of the land; for it is uncleanness and abomination and hatred and defilement to all who do them on the earth before our God.

There is no greater sin than the fornication they commit on the earth, for Israel is a holy people to the Lord its God, and a people of inheritance, and a priestly and royal people, and set apart; and let no uncleanness appear among the holy people.
In the third year of the sixth week Jacob went, with all his sons, and they lived in the house of Abraham, near Isaac his father and Rebekah his mother.

These are the names of the sons of Jacob: the firstborn Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, the sons of Leah; and the sons of Rachel, Joseph and Benjamin; and the sons of Bilhah, Dan and Naphtali; and the sons of Zilpah, Gad and Asher; and Dinah, the daughter of Leah, Jacob's only daughter.

They came and bowed down to Isaac and Rebekah; and when they saw them, they blessed Jacob and all his sons; and Isaac rejoiced greatly, because he saw the sons of Jacob his younger son, and he blessed them.

chapters.title: The Amorite Kings, Joseph Sold, and the Day of Atonement
chapters.html:
Jubilees 34

1In the sixth year of this week of this forty-fourth jubilee, Jacob sent his sons to pasture his sheep, and his servants with them, to the field of Shechem.

2The seven kings of the Amorites gathered against them, hiding under the trees, to kill them and to carry off their cattle as plunder.

3Jacob and Levi and Judah and Joseph were in the house with Isaac their father, for his spirit was grieved, and they could not leave him; and Benjamin was the youngest, and for this reason he stayed with him.

4There came the kings of Taphu, and the kings of Ares, and the kings of Seragan, and the kings of Selo, and the king of Gaaz, and the king of Beth-horon, and the king of Maanisakir, and all who live in this mountain country, who live in the forest of the land of Canaan.

5They told Jacob, saying, "The kings of the Amorites have surrounded your sons, and their flocks have been plundered."

6He rose from his house, he and his three sons and all his father's servants and his own servants, and went against them with six thousand men who carried swords.

7He killed them in the pastures of Shechem, and pursued those who fled, and killed them with the edge of the sword; and he killed Ares and Taphu and Seragan and Selo and Maanisakir and Gaaz.

8He gathered in his flocks; and he prevailed over them and laid tribute on them, that they should pay him tribute, five fruits of their land; and he built Robel and Tamnatares.

9He returned in peace, and made peace with them, and they became his servants until the day that he and his sons went down into Egypt.

10In the seventh year of this week he sent Joseph from his house to the land of Shechem, to learn how his brothers were, and he found them in the land of Dothan.

11They dealt treacherously with him and made a plan against him to kill him; but changing their minds, they sold him to Ishmaelite merchants, and they brought him down into Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the eunuch of Pharaoh, the chief of the cooks, the priest of the city of Elew.

12The sons of Jacob slaughtered a kid of the goats, and dipped Joseph's garment in its blood, and sent it to Jacob their father on the tenth of the seventh month.

13He mourned all that night, for they had brought it to him in the evening, and he became feverish with mourning for his death, and he said, "A fierce beast has devoured Joseph"; and all the people of his house mourned with him that day, and they were grieving and mourning with him all that day.

14His sons and his daughter rose to comfort him, and he would not be comforted for his son.

15On that day Bilhah heard that Joseph had perished, and she died mourning for him; she was living in Qafratef. Dinah his daughter also died after Joseph had perished. These three mournings came upon Israel in one month.

16They buried Bilhah opposite the tomb of Rachel, and Dinah his daughter they also buried there.

17He mourned for Joseph one year and did not cease, for he said, "Let me go down to the grave mourning for my son."

18For this reason it is ordained for the sons of Israel that they should afflict themselves on the tenth of the seventh month — on the day the news came to Jacob his father that made him weep for Joseph — to make atonement for themselves on it with a kid of the goats, on the tenth of the seventh month, once a year, for their sins; for they had grieved the affection of their father over Joseph his son.

19This day has been ordained, that they should grieve on it for their sins, and for all their transgressions, and for all their errors, so that they may cleanse themselves on this day once a year.

20After Joseph perished, the sons of Jacob took wives for themselves. [The name of Reuben's wife is Ada;] the name of Simeon's wife is Adlbaa, a Canaanite; and the name of Levi's wife is Melka, of the daughters of Aram, of the seed of the sons of Terah; and the name of Judah's wife, Betasuel, a Canaanite; [and the name of Issachar's wife, Hezaqa;] and the name of Zebulun's wife, Niiman; and the name of Dan's wife, Egla; and the name of Naphtali's wife, Rasuu, of Mesopotamia; and the name of Gad's wife, Maka; and the name of Asher's wife, Ijona; and the name of Joseph's wife, Asenath the Egyptian; and the name of Benjamin's wife, Ijasaka.

21Simeon repented, and took a second wife from Mesopotamia, like his brothers.

Notes

  • vv1, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 18, 20 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter as far as v5, has v1 too. Without them the EOTC never says where Jacob's sons were, never tells how Joseph came to Egypt, and never names the wives. Words in [brackets] (v20) are in no Ge'ez text here: the Asmara printing numbers the wives one by one and skips Reuben's and Issachar's, which follow Charles's English.

  • vv1–9 the war with the Amorite kings — not in Genesis. Genesis 48:22 has Jacob speak of one shoulder above your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow; this war tells how. v4 the kings — the Ge'ez names are given as it writes them; the Latin reads Shiloh for Selo and Gaash for Gaaz. v1 the date — the sixth year of this week, the sixth of the forty-fourth jubilee, is 2148.

  • vv10–17 Joseph sold — Genesis 37. v10 the date — the seventh year of this week is 2149; Joseph, born in 2134 (28:24), is fifteen. Genesis 37:2 has Joseph, a son of seventeen years. v11 "the chief of the cooks" — Genesis 37:36 has chief of the slaughterers. v12 — Genesis 37:31: They took Joseph's coat and slaughtered a male goat and dipped the coat in the blood. vv14, 17 — Genesis 37:35: All his sons and all his daughters rose to comfort him, and he refused to be comforted, and said, "For I will go down to my son, mourning, to Sheol." v15 Bilhah and Dinah — their deaths are not in Genesis.

  • vv18–19 the Day of Atonement — Leviticus 16:29–30: in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month, you shall afflict yourselves… because on this day atonement shall be made for you, to cleanse you. Jubilees roots the day in the tenth of the seventh month, when Jacob's sons brought him the goat-bloodied coat: the kid of the goats that deceived their father becomes the kid of the goats of atonement.

  • vv20–21 the wives — "Betasuel, a Canaanite" — Genesis 38:2: Judah saw there the daughter of a Canaanite man whose name was Shua; bat-Shua, "daughter of Shua," has become her name. "Asenath the Egyptian" — Genesis 41:45. v21 "Simeon repented" — Genesis 46:10 names Shaul son of the Canaanite woman among Simeon's sons.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Rebekah's Last Charge to Her Sons
chapters.html:
Jubilees 35

1In the first year of the first week of the forty-fifth jubilee Rebekah called Jacob her son and commanded him about his father and about his brother, that he should honor them all the days of Jacob's life.

2Jacob said, "I will do everything as you have commanded me, for this thing will be honor and greatness to me, and righteousness before the Lord, that I should honor them.

3You too, mother, know from the day I was born until this day all my deeds and all that is in my heart, that all the days I think good toward all.

4How should I not do this thing that you have commanded me, to honor my father and my brothers?

5Tell me, mother, what perversity you have seen in me, and I will turn away from it, and mercy will be on me."

6She said to him, "My son, in all my days I have seen in you no perverse deed at all, but only upright ones. Yet I will tell you the truth, my son: I will die this year, and I will not live through this year; for I have seen in a dream the day of my death, that I would not live beyond a hundred and fifty-five years; and I have completed all the days of my life that I am to live."

7Jacob laughed at his mother's words, because his mother had told him that she would die, and she was sitting opposite him with her strength on her, and she had not grown weak in her strength; for she went in and out and could see, and her teeth were strong, and no sickness had touched her all the days of her life.

8Jacob said to her, "Blessed am I, mother, if my days come near to the days of your life, and my strength stays with me as your strength does; and you will not die, for you are speaking with me idly about your death."

9She went in to Isaac and said to him, "One request I ask of you: make Esau swear that he will not harm Jacob, and will not pursue him with hatred; for you know Esau's mind, that it is evil from his youth, and there is nothing upright in him; for he wants to kill him after your death.

10You know all he has done from the day Jacob his brother went to Harran until this day, how with all his heart he has forsaken us, and has done evil to us; your flocks he has taken for himself, and carried off all your possessions from before your face.

11When we begged and asked him for what was ours, he acted like a man who was doing us a kindness.

12He is bitter against you because you blessed Jacob your whole and upright son, for there is no evil in him, only goodness; and since he came from Harran until this day he has not robbed us of anything, for he brings us everything in its season, always, and rejoices with all his heart when we take from his hands, and he blesses us; and he has not parted from us since he came from Harran until this day, and he stays with us always at home, honoring us."

13Isaac said to her, "I too know and see the deeds of Jacob who is with us, how with all his heart he honors us; but before, I loved Esau more than Jacob, because he was the firstborn; but now I love Jacob more than Esau, for he has done many evil deeds, and there is no righteousness in him, for all his ways are unrighteousness and violence, and there is no righteousness around him.

14Now my heart is troubled because of his deeds, and neither he nor his seed is to be saved, for they are those who will be destroyed from the earth and who will be rooted out from under heaven; for he has forsaken the God of Abraham and gone after his wives and after their uncleanness and after their error, he and his children.

15You ask me to make him swear that he will not kill Jacob his brother; even if he swears, he will not keep his oath, and he will not do good but only evil.

16But if he wants to kill Jacob his brother, he will be given into Jacob's hand, and he will not escape from his hand, for he will fall into his hand.

17Do not fear for Jacob, for Jacob's guardian is great and mighty and honored, and more praised than Esau's guardian."

18Rebekah sent and called Esau, and he came to her, and she said to him, "I have a request, my son, that I ask of you; say that you will do it, my son."

19He said, "I will do everything you tell me, and I will not refuse your request."

20She said to him, "I ask of you that on the day I die you will bring me in and bury me near Sarah, your father's mother; and that you and Jacob will love each other, and neither will seek evil for his brother, but only love; and so you will prosper, my sons, and be honored in the middle of the land, and no enemy will rejoice over you, and you will be a blessing and a mercy in the eyes of all who love you."

21He said, "I will do all that you have told me, and I will bury you on the day you die near Sarah, my father's mother, as you have wished, that her bones may be near your bones.

22Jacob my brother I too will love above all flesh, for I have no brother in all the earth but him alone; and it is no great merit for me if I love him, for he is my brother, and we were sown together in your body, and together we came out of your womb; and if I do not love my brother, whom shall I love?

23I myself ask you to urge Jacob concerning me and my sons, for I know that he will surely reign over me and over my sons; for my father made him the higher and me the lower.

24I swear to you that I will love him, and will not seek evil for him all the days of my life, but only good." He swore to her about all this.

25She called Jacob before Esau's eyes and commanded him according to the words she had spoken with Esau.

26He said, "I will do your will. Believe me that no evil will come from me or from my sons against Esau; I will go before him in nothing but love."

27They ate and drank, she and her sons, that night; and she died, three jubilees and one week and one year old, on that night; and her two sons, Esau and Jacob, buried her in the double cave near Sarah, their father's mother.

Notes

  • vv6, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 22, 23, 24, 27 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v3 to v12 in broken form, has parts of vv6–12 too. He swore to her about all this stands at the end of v24, where the Asmara printing has it. v6 — the Latin is broken at the point of Rebekah's age (… fifty years am I completing); the Asmara printing has a hundred and fifty-five years. Without the end of v27, the EOTC never tells of Rebekah's death.

  • v1 the date — the first year of the forty-fifth jubilee is 44 × 49 + 1 = 2157. v27 "three jubilees and one week and one year" — 147 + 7 + 1 = 155, the age of her dream in v6.

  • vv1–8 Rebekah and Jacob — Honor your father and your mother, so that your days may be long (Exodus 20:12). v7 "Jacob laughed" — she is still strong and her teeth are sound; he takes her foreknowledge of death for a jest.

  • vv9–17 Rebekah and Isaac — Isaac at last says that he loves Jacob more than Esau (v13, in Charles's text), reversing Genesis 25:28, Isaac loved Esau. v17 "Jacob's guardian… Esau's guardian" — each brother has a heavenly guardian. The Greek sums up the chapter: Rebecca asked Isaac in his old age to exhort Esau and Jacob to love one another.

  • vv18–26 Rebekah and Esau — Esau swears to love Jacob. v23 "he will surely reign over me" — the oracle at the twins' birth: One people will be stronger than the other, and the elder shall serve the younger (Genesis 25:23).

  • v27 the double cave — Genesis does not tell of Rebekah's death; Jacob names her grave at his own: There they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife (Genesis 49:31).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin and Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Isaac's Last Words, and the Deaths of Isaac and Leah
chapters.html:
Jubilees 36

1In the sixth year of this week Isaac called his two sons, Esau and Jacob, and they came to him, and he said to them, "My sons, I am going the way of my fathers, to the eternal house where my fathers are.

2Bury me near Abraham my father, in the double cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite, which Abraham acquired to bury in; in the grave that I dug for myself there, there bury me.

3This I command you, my sons: do righteousness and uprightness on the earth, so that the Lord may bring on you all that the Lord said He would do for Abraham and his seed.

4Be, my sons, loving your brothers among yourselves as a man loves his own soul, and let each seek what is good for his brother, and act together on the earth, and let them love each other as their own souls.

5About idols, I charge you to despise them and hate them and not love them, for they are full of error for those who serve them and those who bow down to them.

6Remember, my sons, the Lord, the God of Abraham your father, and how I too worshiped Him and served Him in righteousness and in joy, so that He may multiply you and make your seed grow as the stars of heaven in number, and plant you on the earth as a plant of righteousness that will not be rooted out, for all the eternal generations.

7Now I will make you swear a great oath — for there is no oath greater than it — by the name glorious and honored and great, splendid and wonderful and mighty, who made the heavens and the earth and all things together, that you will fear Him and worship Him;

8and that each will love his brother with mercy and righteousness, and no man will want evil for his brother, from now on and forever, all the days of your life, so that you may prosper in all your deeds and not perish.

9If any of you seeks evil for his brother, know from now on that everyone who seeks evil for his brother will fall into his hand and be rooted out of the land of the living, and his seed will perish from under heaven.

10On the day of turmoil and curse and wrath and anger, with devouring fire, as He burned Sodom, so He will burn his land and his city and all that is his; and he will be blotted out of the book of the instruction of the sons of men, and not be written in the book of life, but in the one appointed for destruction, and he will go into an eternal curse, so that their condemnation may be always renewed, in hate and in curse and in wrath, in torment and in indignation, in plagues and in sickness, forever.

11I tell you and testify to you, my sons, according to the judgment that will come on the man who wants to do harm to his brother."

12He divided all his possessions between the two of them that day, and gave the larger portion to the man who was born first, and the tower and all that was around it, and all that Abraham had acquired at the Well of the Oath.

13He said, "This larger portion I will give to the man who was born first."

14Esau said, "I sold it to Jacob and gave my birthright to Jacob; let it be given to him, and I have not a single word to say about it, for it is his."

15Isaac said, "May a blessing rest on you, my sons, and on your seed this day, for you have given me rest, and my heart is not grieved over the birthright, that you might do wickedness on account of it.

16May the Lord Most High bless the man who does righteousness, him and his seed forever."

17He finished commanding them and blessing them, and they ate and drank together before him, and he rejoiced because there was one mind between them; and they went out from him and rested that day and slept.

18Isaac slept on his bed that day rejoicing, and he slept the sleep of eternity, and died one hundred and eighty years old. He completed twenty-five weeks and five years; and his two sons, Esau and Jacob, buried him.

19Esau went to the land of Edom, to Mount Seir, and lived there.

20Jacob lived on the mountain of Hebron, in the tower of the land where his father Abraham had lived as a guest, and he served God with all his heart and with all his soul, and according to the visible commandments, according to the division of the times of his generations.

21Leah his wife died in the fourth year of the second week of the forty-fifth jubilee, and he buried her in the double cave near Rebekah his mother, to the left of the grave of Sarah, his father's mother.

22All her sons and his sons came to mourn Leah his wife with him and to comfort him over her, for he was lamenting her.

23For he loved her very much from the time Rachel her sister died, for she was whole and upright in all her ways, and honored Jacob all the days he lived with her; and he did not hear a harsh word from her mouth, for she was quiet and peaceable and upright and honorable.

24He remembered all the deeds she had done in her life, and lamented her greatly, for he loved her with all his heart and with all his soul.

  • vv7, 10, 12, 18, 20, 23 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v20 on, has vv20 and 23 too. Without the end of v18 the EOTC never says that Isaac died or that his sons buried him.

  • vv1–11 Isaac's charge — v2 "in the grave that I dug for myself" — the words Jacob will use of his own grave: In my grave that I dug for myself in the land of Canaan, there you shall bury me (Genesis 50:5). v4 "as a man loves his own soul" — Leviticus 19:18: you shall love your neighbor as yourself. v9 "will fall into his hand" — the Greek has it as a prophecy: if Esau rises up against Jacob, he will fall into his hands; it comes true in chapters 37–38.

  • vv12–16 the birthright — Isaac means to give the larger share to the firstborn, and Esau gives it up: I sold it to Jacob (Genesis 25:33, he sold his birthright to Jacob).

  • v18 Isaac's death — Genesis 35:28–29: The days of Isaac were a hundred years and eighty years. Isaac breathed his last and died… Esau and Jacob his sons buried him. "twenty-five weeks and five years" — 175 + 5 = 180. The date — the sixth year of this week, the first of the forty-fifth jubilee, is 2162; by this book's date for his birth, 1987 (16:15), Isaac is 175. The text is left as it stands.

  • vv21–24 Leah — the fourth year of the second week is 2167. Genesis says only There I buried Leah (Genesis 49:31); Jubilees gives Jacob's grief and her praise.

speech.text: Jubilees 36

In the sixth year of this week Isaac called his two sons, Esau and Jacob, and they came to him, and he said to them, "My sons, I am going the way of my fathers, to the eternal house where my fathers are.
Bury me near Abraham my father, in the double cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite, which Abraham acquired to bury in; in the grave that I dug for myself there, there bury me.
This I command you, my sons: do righteousness and uprightness on the earth, so that the Lord may bring on you all that the Lord said He would do for Abraham and his seed.

Be, my sons, loving your brothers among yourselves as a man loves his own soul, and let each seek what is good for his brother, and act together on the earth, and let them love each other as their own souls.
About idols, I charge you to despise them and hate them and not love them, for they are full of error for those who serve them and those who bow down to them.

Remember, my sons, the Lord, the God of Abraham your father, and how I too worshiped Him and served Him in righteousness and in joy, so that He may multiply you and make your seed grow as the stars of heaven in number, and plant you on the earth as a plant of righteousness that will not be rooted out, for all the eternal generations.

Now I will make you swear a great oath — for there is no oath greater than it — by the name glorious and honored and great, splendid and wonderful and mighty, who made the heavens and the earth and all things together, that you will fear Him and worship Him;

and that each will love his brother with mercy and righteousness, and no man will want evil for his brother, from now on and forever, all the days of your life, so that you may prosper in all your deeds and not perish.

If any of you seeks evil for his brother, know from now on that everyone who seeks evil for his brother will fall into his hand and be rooted out of the land of the living, and his seed will perish from under heaven.

On the day of turmoil and curse and wrath and anger, with devouring fire, as He burned Sodom, so He will burn his land and his city and all that is his; and he will be blotted out of the book of the instruction of the sons of men, and not be written in the book of life, but in the one appointed for destruction, and he will go into an eternal curse, so that their condemnation may be always renewed, in hate and in curse and in wrath, in torment and in indignation, in plagues and in sickness, forever.
I tell you and testify to you, my sons, according to the judgment that will come on the man who wants to do harm to his brother."

He divided all his possessions between the two of them that day, and gave the larger portion to the man who was born first, and the tower and all that was around it, and all that Abraham had acquired at the Well of the Oath.
He said, "This larger portion I will give to the man who was born first."

May the Lord Most High bless the man who does righteousness, him and his seed forever."

He finished commanding them and blessing them, and they ate and drank together before him, and he rejoiced because there was one mind between them; and they went out from him and rested that day and slept.

Esau went to the land of Edom, to Mount Seir, and lived there.

Jacob lived on the mountain of Hebron, in the tower of the land where his father Abraham had lived as a guest, and he served God with all his heart and with all his soul, and according to the visible commandments, according to the division of the times of his generations.

Leah his wife died in the fourth year of the second week of the forty-fifth jubilee, and he buried her in the double cave near Rebekah his mother, to the left of the grave of Sarah, his father's mother.
All her sons and his sons came to mourn Leah his wife with him and to comfort him over her, for he was lamenting her.

For he loved her very much from the time Rachel her sister died, for she was whole and upright in all her ways, and honored Jacob all the days he lived with her; and he did not hear a harsh word from her mouth, for she was quiet and peaceable and upright and honorable.
He remembered all the deeds she had done in her life, and lamented her greatly, for he loved her with all his heart and with all his soul.

chapters.title: Esau Breaks His Oath
chapters.html:
Jubilees 37

1On the day Isaac, the father of Jacob and Esau, died, the sons of Esau heard that Isaac had given the elder's portion to Jacob his younger son[, and they were very indignant].

2They quarreled with their father, saying, "Why, when you are the elder and Jacob the younger, has your father given Jacob the elder's portion and passed you over?"

3He said to them, "Because I sold my birthright to Jacob for a little dish of lentils; and on the day my father sent me to hunt game for him, so that after eating he might bless me, he came with deceit and brought food and drink to my father, and my father blessed him and put me under his hand.

4Now our father has made us swear, me and him, that we will not seek evil, one against his brother, and that we will live in love and in peace, each with his brother, and not corrupt our ways."

5They said to him, "We will not listen to you and make peace with him, for our strength is greater than his strength, and we are stronger than he. We will go against him and kill him and destroy his sons; and if you will not go with us, we will do you harm too.

6Now listen to us: let us send to Aram and to Philistia and to Moab and to Ammon, and choose for ourselves chosen men who are eager for battle, and go against him and fight with him, and root him out of the earth before he grows strong."

7Their father said to them, "Do not go, and do not make war with him, or you will fall before him."

8They said to him, "This is just your way, from your youth until this day: you put your neck under his yoke. We will not listen to this word."

9They sent to Aram, and to Aduram, to their father's friend, and hired with them a thousand fighting men, chosen men of war.

10There came to them from Moab and from the sons of Ammon, hired, a thousand chosen men; and from Philistia a thousand chosen men of war; and from Edom and from the Horites a thousand chosen fighting men; and from the Kittim mighty men of war.

11They said to their father, "Go out and lead them, or else we will kill you."

12He was filled with wrath and anger when he saw that his sons were forcing him to go before them and lead them against Jacob his brother.

13But then he remembered all the evil that lay hidden in his heart against Jacob his brother, and he did not remember the oath he had sworn to his father and his mother, that he would seek no evil, all his days, against Jacob his brother.

14Through all this Jacob did not know that they were coming against him to battle; and he was mourning for Leah his wife, until they came very near to the tower with [four thousand] warriors, chosen men of war.

15The men of Hebron sent to him, saying, "Your brother has come against you to fight you with four thousand men girded with the sword, and they carry shields and weapons of war"; for they loved Jacob more than Esau. They told him, for Jacob was a more generous and merciful man than Esau.

16Jacob did not believe it until they came near the tower.

17He shut the gates of the tower; and he stood on the battlements and spoke to his brother Esau and said, "Noble is the comfort with which you have come to comfort me for my wife who has died! Is this the oath that you swore to your father, and again to your mother, before they died? You have broken the oath, and in the moment you swore it to your father you were condemned."

18Then Esau answered and said to him, "Neither the sons of men nor the beasts of the earth have an oath of righteousness that, once sworn, they keep forever; but every day they plan evil against one another, how each may kill his enemy and foe.

19You hate me and my sons forever, and there is no keeping brotherhood with you.

20Hear this word that I tell you: if the boar changes its skin and makes its bristles soft as wool, and if horns come out on its head like the horns of a stag and of sheep, then I will keep brotherhood with you. If the breasts have been parted from their mother, you have not been a brother to me.

21If the wolves make peace with the lambs, so as not to devour them or do them violence, and if their hearts are toward them for good, then there will be peace in my heart toward you.

22If the lion becomes the ox's yokefellow, and makes peace with him, and is bound under one yoke with him and plows with him, then I will make peace with you.

23If the ravens become white like the raza, then know that I have loved you, and I will make peace with you. You will be rooted out, and your sons will be rooted out, and there will be no peace for you."

24When Jacob saw that he meant evil against him from his heart and with all his soul, to kill him, and that he had come springing like the wild boar that comes on the spear that pierces and kills it and does not draw back from it,

25then he spoke to his own men and to his servants, to attack him and all his companions.

Notes

  • vv3, 10, 14, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter as far as v5, has v3 too. v20 — the last sentence is obscure in the Asmara printing and in Charles, an if whose sense is not clear. Words in [brackets] are in no Ge'ez text here: in v1 they follow the Latin; in v14 four thousand follows Charles and the sum of v10, four companies of a thousand, where the Asmara printing reads four hundred.

  • vv1–13 Esau's sons — not in Genesis. The Greek tells it in brief: after Isaac died, Esau, incited by his sons… having gathered nations, came against Jacob and his sons for war. v3 "for a little dish of lentils" — Genesis 25:34; Hebrews 12:16–17: that no one be… profane like Esau, who for a single meal sold his birthright. For you know that afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected. v13 "he did not remember the oath" — the oath of 35:24 and 36:7–8.

  • vv17–23 at the tower — the Greek: Jacob, having shut the gates of the fortress, implored Esau to remember their parents' commandments. But since he would not yield, but was insolent and reproachful… vv20–23 the impossible things — Esau's answer turns the prophets' pictures around. Jeremiah 13:23: Can the Cushite change his skin, or the leopard his spots? Isaiah 11:6: The wolf shall live with the lamb; Isaiah 65:25: the lion shall eat straw like the ox. What the prophets promise for the last days, Esau names as the day he will make peace. v23 "the raza" — so the Ge'ez; something white, but what is not known. Charles leaves the word untranslated.

Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin and Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Death of Esau, and the Kings of Edom
chapters.html:
Jubilees 38

1After that Judah spoke to Jacob his father and said to him, "Bend your bow, father, and send your arrow, and shoot the adversary and kill the enemy, and may you have the strength; for we will not kill your brother, for he is close to you and like you, and to us he is owed honor."

2Then Jacob bent his bow and sent an arrow and struck Esau his brother [in his right breast] and killed him.

3Again he sent an arrow and struck Adoran the Aramean in the left breast, and drove him back and killed him.

4Then the sons of Jacob went out, they and their servants, dividing themselves on the four sides of the tower.

5Judah went out in front, and Naphtali and Gad with him, and fifty servants with him, on the south side of the tower, and they killed all they found before them, and not one of them escaped.

6Levi and Dan and Asher went out on the east side of the tower, and fifty with them, and they killed the fighting men of Moab and of Ammon.

7Reuben and Issachar and Zebulun went out on the north side of the tower, and fifty with them, and they killed the fighting men of the Philistines.

8Simeon and Benjamin and Hanoch, Reuben's son, went out on the west side of the tower, and fifty with them, and they killed of Edom and of the Horites four hundred men, strong warriors; and six hundred fled, and the four sons of Esau fled with them, and left the body of their father cast out on the hill that is in Aduram.

9The sons of Jacob pursued them as far as Mount Seir; and Jacob buried Esau his brother on the hill that is in Aduram, and returned to his house.

10The sons of Jacob pressed hard on the sons of Esau on Mount Seir and bowed their necks, so that they became servants of the sons of Jacob.

11They sent to their father, to ask whether they should make peace with them or kill them.

12Jacob sent word to his sons to make peace, and they made peace with them, and put the yoke of servitude on them, so that they paid tribute to Jacob and to all his sons.

13They went on paying tribute to Jacob until the day Jacob went down into Egypt.

14The sons of Edom have not got free of the yoke of servitude that the twelve sons of Jacob laid on them, to this day.

15These are the kings who reigned in Edom before a king reigned over the sons of Israel, to this day, in the land of Edom.

16Bela son of Beor reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.

17Bela died, and Jobab son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his place.

18Jobab died, and Husham of the mountain of Teman reigned in his place.

19Husham died, and Hadad son of Bedad, who struck Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place, and the name of his city was Avith.

20Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.

21Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth-on-the-River reigned in his place.

22Shaul died, and Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.

23Baal-hanan son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his place, and his wife's name was Mehetabel daughter of Matred daughter of Me-zahab.

24These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom.

Notes

  • vv8, 9 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v1 to v16, has them too. Without the end of v9 the EOTC never says that Jacob buried his brother. Words in [brackets] (v2) are in no Ge'ez text here; they follow the Latin.

  • vv1–3 the death of Esau — not in Genesis, which has Esau alive and at peace with Jacob at their father's burial (Genesis 35:29) and says nothing of his death. Here Jacob shoots him only when Judah presses him; the Greek: Jacob, being pressed by Judah… bent his bow, and striking Esau upon his right breast, he brought him down. So the word of Isaac's last charge comes true: everyone who seeks evil for his brother will fall into his hand (36:9).

  • vv4–9 the battle — the sons of Jacob go out by threes on the four sides of the tower, as the tribes will later camp by threes on the four sides of the tabernacle (Numbers 2). v8 "Hanoch, Reuben's son" — Genesis 46:9: The sons of Reuben: Hanoch and Pallu and Hezron and Carmi. The EOTC writes ʾEnok.

  • vv10–14 Edom under the yoke — Isaac's words over Jacob, Be lord over your brothers (26:24), and over Esau, you will serve your brother (26:34). Kings tells when the yoke broke: In his days Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah, and they made a king over themselves (2 Kings 8:20).

  • vv15–24 the kings of Edom — Genesis 36:31–39, with the names as in this project's Genesis. The EOTC's forms differ: Balāq for Bela, Danābā for Dinhabah, ʾAsām for Husham, ʾAdāt son of Bārd for Hadad son of Bedad, Salomān for Samlah, ʾAdāt again for Hadar, and Mayṭabit daughter of Maṭrit for Mehetabel daughter of Matred. Jubilees leaves out Hadar's city, Pau.
