chapters.title: Joseph in Potiphar's House and in Prison
chapters.html:
Jubilees 39

1Jacob lived in the land where his father had lived as a guest, the land of Canaan.

2These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph was seventeen years old when they took him down into the land of Egypt, after his brothers sold him, and Potiphar, a eunuch of Pharaoh, the chief of the cooks, bought him.

3He set Joseph over all his house; and the blessing of the Lord came on the Egyptian's house because of Joseph, and the Lord prospered him in all that he did.

4The Egyptian left everything in Joseph's charge, for he saw that the Lord was with him, and the Lord prospered all that he did.

5Joseph was beautiful to look at, and very lovely to look at; and his master's wife lifted her eyes and saw Joseph, and she loved him and begged him to lie with her.

6He did not give up his soul, and he remembered the Lord and the words that Jacob his father used to read from the words of Abraham: that no man should commit fornication with a woman who has a husband; that for him the judgment of death has been ordained in heaven before God Most High, and the sin will be written against him in the eternal books, always, before the Lord.

7Joseph remembered this word and would not lie with her.

8She begged him for one year and a second, and he refused to listen.

9She embraced him and held him fast in the house, to force him to lie with her; and she shut the door of her house and held him openly; but he escaped from her hands, and left his garment in her hands, and broke the door, and fled outside from her presence.

10The woman saw that he would not lie with her, and she slandered him before his master, saying, "Your Hebrew servant, whom you love, wanted to force me, to lie with me; and it came to pass, when I lifted up my voice, that he fled and left his garment in my hands when I held him, and he broke through the door."

11The Egyptian saw Joseph's garment and the broken door, and heard the words of his wife, and put Joseph into the prison, into the place where the king's prisoners were kept.

12He was there in the prison; and the Lord gave him favor in the sight of the chief of the prison guards, and mercy before him, because he saw that the Lord was with him, and that all Joseph did, the Lord prospered.

13He left everything in his charge, and the chief of the prison guards knew nothing of what was with him, for Joseph did everything and the Lord completed it; and he stayed there two years.

14In those days Pharaoh king of Egypt was angry with his two eunuchs, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker, and put them in custody in the house of the chief of the cooks, in the prison where Joseph was held.

15The chief of the prison guards appointed Joseph to serve them, and he served before them.

16They both dreamed a dream, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker, and they told it to Joseph.

17As he interpreted to them, so it happened to them: Pharaoh restored the chief cupbearer to his office, and hanged the chief baker, just as Joseph had told them.

18The chief cupbearer forgot Joseph in the prison, though he had told him what would happen to him, and did not remember to tell Pharaoh what Joseph had told him, for he forgot.

Notes

  • vv2, 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 17 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v9 on, has most of vv9–17 too. Without the end of v5 the EOTC never says who wanted Joseph, and without the end of v6 it never says what he remembered.

  • vv1–13 Joseph and Potiphar's wife — Genesis 39, retold in brief: He left all he had in Joseph's hand… Joseph was beautiful of form and beautiful of appearance (39:6). v2 "seventeen years old" — as Genesis 37:2, Joseph, a son of seventeen years; by this book's own dates (34:10) he was fifteen. v6 "the words that Jacob his father used to read from the words of Abraham" — in Genesis Joseph refuses because he will not wrong his master or sin against God (39:9); in Jubilees he remembers the law against adultery, handed down in writing from Abraham, with its penalty written in heaven. v8 "one year and a second" — so the Ge'ez; Charles has a year.

  • vv12–13 the prison — Genesis 39:21–23: The LORD was with Joseph… The keeper of the round house did not look at anything in his hand, because the LORD was with him. "two years" — Jubilees counts two years in prison before the dreams; Genesis 41:1 counts two full years after them.

  • vv14–18 the dreams — Genesis 40, in four verses. v18 — Genesis 40:23: The chief of the cupbearers did not remember Joseph, and he forgot him.

chapters.title: Joseph Made Ruler over Egypt
chapters.html:
Jubilees 40

1In those days Pharaoh dreamed two dreams in one night, about the famine that was to come on all the land; and he woke from his sleep and called all the interpreters of dreams who were in Egypt, and the magicians, and told them his two dreams, and they could not understand them.

2Then the chief cupbearer remembered Joseph and spoke of him to the king; and they brought him out of the prison, and he told his two dreams before him.

3He said before Pharaoh that his two dreams were one: "Seven years of abundance will come throughout all the land of Egypt, and after them seven years of famine, such as has not been throughout all the land.

4Now let Pharaoh appoint overseers in all the land of Egypt, and let them store up food in every city in the days of the years of plenty, and there will be food for the seven years of famine, and the land will not perish before the famine, for it will be very severe."

5The Lord gave Joseph favor and mercy in Pharaoh's eyes, and Pharaoh said to his servants, "We will not find a man as wise and understanding as this man, for the spirit of the Lord is with him."

6He appointed him second in all his kingdom, and gave him authority over all Egypt, and had him ride in Pharaoh's second chariot.

7He clothed him in garments of fine linen, and put a gold chain on his neck; and they proclaimed before him, "Elel and Habirel," and he put a ring on his hand, and set him over all his house, and made him great, and said, "Only in my throne will I be greater than you."

8Joseph ruled over all the land of Egypt, and all Pharaoh's princes and all his servants and all who did the king's work loved him, because he walked in truth, and there was no pride or arrogance in him; and he had no respect of persons and did not accept gifts, but he judged all the people of the land in uprightness.

9The land of Egypt was at peace before Pharaoh because of Joseph, for the Lord was with him, and gave him favor and mercy for all his kindred before all who knew him and who heard news of him; and Pharaoh's kingdom was upright, and there was no Satan and no evil one.

10The king called Joseph's name Zaphenath-paneah, and gave Joseph as a wife the daughter of Potiphar, the daughter of the priest of On, the chief of the cooks.

11On the day Joseph stood before Pharaoh he was thirty years old, when he stood before Pharaoh.

12In that year Isaac died. And it came to pass, as Joseph had said in the interpretation of his two dreams, as he had told him, that there were seven years of plenty over all the land of Egypt, and the land bore abundantly, one measure yielding eighteen hundred measures.

13Joseph gathered food in every city, until it was full of grain, until they could not count it or measure it for its abundance.

Notes

  • vv3, 7, 8, 10 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter as far as v8, has vv3–8 too. Joseph's words begin at the end of v3 and go on in v4, which is in the EOTC.

  • vv1–13 Joseph before Pharaoh — Genesis 41, retold in brief. v5 "for the spirit of the Lord is with him" — Genesis 41:38: Shall we find one like this, a man in whom is the spirit of God? vv6–7 — Genesis 41:42–43: Pharaoh took off his signet ring… and clothed him in garments of fine linen, and put the gold collar on his neck. He had him ride in the second chariot… and they called out before him, "Abrek!" "Elel and Habirel" — the Latin's form of the cry; Charles's text has El El wa Abirer. "Only in my throne will I be greater than you" — Genesis 41:40. v8 "he had no respect of persons and did not accept gifts" — the marks of a just judge, not in Genesis.

  • v9 "there was no Satan and no evil one" — the words used of the last days in 23:29, here of Egypt under Joseph.

  • v10 "Zaphenath-paneah" — Genesis 41:45; the EOTC writes Sefānṭifānəs. "the daughter of Potiphar, the daughter of the priest of On" — Genesis 41:45 has Asenath daughter of Poti-phera, priest of On; Charles's text makes Joseph's father-in-law the same man as his master Potiphar. Charles writes Heliopolis, the Greek name for On.

  • v11 "thirty years old" — Genesis 41:46. v12 "In that year Isaac died" — by this book's dates Isaac died in 2162 (36:1, 18) and Joseph was born in 2134 (28:24), which makes him twenty-eight, not thirty. The text is left as it stands. "one measure yielding eighteen hundred measures" — Genesis 41:47 has the land produced by handfuls. v13 — Genesis 41:49: until he stopped counting, for there was no number.

chapters.title: Judah and Tamar
chapters.html:
Jubilees 41

1In the forty-fifth jubilee, in the second week, in the second year, Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn from the daughters of Aram, and her name was Tamar.

2He hated her and did not lie with her, because his mother was of the daughters of Canaan, and he wanted to take a wife from his mother's kin; but Judah his father would not let him.

3This Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil, and the Lord put him to death.

4Judah said to Onan his brother, "Go in to your brother's wife and do the brother's duty by her, and raise up seed for your brother."

5Onan knew that the seed would not be his, but his brother's only; and he went into the house of his brother's wife and spilled the seed on the ground, and he was evil in the eyes of the Lord, and He put him to death.

6Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, "Stay in your father's house as a widow until Shelah my son grows up, and I will give you to him as a wife."

7He grew up, but Bedsuel, Judah's wife, did not let Shelah her son marry; and Bedsuel, Judah's wife, died in the fifth year of this week.

8In its sixth year Judah went up to shear his sheep at Timnah; and it was told to Tamar, "Your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep."

9She put off her widow's garments and put on a veil and adorned herself, and sat at the gate by the road to Timnah.

10As Judah was going, he found her and took her for a prostitute, and said to her, "Let me come in to you." She said to him, "Come in," and he went in.

11She said to him, "Give me my hire." He said to her, "I have nothing in my hand but the ring on my finger, and my cord, and my staff that is in my hand."

12She said to him, "Give them to me until you send me my hire." Judah said, "I will send you a young goat." He gave them to her, and was with her, and she conceived by him.

13Judah went to his sheep, and she went to her father's house.

14Judah sent a kid by the hand of his shepherd, the Adullamite, and he did not find her; and he asked the people of the place, saying, "Where is the prostitute who was here?" They said to him, "There is no prostitute here, and we have no prostitute among us."

15He returned and told him that he had not found her, and said to him, "I asked the people of the place too, and they said to me, 'There is no prostitute here.'" He said, "Get up, let us go, so that we do not become a laughingstock."

16When three months had passed, it became known that she was with child; and they told Judah, saying, "Tamar your daughter-in-law is with child by prostitution."

17Judah went to her father's house and said to her father and her brothers, "Bring her out and let them burn her, for she has done an unclean thing in Israel."

18And it came to pass, when they brought her out to burn her, that she sent to her father-in-law the ring and the cord and the staff, and said, "Recognize whose these are, for by him I am with child."

19Judah recognized them and said, "Tamar is more righteous than I," and they did not burn her after all.

20For this reason she was not given to Shelah, and he did not come near her again.

21After that she bore two sons, Perez and Zerah, in the seventh year of this second week.

22Then the seven years of plenty that Joseph had told Pharaoh of were completed.

23Judah knew that the deed he had done was evil, for he had lain with his daughter-in-law, and it was hateful in his eyes; and he knew that he had sinned and gone astray, for he had uncovered his son's skirt; and he began to lament and to plead before the Lord for his transgression.

24We told him in a dream that it was forgiven him, because he pleaded earnestly and lamented, and did not do it again.

25He had forgiveness, because he turned from his sin and from his ignorance, for the transgression before our God was great; and everyone who does so, everyone who lies with his mother-in-law, let them burn him with fire, that he may burn in it, for there is uncleanness and defilement on them; with fire let them burn them.

26You too, command the sons of Israel, and let there be no uncleanness among them; for everyone who lies with his daughter-in-law or with his mother-in-law has done an unclean thing. With fire let them burn the man who has lain with her, and the woman too, and He will turn away wrath and punishment from Israel.

27To Judah we said that his two sons had not lain with her; and for this reason his seed was established for a second generation.

28For in the singleness of his eye he had gone and sought judgment; for according to the judgment of Abraham, which he had commanded his sons, Judah wanted to burn her with fire.

Notes

  • vv5, 7, 8, 12, 15, 16, 25, 27 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v6 to v18, has most of vv7–16 too. Without the end of v12 the EOTC never says that Tamar conceived by Judah. v15 — in the Latin Judah says Let her keep them; in the Asmara printing he says Get up, let us go.

  • vv1–21 Judah and Tamar — Genesis 38, retold in order, in this project's wording where the Ge'ez allows. v1 "from the daughters of Aram" — Genesis 38:6 does not say where Tamar came from; Jubilees makes her an Aramean, of Abraham's kin, and not a Canaanite. v2 Er's hatred — Genesis 38:7 says only that Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of the LORD; Jubilees gives the reason: he wanted a Canaanite wife like his mother. v7 "Bedsuel" — so the EOTC here; the Latin has Bathshua, and the bracket at 34:20, from Charles, has Betasuel. All are bat-Shua, "daughter of Shua" (Genesis 38:2). v11 "the ring on my finger" — Genesis 38:18 has Your seal and your cord, and your staff. v19 "Tamar is more righteous than I" — Genesis 38:26: She is more in the right than I, because I did not give her to Shelah my son.

  • v1 and v21 the dates — the second year of the second week of the forty-fifth jubilee is 2165; Perez and Zerah are born in its seventh year, 2170. v22 — the seven years of plenty began in the year of Isaac's death (40:12).

  • vv23–28 Judah's repentance — Jubilees has just said that there is no atonement for such a sin (33:13, of Reuben). The text gives two reasons Judah is forgiven: he turned from his sin and from his ignorance (v25), and his two sons had not lain with Tamar (v27). v26 "with fire let them burn" — Leviticus 20:12 sets death for a man who lies with his daughter-in-law, and 20:14 burning for a man who takes a woman and her mother. v28 "the judgment of Abraham" — Abraham's charge, If any woman or girl among you commits fornication, burn her with fire (20:4).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Famine, and the Brothers in Egypt
chapters.html:
Jubilees 42

1In the first year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee the famine began to come on the land, and the rain refused to be given to the earth, for none at all came down.

2The earth grew barren; but in the land of Egypt there was bread, for Joseph had gathered the grain of the land in the seven years of abundance and was keeping it.

3The Egyptians came to Joseph, for him to give them food, and he opened the storehouses where the grain of the first year was, and sold it to the peoples of the land for gold.

4[The famine grew very severe in the land of Canaan.] Jacob heard that there was food in Egypt, and he sent his ten sons to get food for him in Egypt; but Benjamin he did not send; and they arrived with those who were going there.

5Joseph recognized them, but they did not recognize him; and he spoke with them and questioned them, and said to them, "Are you not spies, who have come to search out the tracks of the land?" Then he shut them up.

6After that he let them go, and kept back Simeon alone, and sent away his nine brothers.

7He filled their sacks with grain, and put their gold back in their sacks, and they did not know.

8He commanded them to bring their younger brother, for they had told him that their father was alive, and their younger brother.

9They went up from the land of Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, and told their father all that had happened to them, and how the lord of the land had spoken harshly with them and had seized Simeon until they should bring Benjamin.

10Jacob said, "You have bereaved me! Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and Benjamin you would take from me. On me your evil has come."

11He said, "My son will not go with you, in case he falls sick; for their mother bore these two, and one has perished; and if you take this one, and some sickness befalls him on the way, you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol."

12For he saw that all their gold had come back, each in his sack, and for this reason he was afraid to send him.

13The famine grew and became severe in the land of Canaan, and in all the land except the land of Egypt; for many of the sons of the Egyptians had stored up their seed ever since they saw Joseph gathering grain and laying it up in storehouses, so that it might be kept for the years of famine.

14The people of Egypt fed on it in the first year of the famine.

15When Israel saw that the famine was very severe in the land, and there was no deliverance, he said to his sons, "Go back, and get food for us, so that we do not die."

16They said, "We will not go. Unless our youngest brother comes with us, we will not go."

17Israel saw that if he did not send him with them, they would all perish before the famine.

18Reuben said, "Give him into my hand, and if I do not bring him back to you, kill my two sons for his life."

19[He said to him, "He will not go with you."] Judah came near and said, "Send him with us, and if I do not bring him back to you, let me bear the guilt before you all the days of my life."

20He sent him with them in the second year of this week, on the new moon of the month, and they came to the land of Egypt with all who were going, with gifts in their hands: stacte and almonds and terebinth nuts and honeycombs.

21They came and stood before Joseph, and he saw Benjamin his brother and recognized him, and said to them, "Is this your youngest brother?" They said to him, "It is he." He said, "The Lord be gracious to you, my son."

22He sent him into his house, and brought Simeon out to them; and he made a feast for them, and they presented to him the gift they had brought in their hands.

23They ate before him, and he gave them all a portion, and Benjamin's portion was seven times larger than the portion of any of them.

24They ate and drank, and rose and stayed with their donkeys.

25Joseph thought of a plan by which he might know their thoughts, whether there were thoughts of peace among them; and he said to the steward who was over his house, "Fill all their sacks with food, and put their money back in their vessels; and my cup, the silver cup that I drink from, put it in the sack of the youngest, and send them away."

Notes

  • vv2, 4, 5, 11, 13, 21, 22, 25 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v2 to v14, has most of vv2–13 too.   • vv15–25 the second journey — Genesis 43–44. v18 Reuben's offer — Genesis 42:37. v19 Judah's pledge — Genesis 43:9: I myself will stand as the pledge for him… If I do not bring him to you and set him before you, then I will have sinned against you all my days. v20 the date and the gifts — the second year of this week is 2172. speech.text: Jubilees 42
In the first year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee the famine began to come on the land, and the rain refused to be given to the earth, for none at all came down.
The earth grew barren; but in the land of Egypt there was bread, for Joseph had gathered the grain of the land in the seven years of abundance and was keeping it.
The Egyptians came to Joseph, for him to give them food, and he opened the storehouses where the grain of the first year was, and sold it to the peoples of the land for gold.

[The famine grew very severe in the land of Canaan.] Jacob heard that there was food in Egypt, and he sent his ten sons to get food for him in Egypt; but Benjamin he did not send; and they arrived with those who were going there.

Joseph recognized them, but they did not recognize him; and he spoke with them and questioned them, and said to them, "Are you not spies, who have come to search out the tracks of the land?" Then he shut them up.
After that he let them go, and kept back Simeon alone, and sent away his nine brothers.
He filled their sacks with grain, and put their gold back in their sacks, and they did not know.
He commanded them to bring their younger brother, for they had told him that their father was alive, and their younger brother.

They went up from the land of Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, and told their father all that had happened to them, and how the lord of the land had spoken harshly with them and had seized Simeon until they should bring Benjamin.
Jacob said, "You have bereaved me! Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and Benjamin you would take from me. On me your evil has come."

He said, "My son will not go with you, in case he falls sick; for their mother bore these two, and one has perished; and if you take this one, and some sickness befalls him on the way, you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol."
For he saw that all their gold had come back, each in his sack, and for this reason he was afraid to send him.

The famine grew and became severe in the land of Canaan, and in all the land except the land of Egypt; for many of the sons of the Egyptians had stored up their seed ever since they saw Joseph gathering grain and laying it up in storehouses, so that it might be kept for the years of famine.
The people of Egypt fed on it in the first year of the famine.
When Israel saw that the famine was very severe in the land, and there was no deliverance, he said to his sons, "Go back, and get food for us, so that we do not die."
They said, "We will not go. Unless our youngest brother comes with us, we will not go."
Israel saw that if he did not send him with them, they would all perish before the famine.
Reuben said, "Give him into my hand, and if I do not bring him back to you, kill my two sons for his life."
[He said to him, "He will not go with you."] Judah came near and said, "Send him with us, and if I do not bring him back to you, let me bear the guilt before you all the days of my life."

He sent him with them in the second year of this week, on the new moon of the month, and they came to the land of Egypt with all who were going, with gifts in their hands: stacte and almonds and terebinth nuts and honeycombs.

They came and stood before Joseph, and he saw Benjamin his brother and recognized him, and said to them, "Is this your youngest brother?" They said to him, "It is he." He said, "The Lord be gracious to you, my son."
He sent him into his house, and brought Simeon out to them; and he made a feast for them, and they presented to him the gift they had brought in their hands.
They ate before him, and he gave them all a portion, and Benjamin's portion was seven times larger than the portion of any of them.
They ate and drank, and rose and stayed with their donkeys.

Joseph thought of a plan by which he might know their thoughts, whether there were thoughts of peace among them; and he said to the steward who was over his house, "Fill all their sacks with food, and put their money back in their vessels; and my cup, the silver cup that I drink from, put it in the sack of the youngest, and send them away."

chapters.title: The Silver Cup, and Joseph Makes Himself Known
chapters.html:
Jubilees 43

1He did as Joseph had told him, and filled all their sacks with food for them, and put their money in their sacks, and put the cup in Benjamin's sack.

2Early in the morning they went; and it came to pass, when they had gone out from there, that Joseph said to the man of his house, "Pursue them, run, and contend with them, saying, 'You have repaid me evil for good; you have stolen from me the silver cup from which my lord drinks.' Bring back to me their youngest brother, and bring him quickly, before I go out to my judgment seat."

3He ran after them and spoke to them according to these words.

4They said to him, "Far be it from your servants to do this thing, and to steal any vessel from the house of your lord; and the money too, which we found in our sacks the first time, we your servants brought back from the land of Canaan.

5How then would we steal any vessel? Here we are with our sacks; search, and wherever you find the cup, in the sack of any man among us, let him be put to death, and we and our donkeys will serve your lord."

6He said to them, "Not so. The man with whom I find it, him alone I will take as a servant, and you will go back to your house in peace."

7As he was searching in their vessels, beginning with the eldest and ending with the youngest, it was found in Benjamin's sack.

8They tore their garments, and loaded their donkeys, and went back to the city, and came to Joseph's house, and they all bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.

9Joseph said to them, "You have done evil." They said, "What shall we say, and how shall we defend ourselves? Our lord has found out the guilt of his servants. Here we are, the servants of our lord, and our donkeys too."

10Joseph said to them, "I fear the Lord. As for you, go to your homes, and let your brother be a servant, for you have done evil. Do you not know that a man delights in his cup, as I do in this cup? Yet you have stolen it from me."

11Judah said, "Let your servant, my lord, speak a word in my lord's ear: two brothers did your servant's mother bear to our father; one went away and was lost and has not been found, and he alone is left of his mother, and your servant our father loves him, and his life is bound up with the life of this boy.

12It will come to pass, when we go to your servant our father and the boy is not with us, that he will die, and we will bring our father down with sorrow to death.

13Rather, let me, your servant, stay instead of the boy as a servant to my lord, and let the boy go with his brothers; for I became his pledge at the hand of your servant our father, and if I do not bring him back, your servant will bear the guilt before our father forever."

14Joseph saw that the hearts of all of them were one, each with the other, for good; and he could not hold himself in, and he told them that he was Joseph.

15He spoke with them in the Hebrew tongue, and fell on their necks and wept; but they did not know him, and they too began to weep.

16He said to them, "Do not weep over me. Hurry and bring my father to me, so that I may see him before I die, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see it too.

17For this is the second year of the famine, and there are still five years, with no harvest, and no fruit of trees, and no plowing.

18Come down quickly, you and your households, so that you do not perish in the famine; and do not be troubled about your possessions, for the Lord sent me ahead of you to set things in order, so that many people may live.

19Tell my father that I am still alive; and you see that the Lord has made me as a father to Pharaoh, and to rule in his house and over all the land of Egypt.

20Tell my father of all my honor, and all the wealth and honor the Lord has given me."

21By the word of Pharaoh's mouth he gave them chariots and provisions for the way, and he gave them all garments of many colors, and silver.

22To their father he sent garments and silver, and ten donkeys carrying grain, and he sent them away.

23They went up and told their father that Joseph was alive, and was measuring out grain to all the nations of the earth, and that he was ruler over all the land of Egypt.

24Their father did not believe it, for he was stunned in his mind; but when he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, his spirit was renewed and revived, and he said, "It is a great thing for me that Joseph is alive; I will go down and see him before I die."

Notes

  • vv3, 4, 5, 11, 13, 15, 23, 24 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). Without the ends of vv23–24 the EOTC never says what the brothers told their father, or that he went.

  • vv1–13 the silver cup — Genesis 44. v10 "a man delights in his cup" — in Genesis the cup is the one Joseph reads the omens with (44:5), and he asks, Did you not know that a man like me certainly divines? (44:15). Jubilees leaves out the divining. v11 "his life is bound up with the life of this boy" — Genesis 44:30. v13 — Genesis 44:33: let your servant stay instead of the boy as a slave to my lord, and let the boy go up with his brothers.

  • vv14–20 Joseph makes himself known — Genesis 45:1–13. v14 "the hearts of all of them were one… for good" — the test Joseph set in 42:25, whether there were thoughts of peace among them, is passed. v15 "in the Hebrew tongue" — the language restored to Abraham (12:25–26). v17 — Genesis 45:6: For these two years the famine has been within the land, and there are five more years in which there is no plowing and no harvest. By this book's dates the famine began in 2171 (42:1), and this is 2172 (42:20). v18 "so that many people may live" — Genesis 45:5, 7: it was to preserve life that God sent me ahead of you. v19 "a father to Pharaoh" — Genesis 45:8.

  • vv21–24 the wagons — Genesis 45:21–28: His heart went numb, for he did not believe them… he saw the wagons Joseph had sent to carry him. The spirit of Jacob their father revived. Israel said, "Enough. Joseph my son is still alive. Let me go and see him before I die."

chapters.title: Jacob Goes Down to Egypt, and the Seventy Souls
chapters.html:
Jubilees 44

1Israel set out from Harran, from his house, on the new moon of the third month, and went by the way of the Well of the Oath, and offered a sacrifice to the God of his father Isaac on the seventh of this month.

2Jacob remembered the dream he had seen at Bethel, and was afraid to go down into Egypt.

3He was thinking of sending to Joseph to come to him, so that he himself would not go down; and he stayed there seven days, in case he might see a vision about whether he should stay or go down.

4He kept the festival of the harvest, the first fruits of wheat, with old wheat, for in all the land of Canaan there was not a handful of seed in the land; for the famine was on all the beasts and the cattle and the birds, and on men too.

5On the sixteenth the Lord appeared to him and said to him, "Jacob, Jacob"; and he said, "Here I am." He said to him, "I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and Isaac. Do not be afraid to go down into Egypt, for I will make you a great nation there.

6I will go down with you, and I will bring you up, and in this land you will be buried, and Joseph will put his hand on your eyes. Do not be afraid; go down into Egypt."

7His sons and his sons' sons rose, and set their father and their goods on wagons.

8Israel set out from the Well of the Oath on the sixteenth day of this third month, and went to the land of Egypt.

9Israel sent Judah his son ahead of him to Joseph, to look over the land of Goshen; for Joseph had told his brothers to come and live there, so that they would be near him.

10It was the best in the land of Egypt, and near to him, for all of them and for the cattle too.

11These are the names of the sons of Jacob who went into Egypt with Jacob their father.

12Reuben, Israel's firstborn; and these are the names of his sons: Hanoch and Pallu and Hezron and Carmi — five.

13Simeon and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Jemuel and Jamin and Ohad and Jachin and Zohar, and Shaul the son of Finisawet — seven.

14Levi and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Gershon and Kohath and Merari — four.

15Judah and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Shelah and Perez and Zerah — four.

16Issachar and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Tola and Puvah and Jashub and Shimron — five.

17Zebulun and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Sered and Elon and Jahleel — four.

18These are the sons of Jacob and their sons, whom Leah bore to Jacob in Mesopotamia, six, and their one sister Dinah; and all the souls of the sons of Leah and their sons who went with Jacob their father into Egypt were twenty-nine, and with Jacob their father, thirty.

19The sons of Zilpah, the maid of Leah, Jacob's wife, whom she bore to Jacob: Gad and Asher.

20These are the names of their sons who went with him into Egypt. The sons of Gad: Ziphion and Haggi and Shuni and Ezbon and Eri and Areli and Arodi — eight.

21The sons of Asher: Imnah and Ishvah and Ishvi and Beriah, and Serah their one sister — five.

22All the souls were fourteen, and all of Leah's were forty-four.

23The sons of Rachel, Jacob's wife: Joseph and Benjamin.

24There were born to Joseph in Egypt, before his father came into Egypt, whom Asenath daughter of Poti-phera, priest of On, bore to him: Manasseh and Ephraim.

25The sons of Benjamin: Bela and Becher and Ashbel, Gera and Naaman, Ehi and Rosh, Muppim and Huppim and Ard — eleven.

26All the souls of Rachel were fourteen.

27The sons of Bilhah, the maid of Rachel, Jacob's wife, whom she bore to Jacob: Dan and Naphtali.

28These are the names of their sons who went with them into Egypt. The sons of Dan: Hushim and Samon and Asudi and Iyaka and Salomon — six.

29They died in Egypt in the year they came in, and there was left to Dan Hushim alone.

30These are the names of the sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel and Guni and Jezer and Shillem and Ew.

31Ew, who was born after the years of famine, died in Egypt.

32All those of Rachel were twenty-six.

33All the souls of Jacob that went into Egypt were seventy souls. These are his children and his children's children, seventy in all; but five died in Egypt before Joseph, and had no children.

34In the land of Canaan two sons of Judah died, Er and Onan, and they had no children; and the sons of Israel buried those who perished, and they were set among the seventy nations.

Notes

  • vv3, 5, 18, 33 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63). v18 "six" — so the EOTC; the Asmara printing reads seven.

  • v1 "from Harran" — so the EOTC, and Charles has Haran; but Jacob had been living at Hebron, in the tower of Abraham (36:20; 37:14). vv1–8 the dates — Jacob leaves on the new moon of the third month and sacrifices on the seventh; he keeps the festival of first fruits (v4), the Festival of Weeks of the middle of the third month (6:17–21; 15:1); the Lord appears to him on the sixteenth, and he sets out the same day.

  • vv2–6 the vision at the Well of the Oath — Genesis 46:1–4: Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you a great nation there. I Myself will go down with you to Egypt, and I Myself will surely bring you up again. Joseph will set his hand on your eyes. v2 "the dream he had seen at Bethel" — the seven tablets, and the word in Egypt you will die (32:21–23).

  • v9 Judah sent ahead — Genesis 46:28: He sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph, to point the way before him to Goshen.

  • vv11–34 the seventy souls — Genesis 46:8–27, with the names as in this project's Genesis where the Ge'ez has the same person. The Ge'ez differs from Genesis in these places: - v13 "Shaul the son of Finisawet" — Genesis 46:10 has Shaul son of the Canaanite woman; Charles has the Zephathite woman. - v15 — Er and Onan are not counted here but set apart in v34. - v16 "Jashub" — so Numbers 26:24; Genesis 46:13 has Job. - vv20–21 — the EOTC puts Eri and Ishvi in square brackets of its own; they are rendered as plain text. v21 "five" — Charles has six. - v24 — the EOTC writes Heliopolis, the Greek name of On (Genesis 41:45). - v28 "six" — the Ge'ez lists five names under that count. Genesis 46:23 gives Dan one son, Hushim; v29 explains that the others died the year they came in. - v30 "Ew", v31 — a fifth son of Naphtali, not in Genesis 46:24, who died in Egypt. - v33 "seventy souls" — Genesis 46:27: All the souls of the house of Jacob coming to Egypt: seventy. - v34 "set among the seventy nations" — Er and Onan, who died childless in Canaan, are not counted in Israel's seventy; Charles has reckoned among the seventy Gentile nations.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Jacob in Egypt, and His Death
chapters.html:
Jubilees 45

1Israel came into the country of Egypt, into the land of Goshen, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the second year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee.

2Joseph came to meet his father Jacob in the land of Goshen, and he fell on his father's neck and wept.

3Israel said to Joseph, "Now let me die, since I have seen you. Now blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac, who has not withheld His mercy and His grace from His servant Jacob.

4It is great for me that I have seen your face while I am alive; for true indeed is the vision I saw at Bethel. Blessed be the Lord my God forever and ever, and blessed be His name."

5Joseph and his brothers ate bread before their father and drank wine, and Jacob rejoiced with very great joy, because he saw Joseph eating with his brothers and drinking before him; and he blessed the Creator of all things, who had kept him and had kept his twelve sons for him.

6Joseph gave to his father and his brothers, as a gift, the right to live in the land of Goshen and in Rameses and all its region, which he ruled before Pharaoh. Israel and his sons lived in the land of Goshen, the best of the land of Egypt; and Israel was one hundred and thirty years old when he came into Egypt.

7Joseph fed his father and his brothers, and their possessions too, with bread, as much as was enough for them for the seven years of famine.

8The land of Egypt suffered before the famine; and Joseph acquired all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh in return for food, for he bought the people and the cattle and everything for Pharaoh.

9The years of famine were completed; and Joseph gave the people of the land seed and food, so that they might sow the land in the eighth year, for the river had overflowed all the land of Egypt.

10For in the seven years of famine it had not overflowed, and had watered only a few places along the bank of the river; but in the eighth year the Egyptians sowed their land and gathered good fruit that year.

11This was the first year of the fourth week of the forty-fifth jubilee.

12Joseph took from the grain they sowed a fifth for the king, and four parts he left to them for food and for seed; and Joseph made it an ordinance for the land of Egypt to this day.

13Israel lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years; and all the years of his life that he lived were three jubilees, one hundred and forty-seven years; and he died in the forty-fifth jubilee, in the fourth year of the fifth week.

14Israel blessed his sons before he died, and told them all that would happen to them in the land of Egypt; and he made known to them what would come on them in the last days, and blessed them; and to Joseph he gave two portions in the land.

15He slept with his fathers, and was buried in the double cave in the land of Canaan, near Abraham his father, in the grave he had dug for himself in the double cave in the land of Hebron.

16He gave all his books and the books of his fathers to Levi his son, to keep them and to renew them for his sons to this day.

Notes

  • vv5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 13, 14 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v8 on, has vv8–14 too. Without the end of v13 the EOTC never tells Jacob's age or the year of his death. v14 "two portions" — the Latin has blessed twofold.

  • vv1–7 the meeting in Goshen — Genesis 46:29–30: Joseph… went up to meet Israel his father at Goshen… and fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a long while. Israel said to Joseph, "Let me die this time, after seeing your face." v4 "true indeed is the vision I saw at Bethel" — the seven tablets (32:21–26). v6 "Rameses" — Genesis 47:11; "one hundred and thirty years old" — Genesis 47:9.

  • vv8–12 the famine — Genesis 47:13–26: Joseph bought all the ground of Egypt for Pharaoh… Joseph made it a statute to this day over the ground of Egypt — a fifth for Pharaoh (47:20, 26). Jubilees adds that the Nile did not flood in the famine years.

  • The dates — Jacob arrives in the second year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee, 2172 (v1). The famine ends with the first year of the fourth week, 2178 (v11; the Latin has fifth week); seven years from 2171 (42:1). Jacob dies in the fourth year of the fifth week, 2188 (v13). By this book's own dates he was born in 2046 (19:13), which makes him 126 on arrival and 142 at death, where v6 and v13 give 130 and 147, as Genesis 47:9 and 47:28 do. The text is left as it stands.

  • v14 "what would come on them in the last days" — Genesis 49:1: Gather, and I will tell you what will befall you in the end of days. "Joseph he blessed twofold" — Genesis 48:22: I have given you one shoulder above your brothers.

  • v16 "all his books and the books of his fathers to Levi" — the line of written lore that began with Enoch and passed through Noah, Shem and Abraham (10:14; 12:27; 21:10) now goes to the priestly tribe.

speech.text: Jubilees 45
Israel came into the country of Egypt, into the land of Goshen, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the second year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee.
Joseph came to meet his father Jacob in the land of Goshen, and he fell on his father's neck and wept.

Israel said to Joseph, "Now let me die, since I have seen you. Now blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac, who has not withheld His mercy and His grace from His servant Jacob.
It is great for me that I have seen your face while I am alive; for true indeed is the vision I saw at Bethel. Blessed be the Lord my God forever and ever, and blessed be His name."

Joseph and his brothers ate bread before their father and drank wine, and Jacob rejoiced with very great joy, because he saw Joseph eating with his brothers and drinking before him; and he blessed the Creator of all things, who had kept him and had kept his twelve sons for him.

Joseph gave to his father and his brothers, as a gift, the right to live in the land of Goshen and in Rameses and all its region, which he ruled before Pharaoh. Israel and his sons lived in the land of Goshen, the best of the land of Egypt; and Israel was one hundred and thirty years old when he came into Egypt.
Joseph fed his father and his brothers, and their possessions too, with bread, as much as was enough for them for the seven years of famine.
The land of Egypt suffered before the famine; and Joseph acquired all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh in return for food, for he bought the people and the cattle and everything for Pharaoh.
The years of famine were completed; and Joseph gave the people of the land seed and food, so that they might sow the land in the eighth year, for the river had overflowed all the land of Egypt.

For in the seven years of famine it had not overflowed, and had watered only a few places along the bank of the river; but in the eighth year the Egyptians sowed their land and gathered good fruit that year.
This was the first year of the fourth week of the forty-fifth jubilee.

He slept with his fathers, and was buried in the double cave in the land of Canaan, near Abraham his father, in the grave he had dug for himself in the double cave in the land of Hebron.
He gave all his books and the books of his fathers to Levi his son, to keep them and to renew them for his sons to this day.

chapters.title: Joseph's Death, and the Bondage in Egypt
chapters.html:
Jubilees 46

1And it came to pass, after Jacob died, that the sons of Israel multiplied in the land of Egypt and became a great people; and they were all of one heart, so that brother loved brother and each man helped his brother; and they increased and multiplied very greatly, ten weeks of years, all the days of Joseph's life.

2There was no Satan and nothing evil at all, all the days of the life of Joseph that he lived after his father Jacob; for all the Egyptians honored the sons of Israel all the days of Joseph's life.

3Joseph died at one hundred and ten years old: seventeen years he lived in the land of Canaan, and ten years he was a servant, and three years in prison, and eighty years he was under the king, ruling all the land of Egypt.

4He died, and all his brothers, and all that generation.

5Before he died he commanded the sons of Israel to carry his bones with them in the days when they went out of the land of Egypt.

6He made them swear about his bones, for he knew that the Egyptians would not again bring him out and bury him in the land of Canaan; for Makamaron, king of Canaan, while he was living in the land of Assyria, fought in the valley with the king of Egypt and killed him there, and pursued the Egyptians to the gates of Ermon.

7He could not enter, for another, a new king, reigned over Egypt, and he was stronger than he; and he went back to the land of Canaan, and the gates of Egypt were shut, and no one went out and no one came into Egypt.

8Joseph died in the forty-sixth jubilee, in the sixth week, in its second year, and they buried him in the land of Egypt; and all his brothers died after him.

9The king of Egypt went out to fight with the king of Canaan in the forty-seventh jubilee, in the second week, in its second year; and the sons of Israel brought out all the bones of the sons of Jacob except the bones of Joseph, and buried them in the field, in the double cave in the mountain.

10Most of them went back to Egypt, and a few of them stayed on the mountain of Hebron, and Amram your father stayed with them.

11The king of Canaan defeated the king of Egypt, and shut the gates of Egypt.

12He devised an evil plan against the sons of Israel, to afflict them, and he said to the people of Egypt,

13"The people of the sons of Israel have grown and multiplied more than we. Come, let us deal shrewdly with them before they multiply, and afflict them with slavery before war comes on us, and before they too fight against us; otherwise they will join the enemy and go out of our land, for their hearts and their faces are toward the land of Canaan."

14He set taskmasters over them, to afflict them with slavery; and they commanded them, and they built fortified cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Rameses, and they built every wall and every rampart that had fallen in the cities of Egypt.

15They made them serve with oppression, and the more they did evil to them, the more they multiplied and the more they increased.

16The people of Egypt held the sons of Israel to be unclean.

Notes

  • vv1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 14 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter in part, has v14 too. Without the end of v6 the EOTC never says who could not enter Egypt in v7: it is Makamaron, king of Canaan.

  • vv1–2 "no Satan and nothing evil" — as in Egypt under Joseph (40:9), and as in the last days (23:29).

  • v3 Joseph's years — seventeen… ten… three… eighty, 110 in all, as Genesis 50:26: Joseph died, a son of a hundred and ten years. The Greek has three years as a slave, and three years in the prison.

  • vv5–6 Joseph's bones — Genesis 50:25: God will surely visit you, and you shall carry my bones up from here; Exodus 13:19: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him. Jubilees gives the reason they were not carried up at once: the war with Canaan and the shut gates of Egypt.

  • The dates — Joseph dies in the second year of the sixth week of the forty-sixth jubilee, 45 × 49 + 5 × 7 + 2 = 2242. By this book's date for his birth, 2134 (28:24), he is 108, where v3 has 110. The war of v9 is in the second year of the second week of the forty-seventh jubilee, 2263. The Asmara printing dates Joseph's death to the second year of the third week of the forty-seventh jubilee, 2270, which makes him 136 and puts his death after the war. The text is left as it stands.

  • v9 the bones of Jacob's sons — buried in the double cave at Hebron, except Joseph's, which wait for the exodus.

  • v10 "Amram your father" — the angel is speaking to Moses; Amram is the father of Moses (Exodus 6:20). The EOTC writes ʾAbrām; the second Ge'ez text has the same.

  • vv11–16 the bondage — Exodus 1:8–14: A new king rose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph… Come, let us deal shrewdly with them — otherwise they will multiply, and it will come to pass that if war breaks out they will be added to those who hate us… They built store cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Rameses. But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied. v12 "He devised an evil plan" — the Ge'ez does not name the king; the Latin says it was the king of Canaan. v14 "Pithom and Rameses" — so the Asmara printing, as Exodus 1:11; the Latin adds On. The Greek adds that the Hebrews were worn out digging canals, building embankments against the Nile, and raising pyramids.

chapters.title: The Birth and Youth of Moses
chapters.html:
Jubilees 47

1In the seventh week, in the seventh year, in the forty-seventh jubilee, your father came from the land of Canaan; and you were born in the fourth week, in its sixth year, in the forty-eighth jubilee, which was the time of distress on the sons of Israel.

2Pharaoh king of Egypt gave a command about them, that they should throw their children, every male that was born, into the river.

3They went on throwing them in for seven months, until the day you were born. Your mother hid you for three months, but they informed on her.

4She made you an ark, and smeared it with pitch and asphalt, and set it in the grass by the bank of the river, and put you in it seven days; and your mother would come by night and nurse you, and by day your sister Miriam guarded you from the birds.

5In those days Tharmuth, Pharaoh's daughter, came out to bathe in the river, and she heard your voice as you cried, and told her Hebrew women to bring you, and they brought you to her.

6She took you out of the ark and had compassion on you.

7Your sister said to her, "Shall I go and call you one of the Hebrew women, to nurse and suckle this child for you?" [She said to her, "Go."]

8She went and called your mother, Jochebed, and she gave her wages, and she nursed you.

9After that, when you had grown, they brought you to Pharaoh's house, and you became her son; and Amram your father taught you writing; and when you had completed three weeks, they brought you into the royal court.

10You were in the court three weeks of years, until the time when you went out from the royal court, and saw an Egyptian striking your companion, of the sons of Israel; and you killed him and hid him in the sand.

11On the second day you found two of the sons of Israel fighting, and you said to the one doing wrong, "Why do you strike your brother?"

12He was angry and indignant, and said, "Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Do you want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?" You were afraid, and fled because of this word.

Notes

  • vv3, 4, 10 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter, has them too. Without the end of v10 the EOTC never tells of the Egyptian that Moses killed, though v12 speaks of him. Words in [brackets] (v7) are in no Ge'ez text here; they follow the Latin.

  • v1 the dates — Amram comes from Canaan in the seventh year of the seventh week of the forty-seventh jubilee, 46 × 49 + 6 × 7 + 7 = 2303 (compare 46:10). Moses is born in the sixth year of the fourth week of the forty-eighth jubilee, 47 × 49 + 3 × 7 + 6 = 2330. Three weeks later he enters the royal court (v9), 2351, and three weeks after that he leaves it (v10), 2372, at forty-two; Stephen says Moses was forty years old when he went out to his brothers (Acts 7:23).

  • vv2–8 the ark on the river — Exodus 1:22–2:9: she hid him three months. She could hide him no longer, and she took for him a basket of papyrus and daubed it with tar and with resin… His sister said to Pharaoh's daughter, "Shall I go and call you a nursing woman from the Hebrews?" v3 "seven months" — the Greek has only ten months. v4 — Jubilees adds the seven days in the reeds, the mother nursing by night, and Miriam keeping off the birds by day. v5 "Tharmuth" — Pharaoh's daughter is not named in Exodus; the Latin and Greek have Thermuthis. "her Hebrew women" — so the Ge'ez; Charles has her maidens, and Exodus 2:5 her young women. v8 "Jochebed" — named in Exodus 6:20.

  • v9 "Amram your father taught you writing" — Moses learns to read and write from his own father, not only from the Egyptians. Acts 7:22: Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians.

  • vv10–12 the Egyptian — Exodus 2:11–15: He saw an Egyptian man striking a Hebrew man… and he struck down the Egyptian and hid him in the sand… Who made you a chief and a judge over us? Are you saying you will kill me as you killed the Egyptian?… Moses fled from before Pharaoh.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin and Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Mastema Against Moses, the Plagues, and the Sea
chapters.html:
Jubilees 48

1In the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you went and lived there [in the land of Midian] five weeks and one year; and you returned to Egypt in the second week, in the second year, in the fiftieth jubilee.

2You know what He spoke to you on Mount Sinai, and what the prince Mastema wanted to do with you when you were returning to Egypt, on the way, at the lodging place.

3Did he not seek with all his strength to kill you, and to save the Egyptians from your hand, because he saw that you were sent to do judgment and vengeance on the Egyptians?

4I delivered you from his hand; and you performed the signs and wonders that you were sent to perform in Egypt, against Pharaoh, and against all his house, and against all his people.

5The Lord did great vengeance on them for Israel's sake, and struck them and killed them with blood and with frogs, with gnats and with dog-flies, and with evil sores breaking out in blisters; and their cattle with death; and with hailstones; with the hail He destroyed everything that grew for them, and the locust devoured what the hail had left; and with darkness; and with the death of their firstborn, of men and of animals; and on all the gods of the Egyptians the Lord took vengeance.

6Everything was sent through your hand, that you might declare it before it was done; and you spoke with the king of Egypt before all his servants and before his people.

7Everything happened by your word: ten great and terrible judgments came on the land of Egypt, so that you might take vengeance on it for Israel.

8The Lord did everything for Israel's sake, and according to His covenant which He had ordained with Abraham, that He would take vengeance on them as they had brought them into bondage by force.

9The prince Mastema stood up against you, and wanted to make you fall into Pharaoh's hands; and he helped the Egyptian sorcerers, and they stood up and worked before you.

10The evils we let them do; but the healings we did not allow to be done by their hands.

11The Lord struck them with evil sores, and they could not stand, for we destroyed them, so that they could not do a single sign.

12Through all the signs and wonders the prince Mastema was not put to shame, until he gathered strength and cried to the Egyptians to pursue you with all the power of the Egyptians, with their chariots and their horses, and with all the multitude of the peoples of Egypt.

13I stood between you and the Egyptians, between the Egyptians and Israel, and we delivered Israel from his hand and from the hand of the people; and the Lord brought them through the middle of the sea as if it were dry land.

14All the people he had brought out to pursue Israel, the Lord our God threw into the middle of the sea, into the depths of the abyss, beneath the sons of Israel. As the people of Egypt had thrown their children into the river, He took vengeance on a million of them; and a thousand strong and energetic men were destroyed for one nursing child of the children of your people whom they had thrown into the river.

15On the fourteenth day, and on the fifteenth, and on the sixteenth, and on the seventeenth, and on the eighteenth, the prince Mastema was bound and shut up behind the sons of Israel, so that he might not accuse them.

16On the nineteenth day we let them loose, that they might help the Egyptians and pursue the sons of Israel.

17He hardened their hearts and made them strong, and they were made strong by the Lord our God, so that He might strike the Egyptians and throw them into the middle of the sea.

18On the fourteenth day we bound him, so that he might not accuse the sons of Israel on the day when they asked the Egyptians for vessels and garments — vessels of silver and vessels of gold and vessels of bronze — to plunder the Egyptians in return for the servitude in which they had forced them to serve.

19We did not bring the sons of Israel out of Egypt empty-handed.

Notes

  • vv4, 5, 8, 13, 14 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter as far as v5, has vv4 and 5 too. Without the end of v5 the EOTC lists only six of the ten plagues. Words in [brackets] (v1) are in no Ge'ez text here; they follow the Latin.

  • v1 the dates — Moses goes to Midian in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee, 48 × 49 + 2 × 7 + 6 = 2372, the year he leaves the court (47:10). He returns in the second year of the second week of the fiftieth jubilee, 49 × 49 + 7 + 2 = 2410, at eighty, as Exodus 7:7 has him. Five weeks and one year is thirty-six years; the dates give thirty-eight; the Asmara printing reads six weeks and one year, forty-three. The text is left as it stands.

  • vv2–4 the lodging place — Exodus 4:24: on the road, at the lodging place, the LORD met him and sought to put him to death. In Jubilees it is Mastema who seeks to kill Moses, and the angel who delivers him.

  • vv5–11 the ten plagues — Exodus 7–12. "on all the gods of the Egyptians" — Exodus 12:12: Against all the gods of Egypt I will carry out judgments. The Greek sets the plagues month by month, from the Nile turned to blood in June to the firstborn in March. v8 — the promise of Genesis 15:14 (14:13–14 in this book). vv9–11 the sorcerers — Exodus 7:11–8:19; 9:11: The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils. v10 "The evils we let them do; but the healings we did not allow" — the Egyptian sorcerers can bring plagues but cannot take them away.

  • vv12–14 the sea — Exodus 14. v13 "I stood between the Egyptians and Israel" — Exodus 14:19–20: The messenger of God who was going before the camp of Israel moved and went behind them… It came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel. v14 "a thousand… for one nursing child" — the Greek has the same: a thousand mighty Egyptian men being drowned for every single Israelite infant.

  • vv15–19 Mastema bound — from the fourteenth of the first month, the day of the Passover, to the eighteenth, Mastema is bound so that he cannot accuse Israel; on the nineteenth he is let loose to drive the Egyptians into the sea. v17 "their hearts" — the EOTC has ʾalbāsihomu, "their garments"; the English follows Charles and the sense. vv18–19 "vessels of silver and vessels of gold" — Exodus 12:35–36; 3:21: when you go, you will not go empty-handed.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin and Greek: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

The evils we let them do; but the healings we did not allow to be done by their hands.
The Lord struck them with evil sores, and they could not stand, for we destroyed them, so that they could not do a single sign.

Through all the signs and wonders the prince Mastema was not put to shame, until he gathered strength and cried to the Egyptians to pursue you with all the power of the Egyptians, with their chariots and their horses, and with all the multitude of the peoples of Egypt.

I stood between you and the Egyptians, between the Egyptians and Israel, and we delivered Israel from his hand and from the hand of the people; and the Lord brought them through the middle of the sea as if it were dry land.

All the people he had brought out to pursue Israel, the Lord our God threw into the middle of the sea, into the depths of the abyss, beneath the sons of Israel. As the people of Egypt had thrown their children into the river, He took vengeance on a million of them; and a thousand strong and energetic men were destroyed for one nursing child of the children of your people whom they had thrown into the river.

On the fourteenth day, and on the fifteenth, and on the sixteenth, and on the seventeenth, and on the eighteenth, the prince Mastema was bound and shut up behind the sons of Israel, so that he might not accuse them.
On the nineteenth day we let them loose, that they might help the Egyptians and pursue the sons of Israel.
He hardened their hearts and made them strong, and they were made strong by the Lord our God, so that He might strike the Egyptians and throw them into the middle of the sea.

On the fourteenth day we bound him, so that he might not accuse the sons of Israel on the day when they asked the Egyptians for vessels and garments — vessels of silver and vessels of gold and vessels of bronze — to plunder the Egyptians in return for the servitude in which they had forced them to serve.
We did not bring the sons of Israel out of Egypt empty-handed.

chapters.title: The Law of the Passover
chapters.html:
Jubilees 49

1Remember the commandment that the Lord commanded you about the Passover, that you should keep it in its season, on the fourteenth of the first month, that you should slaughter it before evening, and that they should eat it by night, on the evening of the fifteenth, from the time the sun sets.

2For on this night — the beginning of the festival and the beginning of joy — you were eating the Passover in Egypt, when all the powers of Mastema had been let loose to kill every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh to the firstborn of the captive maid at the mill, and to the cattle.

3This is the sign the Lord gave them: into every house on whose doorway they saw the blood of a year-old lamb, they should not go in to kill, but should pass over, so that all who were in the house might be saved, because the sign of the blood was on its doorway.

4The powers of the Lord did all that the Lord commanded them, and they passed over all the sons of Israel, and the plague did not come on them to destroy any soul from among them, from cattle to man, even to dog.

5The plague in Egypt was very great, and there was no house in Egypt without a dead body in it, and weeping and wailing.

6All Israel was eating the flesh of the Passover and drinking wine, and praising and blessing and giving thanks to the Lord, the God of their fathers, and was ready to go out from under the yoke of Egypt and from the evil bondage.

7You too, remember this day all the days of your life, and keep it from year to year, all the days of your life, once a year, on its day, according to all its law; and do not move it from day to day, or from month to month.

8For it is an eternal ordinance, and engraved on the tablets of heaven concerning the sons of Israel, that they should keep it every year on its day, once a year, through all their generations; and there is no limit of days, for it is ordained forever.

9The man who is clean and does not come to keep it at the time of its day, to bring an acceptable offering before the Lord and to eat and drink before the Lord on the day of its festival — that man who is clean and near at hand shall be cut off, for he did not bring the Lord's offering in its season; that man shall take the sin on himself.

10Let the sons of Israel come and keep the Passover on the day of its season, on the fourteenth of the first month, between the evenings, from the third part of the day to the third part of the night; for two parts of the day are given to the light, and a third to the evening.

11This is what the Lord commanded you, that you should keep it between the evenings.

12It is not to be slaughtered at any time of the light, but only at the time bordering on the evening; and let them eat it in the time of the evening, until the third part of the night; and whatever is left of all its flesh from the third part of the night on, let them burn it with fire.

13They shall not boil it in water, nor eat it raw, but roasted with fire; cooked with fire, with care, the head with its inner parts and with its feet; and no bone of it shall be broken, for among the sons of Israel no bone of it shall be crushed.

14For this reason the Lord commanded the sons of Israel to keep the Passover on the day of its season, and that no bone of it is to be broken, for it is a festival day and a day of commandment; it is not to be passed over from day to day or from month to month, but kept in its season.

15You too, command the sons of Israel to keep the Passover in their days, every year, once a year, on the day of its season; and it will come as a memorial, pleasing before the Lord, and no plague will come on them to kill or to strike in that year, when they have kept the Passover in its season, in everything as it is commanded.

16It will no longer be eaten outside the sanctuary of the Lord, but before the sanctuary of the Lord; and all the people of the congregation of Israel shall keep it in its season.

17Every man who has come on its day shall eat it in the sanctuary of your God, before the Lord, from twenty years old and upward; for so it is written and ordained, that they should eat it in the sanctuary of the Lord.

18When the sons of Israel come into the land they are to possess, into the land of Canaan, and set up the tabernacle of the Lord in the middle of the land, in one of their tribes, until the sanctuary of the Lord is built on the earth, they shall come and keep the Passover in the middle of the tabernacle of the Lord, and slaughter it before the Lord from year to year.

19In the days when the house has been built in the name of the Lord in the land of their inheritance, they will go there and slaughter the Passover in the evening, when the sun is setting, at the third part of the day.

20They will offer its blood on the base of the altar, and set its fat on the fire that is on the altar, and eat its flesh roasted with fire in the court of the house of the sanctuary, in the name of the Lord.

21They may not keep the Passover in their cities, or in any place, except before the tabernacle of the Lord, or else before the house where His name has dwelt; and they shall not go astray from the Lord.

22You too, Moses, command the sons of Israel to keep the ordinance of the Passover as it was commanded to you, and tell them its year, year by year, and its day among the days; and the Festival of Unleavened Bread, that they eat unleavened bread seven days, and keep its festival, and bring its offering day by day during those seven days of joy before the Lord, on the altar of your God.

23For you kept this festival in haste when you went out of Egypt, until you crossed the sea into the wilderness of Shur; for on the shore of the sea you completed it.

Notes

  • vv2, 13, 14, 18 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the Latin, which covers this chapter from v7 on, has vv13–18 too.

  • vv1–6 the first Passover — Exodus 12. v2 "all the powers of Mastema had been let loose" — in Exodus it is the destroyer whom the LORD does not let come into your houses to strike (12:23); Jubilees names the destroying powers as Mastema's, though in v4 they are the powers of the Lord and do only what He commands. "from the firstborn of Pharaoh to the firstborn of the captive" — Exodus 12:29. v4 "even to dog" — Exodus 11:7: against all the sons of Israel not a dog will sharpen its tongue.

  • vv7–15 the law of the day — v9 — Numbers 9:13: the man who is clean and is not on a journey, and fails to keep the Passover — that person shall be cut off from his people… That man shall carry his sin. vv10–12 "between the evenings… from the third part of the day" — Exodus 12:6, between the evenings; Jubilees fixes it as the last third of the daylight. v13 — Exodus 12:8–9: roasted with fire… Do not eat any of it raw, or boiled at all in water, but roasted with fire — its head with its legs and with its inner parts. "no bone of it shall be broken" — Exodus 12:46; John 19:36: these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled: "Not a bone of Him shall be broken."

  • vv16–21 the place — Deuteronomy 16:5–6: You may not sacrifice the Passover in any of your gates… but at the place that the LORD your God chooses to make His name dwell, there you shall sacrifice the Passover, in the evening, as the sun goes down. Jubilees adds the tabernacle, before the temple is built, and the age of twenty.

  • vv22–23 the Festival of Unleavened Bread — seven days, kept first in haste on the way out of Egypt (Exodus 12:11, You shall eat it in haste) and finished on the shore of the sea, on the way into the wilderness of Shur (Exodus 15:22).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. Latin: Online Critical Pseudepigrapha, CC BY 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Jubilee of Jubilees, and the Law of the Sabbath
chapters.html:
Jubilees 50

1After this law I made known to you the days of the Sabbaths in the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai.

2I told you of the Sabbaths of the land on Mount Sinai, and of the jubilee years in the Sabbaths of years; but its year we have not told you, until you enter the land that you are to possess.

3The land too will keep its Sabbaths while they live on it, and they will know the year of jubilee.

4For this reason I have ordained for you the weeks of years and the jubilees: forty-nine jubilees from the days of Adam until this day, and one week and two years; and there are yet forty years to come for learning the commandments of the Lord, until they cross over into the land of Canaan, crossing the Jordan to the west.

5The jubilees will pass by until Israel is cleansed from all the guilt of fornication and uncleanness and defilement and sin and error, and lives in all the land in safety; and there will no longer be any Satan or any evil one, and the land will be clean from that time for all days.

6The commandment of the Sabbaths too I have written for you, and all the judgments of its laws.

7Six days you shall do work, and on the seventh day is the Sabbath of the Lord your God; you shall not do any work on it — you and your sons, and your male servants and your female servants, and all your cattle, and the stranger who is with you.

8The man who does any work on it shall die: every man who profanes that day, who lies with a woman, or who speaks of any work on it — that he will set out on a journey on it — or of any buying or selling; and whoever draws water on it that he had not prepared for himself on the sixth day; and whoever lifts any burden to carry it out of his tent or out of his house shall die.

9You shall not do any work on the Sabbath but what you have prepared for yourselves on the sixth day, to eat and to drink, and to rest and keep Sabbath from all work on that day, and to bless the Lord your God, who has given you a day of festival and a holy day; and a day of the holy kingdom for all Israel is this day among their days, forever.

10For great is the honor the Lord has given Israel: to eat and drink and be satisfied on this festival day, and to rest on it from all the work that belongs to the work of the sons of men, except burning incense and bringing offerings and sacrifices before the Lord, for the days and for the Sabbaths.

11This work alone shall be done on the Sabbath days in the sanctuary of the Lord your God: to atone for Israel with offering continually, day after day, for a memorial acceptable before the Lord, and that He may receive them forever, day after day, as you have been commanded.

12Every man who does work, or goes on a journey, or works a farm, whether in his house or in any place, and whoever lights a fire, or rides on any beast, or travels by ship on the sea, and whoever strikes or kills anything, or slaughters a beast or a bird, or whoever catches an animal or a bird or a fish, or whoever fasts or makes war on the Sabbaths —

13the man who does any of these things on the Sabbath day shall die, so that the sons of Israel keep the Sabbaths according to the commandments of the Sabbaths of the land, as it is written on the tablets that He gave into my hands, that I should write out for you the laws of the seasons, and the seasons according to the division of their days. Here is completed the account of the division of the days.

Notes

  • vv9, 12, 13 — the words the EOTC text as held here lacks are rendered from the Asmara printing of the Ge'ez (1962/63); the EOTC is cut short in these verses.

  • vv1–5 the jubilee of jubilees — v1 "the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai" — Exodus 16:1, where the Sabbath is first given with the manna (Exodus 16:29). v4 the count — forty-nine jubilees and one week and two years from Adam is 49 × 49 + 7 + 2 = 2410, the year Moses returned to Egypt (48:1). Forty years more make 2450, fifty jubilees exactly: Israel enters the land in the jubilee of jubilees, as each Israelite was to return to his holding in the fiftieth year (Leviticus 25:10, You shall make the fiftieth year holy, and proclaim liberty in the land to all who live in it. It shall be a jubilee for you). v5 "no longer any Satan or any evil one" — as in 23:29, 40:9 and 46:2.

  • vv6–13 the Sabbath — Exodus 20:8–11: Six days you shall work and do all your labor, and the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your God. You shall not do any labor — you, or your son, or your daughter, your male slave or your female slave, or your animal, or the guest who is inside your gates. v8 "shall die" — Exodus 31:14–15: Whoever does work on the sabbath day shall surely be put to death. v12 "whoever lights a fire" — Exodus 35:3. "or whoever fasts" — the Sabbath is a festival day, for eating and drinking (v10), not for fasting. vv10–11 the sacrifices — the one work the Sabbath allows is the work of the altar.

  • v13 "Here is completed the account of the division of the days" — the book ends as it began, with its own title (the prologue above 1:1): This is the account of the division of the days.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. Second Ge'ez text: Ran HaCohen, via Beta Masaheft, CC BY-SA 4.0. Asmara printing (1962/63): Ge'ez Frontier Foundation, CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.
